# CLAUDE.md — Briefing for Claude (and other LLM agents)

> Read this file first whenever you join this repo. It tells you what RELAY is, how it's built, what's already working, what's been deliberately chosen, and what to be careful about. Keeping this file accurate is part of your job as a contributor.

---

## TL;DR

**RELAY** is a self-hosted, browser-based voice / video / chat caller wrapped in a phone-app shell. Visitors pick a display name (or sign in), get a persistent 6-digit number, and can dial each other (peer-to-peer WebRTC mesh up to 6 participants), send SMS-style messages with attachments, and manage contacts. Hosted on **AWS** at `https://your-chat.io` (2× EC2 Mumbai + ALB + ElastiCache Redis + S3) via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. Develop on `claude/connected-ready-glsdab`, PR into **`main`**, and every merge auto-deploys; **any `aws-ops.yml` dispatch must use `ref: main`**, because the deploy role's OIDC trust policy is scoped to that ref and a branch dispatch fails with a misleading STS error — see the Deploying section. The former Manus/`.org` deployment was **emptied and retired by the owner on 2026-07-21** — `.io` is the ONLY live deployment; do not target `.org` or the Manus Publish flow.

Stack: **React 19 + Vite + Tailwind 4 + Express 4 + tRPC 11 + Drizzle ORM (MySQL) + Manus OAuth + Server-Sent Events signaling + native WebRTC + MediaPipe Tasks Vision**. Deployed as a single Node.js process on Cloud Run.

So this is a TONE MAP rather than a colour swap, and **`toward` is its load-bearing member**: dark brightens a channel out of black, light must DARKEN it onto the page, or every particle lands within a few percent of the base. **MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER against the transpiled engine rather than reasoned about** — pixels differing from the base by a visible margin: **light 95.8% visible / 63.9% strong / max delta 221**, dark 64.9% / 9.4% / 251, so the light canvas paints MORE strongly than the dark one rather than being a blank page. **THE TONE IS A PROP, NEVER A `useTheme()` READ INSIDE THE CANVAS**, and that is a correctness decision: the login screen and the passcode lock mount this component BEFORE the app shell exists and are dark by design, so a component that decided its own tone would flip two surfaces nobody asked to change, on a release about a third one; pinned by asserting the component never imports `useTheme`. A theme switch REBUILDS rather than hot-swaps, because the composite operation is captured at init and a running loop cannot be re-toned. **AND THE ACCENT NAV HAD TO STOP RIDING THE SAME BOOLEAN** — `accentNav = liveBackground` was justified as "the two can never disagree about which design is live", which held ONLY while the canvas was dark-only: one boolean was answering two questions, and turning the background on in light would have turned the accent nav on over a pale card and silently reinstated the **measured 1.7:1** contrast failure v2.106.2 exists to avoid. **FOUR PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY, and every one had frozen "dark only"** — two required `const liveBackground = theme === "dark"` verbatim (i.e. they FORBADE this feature while saying nothing about the rule they stand for, which is that the shell's own fill must never sit opaquely over a running canvas), one froze `const accentNav = liveBackground;`, and two froze the propless `<RelayBackground />` element so a legitimate prop broke them. **(2) THE INVITE MESSAGE** (owner, with a screenshot of a party-line invite as it ARRIVED: *"this is it's look very ugly... put the username and then space between two brackets... make a BR break... and also below put kind of a stand-up code for the relay... make it unique. don't make the message very long"*). **TWO DEFECTS IN ONE SCREENSHOT, and the second is worse than the layout**: it read `Join "Gigh Meeting" on RELAY — dial 794 254` followed by the URL, arriving as ONE wrapped line — and the six digits were rendered as a green underlined **PHONE LINK**, so the most tappable thing in the invite dialled the recipient's own carrier. **THE OLD CODE'S OWN COMMENT WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE**: `Dialer.tsx` asserted that passing `title` + `url` separately makes the sheet *"lay them out cleanly (header on top, link below) instead of concatenating into one block"* — WhatsApp joins them with a SPACE. (v2.106.91 — **A DEAD-KEY SWEEP, AND IT FOUND AN ACCESSIBILITY REGRESSION I HAD JUST SHIPPED** (owner: *"Anything pending, anything remaining, or you finish all tasks"* — so the honest answer needed an AUDIT rather than a reading of the task ledger). **THE FINDING IS MINE FROM ONE RELEASE EARLIER**: the thread row's group disc carried `aria-label="Group conversation"`, and v2.106.89 swapping in the shared `GroupAvatar` DROPPED it silently — a screen reader lost the only thing distinguishing a group row from a person's, and no test could have caught it because nothing asserts the absence of an attribute nobody thought about. What caught it was sweeping the dictionary for keys with no reader: `msg.groupConversation` went from one reader to zero, which is a defect made VISIBLE by a translation key precisely because a key with no reader is evidence something stopped rendering. **THE SWEEP IS NOW A STANDING GUARD** (`dictCoverage.test.ts`), on the v2.106.86 reasoning one layer along: a published value nothing consumes reads as a contract, and an unread translation key is worse than that — it looks like COVERAGE, so somebody counting keys would conclude a screen is translated when nothing on it is. **THE EXEMPTIONS ARE NAMED RATHER THAN A THRESHOLD**, because a count-based tolerance ("fewer than N dead keys") is exactly how a real one hides among the accepted ones; and the list may not go STALE in either direction — a key that gains a reader must leave it, and a key that is deleted must leave it too, or the list rots into a comment (the v2.106.31 pattern). **`appearance.arabic` AND `appearance.english` ARE DELETED RATHER THAN WIRED**, which is the interesting half: each language is labelled in ITS OWN language as a LITERAL ("English", "العربية"), deliberately and permanently, because "Arabic" written in English is exactly the label that fails the person it is for — somebody who has landed in a language they cannot read and needs to find their way out. Keys for them would invite a later contributor to "fix" that by translating them, so their ABSENCE is now asserted along with the literals' presence. Four story-viewer aria-labels I created in v2.106.90 and did not wire are wired. **4 of 4 tripwires verified by MUTATION**, and the one SURVIVOR was a real gap in my own test of exactly the v2.106.61 class: the coverage sweep proves a key has a READER, which the call site satisfies, and says NOTHING about whether the component applies it — dropping `aria-label={label}` from `GroupAvatar` left the key "wired" and the screen reader with nothing. Now pinned on the application, and it bites. **THE HONEST REMAINDER, since that was the question**: `GroupInfoSheet` (~50 strings), `Admin` (~15), `GroupCallScreen`, `RelayEngine` and `VoicemailPrompt` are still English; `formatLastSeen`'s relative times return finished English; the RTL pass over the physical `pl-/pr-/ml-/mr-` sites is not done; the light theme still has no animated background (#158); and nobody has verified a call on a real device (#131). Safari cannot decode Opus-in-MP4 either — so preferring bare `audio/mp4` would ship a file with the right container, the right extension and the right type that **still fails on iPhone**, i.e. strictly HARDER to diagnose than the honest WebM failure. A MUTED element is decoration (the conversation's video THUMBNAIL is a muted `<video preload="metadata">`) and is left alone. (v2.106.51 — **MESH REMOTE AUDIO WAS NEVER PLAYED OUT ON ANY CALL WITH NO INCOMING VIDEO, AND THAT IS THE FOURTH INDEPENDENT WAY A CALL COULD CARRY NOTHING.** Found by MEASUREMENT rather than by reading, one hour after v2.106.48-50 deployed: on a real two-browser mesh VOICE call, inbound `totalAudioEnergy` read **EXACTLY 0 on both sides, 6 runs of 6**, while ~508 audio packets/side/direction arrived with 0 loss, candidate-pair `succeeded`, RTT 1ms. The same counter reads 2.3-3.5 on a mesh VIDEO call. `totalAudioEnergy` is the energy of audio actually PLAYED OUT, so zero while packets arrive is received audio that is never rendered — the owner's report verbatim. **THE THREE COMFORTABLE EXPLANATIONS WERE EXCLUDED BY A CONTROL CONTAINING NO RELAY CODE** (`scratchpad/energy-control.mjs`): a bare two-PC loopback in the same browser reads audio-only **2.01**, `visibility:hidden` **1.99**, and `--mute-audio` FORCED **1.87** — so the counter works for audio-only here, muting does not zero it, and hiding the element does not either. **THE MECHANISM**: `attachRemote` handed the tile's `<video>` the WHOLE stream (`v.srcObject = stream`), and `collectAudioEls`' own comment documented it — *"mesh remote `<video>`s (audio rides the video element)"*. On a voice call that stream ALSO carries a video track that will never deliver a frame, because the offerer always negotiates a null-track video m-line for the mutual-consent slot. **A `<video>` cannot reach HAVE_METADATA without dimensions and a frameless track supplies none**, so the element parked at `readyState 0` with the trace `emptied -> play -> waiting`, its `play()` promise NEVER SETTLED, and the audio beside it was never played out. Isolated three ways: strip the frameless track -> energy 2.64-2.77 and `currentTime` advancing in real time; turn both cameras on mid-call through the app's OWN buttons, no patch at all -> energy 0 -> 1.09/1.33 with the element completing to `playing`; hand the SAME received audio to a plain `<audio>` -> 2.50-2.61 while the engine's `<video>` stays stuck. A zero-RELAY-code loopback reproduces it exactly: audio + a sendrecv video transceiver with NO track stalls the `<video>` identically. **NEITHER NOMINATED SUSPECT WAS INVOLVED** — making `createMediaStreamSource` throw (removing the WebAudio metering tap) and making `setSinkId` a no-op both left energy at 0.0000, so both were excluded by measurement rather than by argument. **IT WAS NEVER ONLY ABOUT VOICE MODE, which is the part that matters**: the trigger is NO INCOMING VIDEO FRAMES, so it equally covered every 1:1 VIDEO dial answered with the plain Answer button (under v2.81 no camera transmits until consent — measured at energy 0.0000) and any group participant with their camera off. **AND THE COMPOSITION IS THE ALARMING PART**: the SFU path is structurally immune because it attaches per track (v2.106.50), so this bites through the MESH — which is exactly where v2.106.48's brand-new SFU fallback lands a call. A release written because the fleet's SFU was unusable was routing calls onto a transport whose voice calls had no sound. **THE FIX IS THE SHAPE THE SAME FILE ALREADY USES ON THE OTHER TRANSPORT**: each mesh peer gets its own `<audio>` (`PeerEntry.audioEl`), appended to the tile so it is IN the document (a detached element is not a reliable playout path on Android Chrome — the reason the SFU path inserts too), and the `<video>` receives `getVideoTracks()` only. **THE FRAMELESS CONSENT TRACK STILL REACHES THE VIDEO ELEMENT, deliberately**: a mid-call camera-on arrives by `replaceTrack` on that same track object with no new `ontrack`, so filtering it would mean the camera never appears — a mutation that filters it bites. **`collectAudioEls` IS THE LOAD-BEARING EDIT, not the new element**: it is the ONLY route to remote audio, so `applyAudioSink` (the output-device picker), `armAudioUnlock`'s tap-to-recover and the forced-loudspeaker route all reach it through that one function — an element missing there is three shipped features silently not covering it. The `<video>`s stay collected because they still need `play()` re-kicked for VIDEO, and `routeElToLoudspeaker` already early-returns on a stream with no audio track. **THE MSID-LESS MERGE ACCUMULATOR HAD TO MOVE** onto `PeerEntry.remoteStream`: it read the tile `<video>`'s `srcObject` as its accumulator, and with audio no longer on that element it would have quietly DROPPED the peer's audio — the very bug that merge path was originally written to prevent, one layer along. **`releasePeerAudio` IS ONE HELPER FOR TWO TEARDOWN PATHS** (active and held), because a detached media element with a live `srcObject` can keep playing in Chrome so a departed peer could still be heard; closing the pc ends their tracks, which covers it in practice, and the helper makes it true by construction. **VERIFIED BY DRIVING REAL CALLS, not by reading**: mesh VOICE goes from 0.0000/0.0000 to **2.677 / 2.728** with 512/511 packets and `audioBothWays` true; mesh VIDEO stays correct at **2.293 / 2.474** audio AND 283/374 video packets, so no regression. **10 of 10 tripwires verified by MUTATION** off a confirmed-GREEN baseline from byte-exact backups, the mutator aborting unless its target occurs exactly once, source byte-identical afterwards — including the original `v.srcObject = stream` reinstated verbatim, the held path's release deleted, the accumulator reverted, the element detached, and the consent track filtered. **A PRE-EXISTING PIN HAD FROZEN THE DEFECT, for the seventh time in this session's releases**: `androidAudioCamera.test.ts` asserted the literal `v.srcObject = stream;[\s\S]*?void v.play()` — i.e. it REQUIRED the line that made every voice call silent, under a title about preventing silence. So the state *"we are in the room, they answered, and no remote media arrived"* was covered by nothing at all. **THE DEADLINE IS ARMED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE CANCEL**, which is the point rather than a detail: arming it anywhere else leaves a window in which the call is bounded by nothing, and that window is the bug. On the SFU path the claim is simply FALSE — the caller joined the room at dial time, so nothing is being secured; we are waiting for the other side's media, which is a different problem with a different fix — so it now says *"Waiting for their audio…"* there while still saying *"Securing connection…"* on the mesh, where a transport really is in that phase. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 4760 tests.) (v2.106.36 — **THE MEDIA NODE'S STATS ENDPOINT WAS A PER-ROOM IP-DISCLOSURE PRIMITIVE, IN CODE I SHIPPED.** The removal plan listed three type questions I had not answered, and one of them was a live security question rather than a design detail: *does `WebRtcTransport.getStats()` include `iceSelectedTuple.remoteIp`?* Read off mediasoup's own declarations — **it does**: `WebRtcTransportStat.iceSelectedTuple` is a `TransportTuple`, and `TransportTuple` carries `remoteIp` and `remotePort`, i.e. **each participant's real public address**. The agent's `stats({roomId})` returned the raw report for EVERY transport in the room, so one call handed out every participant's address together. **THE REASON IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN LATER IS WHAT IT IS FOR**: the in-call quality readout is precisely what the coming increments wire to this, and a readout that forwards what it is handed makes one participant able to locate another — and **this app already ruled that class out once**, in v2.99.20, which restricted `avatarUrl` to our own storage because a remote image URL had become *"a remote-fetch primitive aimed at other users"*, harvesting IP and User-Agent from a call nobody answered, *"squarely against this app's no-tracing goal"*. An SFU stat handing the address over directly is the same thing with fewer steps. **STRIPPED AT THE SOURCE rather than in whatever forwards it**, because a filter in the caller is one a later caller can forget, and this way the address never leaves the node at all. **`protocol` IS DELIBERATELY KEPT** — it is the one field of the tuple a readout genuinely needs, since it says whether a call fell back to TCP, and it identifies nobody; stripping the whole tuple would take the answer away with the address. The node's OWN `localIp`/`localPort` go too, not because they are a participant's secret but because there is no reason to publish the private address downstream either. **THE ARRAY IS MAPPED, NOT SANITIZED**: `getStats()` returns one stat PER transport, so handing the array to the strip would have stripped nothing and left every address in place — the shape of a fix that reads as done, and a mutation doing exactly that bites. **AND A SECOND SECURITY CONSEQUENCE, which v2.106.35 delivered as a side effect and is worth stating rather than leaving unnoticed**: with per-transport listen, each transport took a port out of the worker's 10,000-port range, so a leaked transport was a denial-of-service clock — the plan asked how fast. Sharing one `WebRtcServer` per core removes the per-transport port entirely (they are allocated once at boot), so a leak now costs memory and router CPU and can no longer make a node unable to accept calls. **DRIVEN rather than pinned, which is the point**: the strip is a pure function and whether an address survives it is exactly what a source assertion cannot answer, so the function is re-declared in the test against a real mediasoup stat carrying every field the tuple type declares — with a companion assertion pinning that the agent's body is still verbatim, because the one weakness of a re-declared function is the original changing underneath it. `server/voipWebRtcServer.test.ts` → 20. **4 of 5 tripwires verified by MUTATION** off a confirmed-green baseline, `agent.mjs` byte-identical afterwards. **THE FIFTH IS REPORTED AS A NON-DEFECT rather than counted as a gap**: dropping the `typeof !== "object"` guard is behaviourally equivalent, because for a tuple-less stat `return stat` and `return rest` are deep-equal — and every shape that could carry an address (a string, an array, a falsy value) was checked and none leaks either way. The guard is KEPT, because relying on that equivalence would make the function correct only by reasoning about what mediasoup can return rather than by construction — the same call v2.99.49 made about `s3Config`'s unreachable conjunct. **A SYNTAX ERROR OF MY OWN, caught by `node --check` rather than by review**: I inserted the function declaration INSIDE the handlers object literal, which does not parse; reverted and placed at module scope. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 4745 tests.) (v2.106.35 — **THE MEDIA NODE MOVES OFF THE DEPRECATED PER-TRANSPORT LISTEN ONTO ONE `WebRtcServer` PER CORE — AND THE TYPES FORCED A DECISION THE PLAN HAD NOT ANTICIPATED.** Every transport in a room is now created on that room's server, so all of a core's transports share ONE UDP + TCP port pair instead of taking a port each out of the worker's range: one socket pair per core rather than one per participant. **THE PAIR IS RECORDED PER ROOM BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE DERIVED** — `createWebRtcServer` is on `Worker`, not `Router`, and `Router` exposes no `worker` getter, so nothing can walk from a room's router back to the server its transports must be created on; recording it per ROOM rather than looking it up per transport also makes it impossible for one room's transports to end up split across two servers, which would put one participant's media on a different port pair from everybody else's and is invisible until exactly one person cannot connect. **TWO `listenInfos` ENTRIES, AND THAT IS THE ONE MOST WORTH PINNING**: `listenInfos` is a LIST, so supplying only the UDP entry ships a node with NO TCP CANDIDATE AT ALL — and the people that fails are precisely the ones on a UDP-blocking network for whom every other candidate is also unusable, while every reading on the box looks healthy. `announcedAddress` rather than the deprecated `announcedIp`, and the server ports are taken from the BOTTOM of the range with each worker's own range starting above them, so a worker can never allocate a port a server already holds — collision avoided by construction rather than by hoping two ranges do not overlap. **THE DECISION THE TYPES FORCED, and it is the finding**: `announcedAddress` is decided when the SERVER is created and is IMMUTABLE, so converting naively would have made the auto-assigned-IP story WORSE than what it replaced — today's per-transport listen reads the live value at call time, so a re-read fixes new rooms within one interval, whereas a boot-created server announces the OLD address for the REST OF THE PROCESS'S LIFE. Updating the cached address alone would then be the worst possible combination: the heartbeat would report a healthy node at the NEW address while every transport it minted pointed at one that no longer reaches it — **and nothing could detect the difference, because this agent is the only source of that value**, so the app's `assignmentStillValid` compares two copies of the same stale number, they agree, and nothing looks wrong. So an address change now DEREGISTERS AND EXITS for systemd to restart, which is the same reasoning and the same machinery as the worker-death handler directly above it: every room here is already broken by the change, the deregister stops the app sending more, the TTL expires the node, its rooms are reassigned, and clients take the already-shipped rejoin path. Rebuilding the servers in place was the alternative and is strictly more code for the same outcome, because the rooms bound to the old servers have to be torn down either way. **A REAL BUG MY OWN CONVERSION INTRODUCED, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TEST**: `workers` became a list of `{worker, webRtcServer, port}` and the shutdown loop still read `w.close()` — `undefined` on a pair — so a PLANNED stop would have thrown on its way out, taking the clean deregister with it and making every restart wait out the full TTL. **AND THE ADDRESS-CHANGE PATH NEEDED A SECOND CALLER FOR THE DEREGISTER**, which had only ever existed inline inside the shutdown; extracted, because two copies of "how does a node leave the registry" is how one of them comes to leave a record behind. `server/voipWebRtcServer.test.ts` (13), pinned on SOURCE and honest about it — importing `agent.mjs` starts mediasoup workers, binds a port and connects to Redis — with the function bodies located by BRACE MATCHING rather than a fixed character slice (the v2.99.78 fragility, hit six times) and comments stripped, because the file explains in prose exactly what it must not do. **11 of 11 tripwires verified by MUTATION** off a confirmed-green baseline including the shutdown bug reinstated verbatim, the TCP listenInfo deleted, the listen and announce addresses swapped, and the exit removed; `agent.mjs` byte-identical afterwards. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A NODE, said plainly**: no mediasoup worker has been started here, no transport created, no candidate gathered. The security group is deliberately left wider than it now needs to be, and why is recorded rather than left as an oversight. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 4738 tests.) (v2.106.34 — **FOUR API FACTS READ OFF mediasoup'S OWN DECLARATIONS, AND ONE OF THEM IS AN OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINT NOBODY WOULD FIND BY READING THE DOCS.** Three planning decisions rested on documentation; the packages are one `pnpm add` away, so this answers them from the installed `.d.ts` instead. **(1) `announcedAddress` IS IMMUTABLE PER TRANSPORT** — it appears ONLY inside `TransportListenInfo`, a creation option, and there is no setter on `Transport`, `WebRtcServer` or anywhere in the type surface. **So an Elastic IP attached to a RUNNING node cannot be picked up by transports that already exist**: live calls on that node keep announcing the old address and their media stops arriving. There is no second opinion to disagree with, so the only defence is reading it often enough; the re-read moves from 60s to `NODE_TTL_MS`, which bounds the window to the one interval the app already reasons in. Reading IMDS at transport-creation time was considered and REJECTED — that puts a round trip on the call-setup path, where latency is a per-operation cost. **A CONCERN OF MINE THAT WAS UNFOUNDED, said rather than quietly "fixed"**: I expected the agent to have cached its address at boot and never re-read it. It already re-reads on a timer and `createWebRtcTransport` reads the live value at call time, so the code was right and only the interval was worth changing. **(2) `listenInfos` AND `webRtcServer` ARE STILL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE** in 3.23 exactly as in 3.19 (`Either<Either<listenInfos, listenIps>, webRtcServer>`), with `listenIps` and `announcedIp` both `@deprecated` — and a conversion must supply TWO entries, udp and tcp, or it silently ships UDP-only. **(3) `createWebRtcServer` IS ON `Worker`, NOT `Router`**, and `Router` does not expose its worker, so a room must record the `{router, webRtcServer}` PAIR rather than deriving one from the other. **(4) `producer.replaceTrack({track})` EXISTS ON THE CLIENT**, which is what makes one video producer per participant carry camera OR screen — matching how RELAY's screen share already works (`replaceVideoEverywhere` swaps the track on the existing publication) instead of racing two video consumers over one tile. **THE VERSIONS WERE ALREADY LYING AND ARE NOW PINNED EXACTLY**: the live nodes were installed at **3.19.3**, and a fresh `pnpm install` against `^3.19.3` today resolves to **3.23.2** — four minor versions apart, with a C++ worker compiled per install and nothing that would surface the difference until a call behaved differently on ONE box. (v2.106.33 — **THE TWO MEDIA NODES I LAUNCHED COULD HAVE STOPPED EVERY DEPLOY, AND THE FIX NEEDED NO AWS READ.** The 28-agent LiveKit-removal plan flagged this as *check before the next deploy, not after*, and it is the sharpest thing in a 386KB document: **`deploy.yml` runs on every push to `main` and targets `tag:Name=relay-app` with `--max-errors 0`** — so if either mediasoup node carries that tag, the deploy installs the app on it, fails the `/api/health` probe there, and **ABORTS THE WHOLE FLEET DEPLOY**. A push to main would simply stop deploying, and the error would be about a health check on a box nobody was thinking about. **WHETHER THEY CARRY IT CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED FROM THE REPO**: every EC2 call in every workflow filters on that one tag and nothing anywhere records what those instances were named — and this sandbox has no AWS CLI and no credentials, so I could not look. **SO THE GUARD IS NOT A TAG CHECK, WHICH IS WHY IT IS BETTER THAN THE CHECK THE PLAN ASKED FOR**: `[ -d /opt/relay-voip ]` is evidence the HOST ITSELF carries, an app box never has it, and it cannot go stale the way a tag list or a hardcoded instance id would. Those two already require a printed `ADMIN_EXIT=0` / `RECOVER_EXIT=0`, and the guard prints NEITHER, so exiting 0 makes the step FAIL loudly with `SKIP_MEDIA_NODE` in the output saying exactly why. The same line, opposite outcomes, because the callers differ in whether they demand a marker. **DEFINED ONCE at the job level rather than pasted into each action**, because a copy per call site is precisely how the sixth one comes to be forgotten — the class this repo keeps paying for. **AND THE PIN IS A SWEEP RATHER THAN A LIST**: it reads every `ssm send-command` in the file and requires each tag-targeted one to be guarded, so the action somebody adds next is covered instead of exempt. **ONE SITE IS DELIBERATELY UNGUARDED AND SAYS SO**: the coturn probe selects the relay hosts by matching `TURN_HOSTS` addresses against SSM-managed IPs, so a media node can never be selected there, and it is read-only — recorded as a decision rather than left looking like the one that was missed. **THE GUARD'S OWN SAFETY IS ASSERTED TOO**, because the dangerous failure is the opposite one: if the discriminator could ever be true on a real app server, every deploy would silently skip the whole fleet and report success, so the test pins that it keys on that directory AND that the agent's systemd unit really installs there — a guard checking a path nothing creates is a guard checking nothing. **TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN WORK, both caught by an assertion failing rather than by reading**: a python patch asserted its needle occurred once, found FOUR, and aborted **before writing** — which meant an earlier edit in the same script was silently discarded and had to be redone, so the assertion protected the file and cost a round trip; and my reference COUNT was wrong, claiming five where the workflow has six, now derived from the `jq` builders themselves rather than frozen as a literal that goes stale on the seventh. `server/awsOps.test.ts` → 49; **5 tripwires verified by MUTATION** off a confirmed-green baseline, including the guard removed outright and the guard made to exit NON-zero, sources byte-identical afterwards. **STILL OWNER-SIDE, and worth doing anyway**: tag those two instances `relay-voip`. The guard makes a mis-tag harmless; a correct tag is what makes `verify`'s instance table readable and stops aws-ops reporting a media node as part of the app fleet. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 4722 tests.) (v2.106.32 — **HARDENING THE DORMANT SFU REGISTRY, AND THE SHARPEST FINDING IS A FAIL-SHUT DEFECT I SHIPPED FOUR HOURS EARLIER.** A 26-agent design pass over v2.106.28's mediasoup work chose this as increment zero precisely because it is ZERO-RISK — `grep -rln "voipRegistry|mediasoupSignaling" server/ client/ shared/` returns only tests plus the two modules referencing each other, so nothing in `relay.ts` or the client imports either and every function here is pure or takes an injected client. **THE DEFECT: `isNodeFresh` WAS `age >= 0 && age <= ttlMs`, WHERE `updatedAt` IS THE NODE'S CLOCK AND `nowMs` IS THE READER'S** — two machines compared to the millisecond. **ONE MILLISECOND of forward skew excluded that node; both nodes skewed forward excluded the WHOLE FLEET and sent every call to LiveKit with nothing anywhere saying why**, which is exactly the fail-shut direction the module's own header says must never happen. it is admin-only by its ABSENCE from `MEMBER_CAPABILITIES`, and a test forbids that module-level set from ever being MUTATED, since `.add` for one group would grant the capability in EVERY group for the process's life (the v2.105.16 hazard). **EVERY REFUSAL ANSWERS IDENTICALLY** — gone, personal, not-an-admin-here — because status ids are small sequential integers and a distinguishable refusal maps which ids exist and which groups they belong to. **THE FAN-OUT NAMES THE AUTHOR, NOT THE ADMIN**, which is the subtle part: clients key their rings on the author, so publishing under the admin's identity would clear a ring they never had and leave the real one lit for 24h. **THE VIEWER ASKS WHETHER I AM AN ADMIN LAZILY** and only where it matters (a group reel, somebody else's slide) — on the FEED it would be an admin check per group on a query every client polls, for a button almost nobody taps; it defaults to FALSE in flight or on failure (hiding a control beats offering one the server refuses, the v2.103.3 rule) and never appears beside the author's own Delete. **#119**: `countActiveStatuses` counted every story the author had, so posting into three groups cost three personal slots; it now counts the SHELF being posted to — **PER (AUTHOR, GROUP) rather than per group, deliberately**, since a group-wide total would let one member fill the shelf and lock every other member out, a worse failure than the storage it saves, while the group total stays bounded by members × cap. The refusal names WHICH shelf is full, because "you can have up to 30" while a personal reel sits empty cannot be acted on. **THE ASSUMPTION IS STATED**: the owner asked to "add" this and keeping current behaviour would have been no action, so the intent is read as decoupling the caps. `server/groupStoryAdmin.test.ts` (26); **all 21 tripwires verified by MUTATION** off a confirmed-GREEN baseline. **TWO SURVIVORS, BOTH REAL GAPS IN MY OWN TESTS, each fixed and re-verified**: deriving `groupCid` as `?? 1` still satisfies `groupCid != null`, so the admin control could surface on a PERSONAL reel for anybody administering conversation 1 while every assertion stayed green (the KIND derivation is now pinned); and `if (false && !window.confirm(…))` left the confirmation text in place while removing somebody else's story with NO prompt — the v2.105.16 class, where asserting a guard APPEARS says nothing about whether it DECIDES. **ONE PRE-EXISTING PIN REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY**: it froze the one-argument `countActiveStatuses(me.id)`, i.e. forbade exactly this change, and now asserts both the call site's shelf AND that the counter separates the shelves rather than ignoring its argument. **A DEFECT IN MY OWN TEST HELPER, caught by it failing on CORRECT code**: `fnAt` took the first `{` after the name, which for `function f(): Promise<{…}>` is the RETURN TYPE — the v2.105.9 trap in a new position (there, a destructured parameter); the scan now requires parens closed and angles at zero. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A DATABASE, said plainly**: no MySQL here, so no admin has removed a story and no cap has been hit. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 3970 tests.) (v2.105.23 — **AN INVITE LINK NOW KNOWS WHO IT IS FOR, WHICH CLOSES #108** (the owner's group batch, verbatim: _"invitation URL that joins the group directly (guest enters a name, registered logs in) with an admin-chosen audience of guests-only / registered-only / all"_). **I HAD COUNTED THIS ITEM AS DONE AND IT WAS NOT** — v2.105.9 shipped the link, the epoch, the revoke and the join watermark, and the audience clause in the same sentence was never built; found by re-reading the task text against the token rather than against my own notes, which is the correction v2.105.19 was about. **THE AUDIENCE LIVES IN THE TOKEN AND THE EPOCH LIVES IN A COLUMN, and the split is the whole design**: the epoch is a property of the GROUP ("every link is dead now"), so it has to sit somewhere a signature cannot reach; the audience is a property of THIS LINK, because an admin can reasonably have a registered-only link in one place and an open one in another, both live at once. A column would collapse them into one setting AND would rewrite a link already handed out — so a link minted registered-only yesterday would start admitting guests because a toggle moved today, which is not what the person who minted it agreed to. **AN OPEN TOKEN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE OLD FORMAT, deliberately**: `all` is still four segments MAC'd over the same string, so every link minted in the last seven days survives the deploy that adds this — proven by rebuilding the v2.105.9 MAC BY HAND in the test rather than asking the module to confirm its own compatibility with itself. A restricted token is five segments whose MAC input INCLUDES the audience, so the two are domain-separated: appending `.registered` to an open token, swapping one audience for another, or dropping the segment from a restricted one all change the expected MAC and are refused. **A FIVE-SEGMENT TOKEN CARRYING THE LITERAL `all` IS ALSO REFUSED** — since `all` is MAC'd over the four-segment string it would otherwise verify, giving two spellings of one token for no benefit. **THE GATE GOVERNS ADMISSION, NOT MEMBERSHIP, and getting that backwards would have been the real bug**: membership is read BEFORE the audience check, so somebody who joined through a guest-only link and later REGISTERED — keeping their identity and number, per v2.99.49 — is not refused from a group they are already in. **THIS ONE REFUSAL IS NAMED while every other on the endpoint stays uniform**, and the reason is ordering: expired, revoked, mis-signed and no-such-group are one message so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which conversation ids exist, but the audience is reached only AFTER a signature this fleet minted has verified — so naming it reveals nothing a legitimate link-holder did not already hold, and "you need a registered account" is only useful if it is said. **SAID BEFORE THE TAP, NOT AFTER A REFUSED JOIN**: the preview reports `admitted`, and the Join button is REPLACED rather than disabled (the v2.103.3 rule — a control that looks live and always refuses is worse than one that is not there), with a refused guest routed to Profile, which carries the Register button and the copy saying their number and contacts carry over. **A GUEST ARRIVING WITH NO IDENTITY STILL PICKS A NAME FIRST, stated as a decision**: telling them the requirement earlier would mean making the preview anonymous, i.e. widening a signed-capability read to callers with no identity at all — one extra tap is the cheaper trade. **THE TIER RULE GAINED A THIRD READER AND SO WAS EXTRACTED**: `identityTier` is now the one single-identity reader (whoami's badge plus the gate at preview and accept), because two copies of "which tier is this" is how a screen comes to offer a Join button the accept then refuses; `requireIdentity` now carries `verified`, since `getRolesByIdentityIds` fails SOFT by design (it backs a badge) and without that field a DB blip would read a registered caller as a guest — refusing the very person a registered-only link was minted for. `server/inviteAudience.test.ts` (26); **22 of 24 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups off a confirmed-GREEN baseline, all four sources byte-identical afterwards. **ONE SURVIVOR WAS A REAL GAP IN MY OWN TEST**: dropping `audience` from the sheet's `create.mutate` call changed nothing any assertion could see — the picker would have become DECORATION, every link minted open whatever the admin selected, with nothing on screen saying so; now pinned, and it bites. **ONE SURVIVOR IS REPORTED AS A NON-DEFECT, measured rather than assumed**: replacing verify's `if (!audience) return null` with `?? "all"` survives because the one-encoding guard below then refuses the same token (checked by driving the mutated module — an unknown five-segment audience comes back null either way). It is KEPT so that "an audience we do not recognise is refused" is a LOCAL statement instead of a consequence of the next guard's ordering. **ONE MORE SURVIVOR WAS A BAD MUTATION OF MINE, reported rather than counted**: it ADDED a second `inviteAudienceAdmits` call after the join instead of MOVING the gate, so the `indexOf` of the first occurrence was unchanged; re-run as a genuine move, it bit. **AND A TRAP WORTH RECORDING: test files are excluded from `tsc`** (`"exclude": ["**/*.test.ts"]`), so inserting `audience` ahead of `nowMs` broke a positional call in an existing test that `pnpm check` could never have caught — the test caught it, and there is now a pin asserting that a clock in the audience position mints NOTHING rather than falling back to `all`, because the alternative reading hands out an open link to somebody who believes they restricted it. **TWO PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY**: one froze `create.mutate({ conversationId })` as an exact argument list, so it broke the moment the audience joined it while saying nothing about whether a mint could fire on MOUNT — the only thing it exists to prevent; the other froze whoami's inline `getRolesByIdentityIds([ctx.identity.id])`, i.e. it forbade exactly this extraction. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A DATABASE, said plainly**: no MySQL here, so nobody has minted a registered-only link and watched a guest be turned away. ""} ${lastName ?? ""}`.trim() || email.split("@")[0]`, yielding a clean "Prince" with no trailing space; `firstName` stays required so a nameless account is still impossible. CHECKED AGAINST THE SECURITY HISTORY FIRST, since `NameSchema` is named in the v2.99.81 approval comment — that short-circuit inferred "first device" from a name's PRESENCE and was DELETED, so an optional surname cannot reintroduce the bypass. `registerMononym.test.ts` (10) drives the REAL procedure input off the router rather than a copy (a duplicated schema is what drifts); mutation-verified. ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CODE and was corrected rather than forced — `EmailSchema` is deliberately permissive and the RESOLVER validates, so the test now pins where the rule lives. **AND THE WHOLE PAGE IS NOW DRIVEN END TO END**, which the first pass did not do — it only clicked Guest, which is exactly why the Registered path shipped broken: 43/43 headless checks across guest, register (two-word AND mononym), login, the PIN shortcut, Business and the back links, zero page errors. 3259 tests.) (v2.105.0 — **THE /app LOGIN & REGISTRATION PAGE, REBUILT FROM THE DESIGN HANDOFF.** Implemented `RELAY_LOGIN_HANDOFF.md` + the `design_handoff_relay_login/` prototype: one glass auth card over a full-page animated canvas, then LIVE NETWORK stats, feature chips, the "your identity is six digits" section and the footer. Copy, tokens, spacing, radii, type scale and the four keyframes are the spec's; icons are lucide-react, which the spec asks for. New `client/src/lib/relayBackground.ts` carries the spec's canvas code near-verbatim as it requested (glows, drifting grid, 130 parallax stars, cursor-attracted flow field, point vortex, node/link network with travelling pulses and broadcast rings, three orbiting satellites, 12-colour palette easing at ~1.1%/frame). **THREE DEPARTURES, STATED IN THE FILE HEADER RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED**: (1) THE STATS ARE REAL — §4 ticks them on a 2400ms timer with random increments, but RELAY already pushes all five figures over SSE (v2.99.72), so the tiles read `useLiveStats` and the spec's pop fires on a REAL change; inventing traffic on the front page of a comms product would be a lie told in numbers, and a cold cache shows an em-dash rather than a confident 0. (2) `choose` IS PROBE-DRIVEN, because `otpAuth.loginProbe` already knows which branch is correct and letting someone pick "Log in" for an unregistered address is a dead end by construction. (3) A PIN account skips `choose` entirely. **NOTHING SHIPPED WAS DROPPED**, which is the real risk in redesigning this surface: the spec's flow has no 4-digit passcode, no new-device approval and no guest recovery, and all three are live — `pin` (with an email-me-a-code escape), `waiting` (v2.99.7), and the `GuestRestore` card (v2.99.69, for whom restoring IS the primary action) are preserved in the spec's own panel language; MatrixReveal still outlasts identity landing; and the `/i/<pin>` call-link join screen is deliberately NOT routed here, staying the one focused field it has been since v2.94.5. **THE CANVAS IS BUDGETED** — the v2.99.67 lesson, on a heavier canvas: a low-power tier (63x63 -> 45x45 flow field, 1e4 -> 5e3 vortex, DPR 1), a frame budget (30fps / 20fps) instead of uncapped rAF, an early return on `document.hidden` with the rAF re-armed BEFORE it (returning first kills the loop on the first hidden frame — the exact v2.99.67 bug, now pinned by ORDER), and a reduced-motion path keeping glows/grid/stars exactly as §6 specifies. (v2.104.0 — **GROUP ROLES: CREATOR, ADMINS, AND THE DELETE OVERRIDE — WITH THE TAKEOVER PATH CLOSED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN** (owner, #108: *"the creator marked as Creator/admin inside group details; admins can appoint sub-admins; only group admins or sub-admins can delete any type of message"*). The spine of the group batch: two additive nullable columns, ONE predicate, two write paths. **THE MOST VALUABLE WORK IN THIS RELEASE WAS DONE BY AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE DESIGN, AND IT KILLED THE RULE THAT LOOKED MOST HARMLESS.** The first design granted every member FULL admin rights whenever a group had no admin, described as "behaviour-preserving". Statically it is; dynamically it is a **HOSTILE TAKEOVER PRIMITIVE THAT IS DEFAULT-ON FOR EVERY PRE-v2.102.0 GROUP** — they all have `ownerIdentityId` NULL, so any member could appoint THEMSELVES, at which point the group is no longer adminless and **the other nineteen instantly lose every power they had a second earlier**, with nothing telling them. It composed two ways further: a purged guest creator hands their group to everybody (reachable — a guest can create a group and the 30-day reaper takes unverified guests), and an invite link would grant adminship transitively, since a link-joined stranger becomes a member of a still-adminless group and therefore an admin able to remove all twenty originals. **THE FIX IS NOT A SMALLER FALLBACK, IT IS HAVING NONE**: `edit-profile` — the only thing a member can do today — is unconditional for members FOREVER, and the admin capabilities require a stored admin or the derived creator with no fallback whatsoever. So there is nothing for a first-mover to seize; taking adminship in a legacy group would remove NOTHING from anybody. A mutation that reinstates the fallback bites. **THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE IS STATED IN THE UI RATHER THAN HIDDEN**: a group created before v2.102.0 has no creator recorded, therefore no admin and no way to appoint one, so it keeps exactly today's behaviour and the sheet SAYS "created before admins existed" instead of offering a control that always fails. **THE CREATOR IS DERIVED, NOT STORED** — `conversations.ownerIdentityId` has been written at creation since v2.102.0 and read by NOTHING until now, so every group made since then already has an administrator with no backfill; it counts only while they are still a participant, which is what keeps the purge registry's `keep-safer` note true (a purged creator confers adminship on nobody). **ONE TIER, NOT TWO**: admin and "sub-admin" ship as one, because the owner's own sentence gives them identical power and nobody has named a thing one may do that the other may not. **UNSEND IS LEFT BYTE-IDENTICAL** and the admin delete is a SEPARATE function — widening it would have put an isAdmin-shaped parameter in exactly the position the house rule forbids, and `messageHide.test.ts` pins the literal sender clause that stops two concurrent unsends corrupting a stored counter. It REUSES `deletedAt` rather than inventing a mechanism, because five readers already filter on it and SEARCH is where a second rule silently fails; it KEEPS the attachments row and nulls only the reference, because `authorizeStorageKey` serves a key with no row as `unknown` and deleting it would make the media MORE readable (v2.98.4/F3); it **RECOMPUTES** unread rather than decrementing, because `deleteMessage`'s decrement excludes `ne(identityId, …)` — the SENDER there but the ADMIN here — so reusing it would skip the admin and wrongly decrement the real sender; and it **refuses a message that is not in the caller's own group**, since ids are small sequential integers, answering exactly like a missing one so the endpoint is no existence oracle. **`deletedByIdentityId` IS `keep-safer`, NOT `redact`, AND THAT IS THE REVIEW'S CORRECTION**: NULL in that column MEANS "the sender unsent it", so nulling a purged admin's id would rewrite their deletion into an apparent self-unsend — the row would positively assert the sender removed their own words. **AND THE REVIEW'S SHARPEST CATCH IS ABOUT THE GUARD, NOT THE FEATURE**: `REFERENCE_SHAPE` in `identityPurge.test.ts` is an ANCHORED, hand-kept alternation, so `deletedByIdentityId` escaped the machine check entirely and **the build would NOT have failed by name** — the one thing that guard exists to promise. Widened in the same commit, with the weakness recorded in place. **A NAMING COLLISION THAT SILENTLY RE-POINTED AN EXISTING SECURITY PIN, IN SIX FILES**: `deleteMessage` is a PREFIX of `deleteMessageAsGroupAdmin`, and six test files locate a function with `indexOf("export async function " + name)` — so `sweep20.test.ts`'s "unsend stays sender-only" assertion started reading the ADMIN path instead. Caught by the suite going red, fixed in all six with an exact `\b` match, and `sweep20`'s fixed `+2200` slice replaced with the function's own end. **TWO MUTATION SURVIVORS, BOTH THE SAME CLASS AND BOTH NOW THE THIRD OCCURRENCE OF IT**: the role-write scoping pin sliced to the end of the function and was satisfied by the RE-READ's byte-identical WHERE while the mutation stripped it from the UPDATE (an unscoped UPDATE changes a role in EVERY group), and the `conversationInfo` members-only pin was bounded past its own procedure so a stranger's `code: "FORBIDDEN"` satisfied it after this one's guard was deleted. Both rewritten to the write specifically with occurrence counts, then re-verified. **TWO TEST BUGS OF MY OWN, found before shipping**: a slice bounded by `"  list: publicProcedure"`, which occurs 570 lines EARLIER than `conversationInfo`, so the end came before the start and the slice was `""` — every assertion in it would have passed vacuously the moment one was a `not.toMatch`; and an assertion on the CONTENT OF A COMMENT that sits outside the slice, which is prose-pinning besides. **TWO PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY**: both froze `setGroupProfile`'s inline membership SELECT and DM refusal, i.e. they would have forbidden the consolidation into one predicate while saying nothing about the property; they now assert the gate runs inside the function and before the write, and the DM refusal is asserted where it now lives. `server/groupRoles.test.ts` (38); **all 38 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups and a confirmed-GREEN baseline, sources byte-identical afterwards. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A DATABASE, said plainly**: no MySQL is reachable here, so the statements are proven correct by reading and pinned, but no role has been written and no message removed by an admin. **NOT DONE**: the "all users can add" toggle, add/remove member, the 4-digit lock, group invite links and the group-call role seeding are v2.105.0 onward — and membership needs its OWN join watermark, because reusing `clearedUpToMessageId` would make a newly added member's group INVISIBLE (`listThreads` drops the row entirely when nothing is newer, which is exactly what v2.103.0 built it to do). Two additive nullable columns, no new dependency, no new env var. 3185 tests.) (v2.103.3 — **THE SENDER'S THUMBNAIL IN A GROUP, SIXTEEN BUBBLE COLOURS, AND THREE ASKS THAT WERE ALREADY BUILT** (owner, a screenshot batch about groups: *"every user gets a different bubble colour (up to 16) … each user's message shows a small clickable thumbnail of their profile image beside their name on the left, opening their status/story … show name, message/attachment content, date and time; group by day with a header at the top of each day"*). **THIS IS THE FIRST OF SIX RELEASES FROM A 19-AGENT RECON PASS, AND THE MOST VALUABLE THING THAT PASS PRODUCED WAS A LIST OF WHAT NOT TO BUILD.** Three of the four asks in this slice already shipped: per-person bubble colours since v2.99.85, day grouping with a header at the top of each day since v2.71 (Today / Yesterday / "June 28, 2026"), and the DATE on a message from a previous day since v2.99.73 — today's messages show time only on purpose, because repeating today's date forty times is noise. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 3147 tests.) (v2.103.2 — **THE RELAY WORDMARK WAS INVISIBLE THREE DIFFERENT WAYS, AND THE THIRD ONE v2.99.94 DID TO ITSELF** (owner: *"I saw one time you put the relay logo up in the top bar. It's moving animated. Now it's not showing. Why? The word rely itself. I told you every thirty seconds, make animation."*). **NOTHING BROKE IT — the wordmark's markup was BYTE-IDENTICAL to what v2.99.94 shipped**, which is why "why is it not showing" needed a diagnosis rather than a `git log`; a 19-agent investigation returned five findings and three of them are real, independent causes that each had to be fixed separately. **(1) A 390px BREAKPOINT DELETED THE WORD ON MOST PHONES.** `max-[389px]:hidden` removed it outright on 375px iPhones (SE / 8 / 13 mini) and 360px Androids while leaving the dot and the connection line in place — so the bar looked intact and the word was simply gone, which is the most literal reading of the owner's report. **MEASUREMENT SAYS THAT BREAKPOINT WAS TWO WHOLE PHONE SIZES TOO CAUTIOUS**: against the real built stylesheet, over five name shapes (long Arabic, single-glyph CJK, blank), the word coexists with the longest name and the PIN at 360 / 375 / 390 / 430 with real slack, and at 320 the only contact is the PEAK FRAME of the swell grazing an already-truncated name. So the breakpoint is **GONE ENTIRELY** and the swell is sized to the largest peak that keeps positive slack at every width down to 320 — **25/25 cases pass, worst case 2px**. **(2) THE ONLY MOUNT WAS ON A `md:hidden` SURFACE, so above 768px the animated wordmark DID NOT EXIST** — the desktop sidebar drew a different, static, uppercase span, and v2.99.94's own pin (*"exactly ONE mount"*) had frozen exactly that state. The sidebar now mounts `<BrandMark />`, which also gives desktop the connection line it had never had. **TWO MOUNTS IS CORRECT HERE BECAUSE THE SURFACES CANNOT BOTH BE VISIBLE** (`hidden md:flex` vs `md:hidden`), the wordmark's rules still live in one place inside the component so nothing is restated, and `useConnectionState` is a `useSyncExternalStore` over window events with **no timer**, so the second subscription costs nothing measurable — the old comment's objection does not survive being read. **(3) v2.99.94 CUT ITS OWN DUTY CYCLE AND THAT IS THE LIKELIEST ANSWER TO THE ACTUAL COMPLAINT.** Measured by sampling the running animation with a negative `animation-delay`, the three releases side by side: **v2.99.86 moved for 1.3s of a 5.5s cycle (22.8%); v2.99.94 moved for 1.3s of a 30s cycle (4.4%); this release moves for 3.1s of 30s (10.5%)**. Stretching the cycle to the cadence the owner asked for without stretching the motion with it delivered "every thirty seconds" and made the event inside it nearly invisible — a casual glance caught it about one time in ten. **AND A FOURTH DEFECT NOBODY HAD NOTICED, found by that same sampling: THE SHEEN BAND CAME TO REST ON THE WORD.** Its travel ended at `translateX(320%)` of a 24px band, which puts its left edge at 52.8px — inside a 64px mark — and it was HELD there from 7% to 100% of the cycle, so **for 29.2 of every 30 seconds there was a static bright smear over the last letter** instead of a sheen that passes. v2.99.86 had the same end point and only got away with it by repeating every 5.5s. **THE FIX IS PINNED AS A CLEARANCE CALCULATION RATHER THAN A MAGIC NUMBER** — the band is `w-N` at `-left-N`, so at its end keyframe its left edge sits at `(p/100 - 1) * N`, and the test asserts that clears 64px; the old shape computes to 43.2px and FAILS it, so the pin would have caught a bug four releases old. **TWO MORE THINGS HAD TO CHANGE THAT READING THE KEYFRAMES WOULD NEVER HAVE REVEALED**: 40% of the band's travel happened OFF-SCREEN (it is only inside the clip between 0% and 260% of its own width), and the timing was `ease-in-out`, which is **fastest in the middle — and the middle is precisely the visible part**, so the band crossed the letters at its highest speed and was gone in 1.4s of a 3.6s window. Tightening the travel to 8px clear of each edge and switching that one animation to `linear` took the visible band from **1.4s to 3.3s**, matching the word's own 3.1s, so the two halves are ONE event rather than a glint followed by a swell; the pop keeps its easing, because a swell should ease and a sweep should not. **THE WORD NOW BEATS TWICE, THE SECOND SMALLER**, which is the language the brand dot beside it already speaks (*"flashing similar to the heart way"*) — a single swell reads as a glitch. The band is widened 24px → 40px of a 64px mark, which is free safety-wise since it is clipped to the word's own box and cannot reach anything beside it however wide it gets — **unlike the swell, which is a transform and therefore paints outside its layout box even though it changes no geometry**; that is why the peak is a measured value and not a taste call. **THE ONE-SIDED PIN IS WHAT LET THIS REGRESS, AND IT IS NOW TWO-SIDED**: v2.99.94's assertion was that motion ends at or before 10% of the cycle, with no floor — so shortening the flourish to 5% passed cleanly, and a one-sided bound on a *perceptual* property actively rewards making the thing disappear. It now requires the window to end between 8% and 20%, both bounds load-bearing, and a separate pin requires the word and the band to end at the SAME percentage. **A HARNESS BUG OF MY OWN, reported rather than counted as a result**: the first in-motion run said the band was visible 95% of the cycle and I was one step from calling it a code defect — I had dropped the `flex items-center gap-2` wrapper, so `#word` was a bare inline span and the sheen's `inset-0` clip resolved against a body-width box; a flex item is blockified and gets the mark's own 64px, which is what the real bar does. **AND A SECOND**: the before/after comparison first reported 0% motion for both older variants, because `!important` on the `animation` SHORTHAND also pins `animation-delay`, so the inline seek was silently ignored and every sample read the same frame. **SAID PLAINLY, AND IT NEEDS A FIVE-SECOND CHECK ON THE OWNER'S PHONE**: iOS/Android **Reduce Motion** suppresses this entirely, because both animations are inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` and hoisting a decorative flourish out of that gate would override an accessibility request to deliver it. Under reduced motion the still frame is verified to be the plain unscaled mark with the band fully off it — measured, not assumed. `client/src/app/wordmarkFlourish.test.ts` (15); **all 25 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups and a confirmed-GREEN baseline, with the mutator aborting unless its target occurs exactly once, and sources confirmed byte-identical afterwards. **TWO PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY, both of which had frozen halves of this defect**: the mount-count pin asserted the single `md:hidden` mount, and the window pin asserted the one-sided upper bound. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 3132 tests.) (v2.103.0 — **SWIPE A THREAD ROW FOR UNREAD / PIN / MUTE / DELETE / ARCHIVE** (owner, with two screenshots: in the MESSAGES LIST — outside a chat — dragging a row LEFT reveals the right-hand actions and dragging RIGHT the left-hand ones; glassy buttons; holding a finger on the row is a second way in). **FOUR OF THE FIVE ICONS WERE FEATURES THAT DID NOT EXIST**: Mute worked but per-DEVICE, while Unread, Pin, Archive and thread-Delete did not exist at all — so the gesture is the visible half and four new capabilities are the real work, all of them **SERVER-SIDE PER PERSON**, because pinning a chat on a phone that leaves it unpinned on a laptop is the same lie a localStorage "delete for me" would have been (v2.102.2); a test asserts the endpoint mentions mute nowhere. **THE GESTURE LIVES INSIDE A VERTICALLY SCROLLING LIST, WHICH IS THE REAL RISK** — `touch-action: pan-y` keeps vertical panning with the browser so scrolling never has to be given back (the fix people reach for instead, `preventDefault` on touchmove, stops the list scrolling outright), and the pointer is claimed only once movement passes a threshold AND is more horizontal than vertical, with a mostly-vertical move ENDING our interest so it can never be grabbed back mid-scroll; capture happens strictly after the claim. **THE DRAG WRITES THE TRANSFORM IMPERATIVELY** — a state update per pointer move would re-render the whole thread list on every frame of every drag (the v2.99.67 mistake) — and only `transform` and `opacity` animate. **A FULL SWIPE COMMITS ONLY WHEN A SIDE HOLDS ONE UNAMBIGUOUS ACTION**: with three buttons there is nothing a full swipe could mean, and guessing would Delete a chat. Buried actions are not focusable (or Tab walks every hidden button on every row) and the tap that closes an open row cannot also open the conversation. **PIN SORTS TO THE TOP**, because a pin that only draws a marker on a row still buried forty threads down is not a pin; within each group the existing recency rule is untouched, so an unpinned list sorts byte-identically to before. **ARCHIVE GIVES THREADS THEIR OWN SECTION, LAST** — out of the way but not gone — and they leave Direct / Groups / Notes; pin and archive exclude each other, since a thread pinned to the top AND hidden in Archive is a contradiction the list cannot render. **UNREAD SHOWS A DOT, NOT A COUNT**: there is no number and "1 new" would be a claim about a message that may not exist; its own column rather than rewinding the read watermark, which would fight `recomputeUnreadFor` and could not express "unread" at all for a thread whose newest message is your own. **EVERY ACTION IS A TOGGLE** reading the row's own state, because an action that cannot be undone by the same gesture that did it is a trap. **DELETING A THREAD IS RECOVERABLE AND THE COPY SAYS SO**: it stamps the newest message id rather than bulk-inserting a hide per message — one column, and the filter rides the `(conversationId, id)` index, the shape `identities.historyClearedAt` has used for the call log since v2.75 — and **THE THREAD RETURNS BY ITSELF WHEN SOMETHING NEWER ARRIVES, AT NO COST ON THE SEND PATH**, since it is hidden exactly while its newest message id is not greater than the stamp and the groupwise-max has already produced that id. This DIFFERS from a per-message hide, where the thread stays with no preview: there the message went, here the person asked for the thread itself to go. Clearing also zeroes the badge and leaves Archive (a hidden thread with a live badge counts toward a total nobody can act on; a cleared thread in Archive would have no messages in it), and deleting the OPEN thread navigates away rather than leaving an empty conversation nobody can escape except with Back. It is the ONLY action behind a confirmation, whose copy names what survives. `server/swipeActions.test.ts` (22); **all 33 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups and a confirmed-GREEN baseline. **ONE SURVIVOR, AND IT WAS THE SAME CLASS AS LAST RELEASE'S**: the scoping assertion matched the re-read SELECT's copy of the clause while the mutation stripped it from the **UPDATE** — an unscoped UPDATE here pins, archives or CLEARS the thread for every member of the conversation; now pinned on the write specifically, with both halves counted so a missing one on either side is caught. One of my own mutations was bad and is reported rather than counted: its target did not match the source, so it aborted rather than surviving. Two pre-existing pins updated, both expected fallout — the timestamp pin (a pinned row now shows a marker before it, so `ms-auto` moves to whichever comes first) and the Groups-section pin (that filter now also excludes archived). **NOT VERIFIED ON A DEVICE, said plainly**: the scroll-safety rules are pinned and the logic tested, but nobody has dragged a row on a real phone — exactly where a gesture like this is judged. Four additive nullable columns, no new dependency, no new env var. 3113 tests.) (v2.102.2 — **"DELETE FOR ME": HIDE ONE MESSAGE FOR ONE PERSON** (owner, #81 — a way to remove a message somebody ELSE sent, for you alone). **IT IS NOT UNSEND, AND KEEPING THE TWO APART IS THE WHOLE FEATURE**: `deleteMessage` flips `messages.deletedAt`, which takes a message away from EVERYBODY and is rightly restricted to its own sender; this writes a row in a new `message_hides` table and changes nothing for anyone else — which is exactly why it is allowed on a message the caller did NOT send. A test asserts the hide path never touches `deletedAt` and never updates `messages` at all, and that unsend keeps its sender-only guard while hiding deliberately has none. **TWO SEPARATE CONFIRMATIONS**, because one dialog would have to describe two different blast radii — which is how somebody unsends for everyone believing they hid it for themselves; unsend says "removed for everyone", this says "everyone else keeps it, and they aren't told". **SERVER-SIDE, NOT localStorage, and that is why it is a feature rather than a polish item**: a browser-only version would be a lie, because the message would come back on that person's other phone. **THE PERFORMANCE DECISION IS LOAD-BEARING**: four reads had to learn the rule and one of them — the thread list's groupwise-max — is polled by every client every few seconds. The obvious change is a `NOT EXISTS` inside that aggregate and it is the WRONG one: it is a loose index scan over `(conversationId, id)`, and an antijoin defeats the loose scan for every user in the fleet to serve a feature almost nobody has used. So the aggregate is **UNTOUCHED**; instead the code asks which of the WINNING ids this person has hidden — one primary-key range lookup over ids already in hand — and only for the conversations that come back does a second, narrow query find the next-newest visible message. With no hides the extra cost is that single lookup and the plan for everyone else is byte-identical; both the fast path and the guard protecting it are pinned. **A THREAD WITH NO VISIBLE MESSAGE LEFT STAYS**, with no preview — dropping it would hide a conversation other people are still in. **ONE PREDICATE, FOUR READERS**: `notHiddenFor(identityId)` is exported and used by `listMessages`, `searchMessages`, the unread recompute and the preview fallback, so no surface can forget it; a `NOT EXISTS` rather than a `LEFT JOIN`, because MySQL optimises it as an antijoin against the `(identityId, messageId)` primary key. **SEARCH WAS THE LIKELIEST PLACE TO FORGET** — a hidden message reappearing under search is the feature silently not working. **MEMBERSHIP IS CHECKED BEFORE THE ROW IS WRITTEN**, and inside `hideMessageForIdentity` rather than at the call site, because a message id is a small integer and without it anybody could write a row naming any message in the database. **THE INSERT IS THE ATOMIC CLAIM**: `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` reports `affectedRows: 0` for a row that already existed, so a double-tap or a retry cannot run the unread adjustment twice — the defect v2.99.57 found in `deleteMessage`, where two concurrent unsends each moved a STORED counter; an already-hidden message SUCCEEDS without touching it, so the endpoint is idempotent rather than an error the UI must explain. **THE UNREAD COUNT IS RECOMPUTED, NEVER DECREMENTED** (v2.99.74: a decrement is not idempotent and a retry drives a stored counter negative) — new `recomputeUnreadFor` derives it from the read watermark, excluding this person's own messages, unsent ones and hidden ones, which also heals any pre-existing drift for that participant. **"NOT A MEMBER" AND "NO SUCH MESSAGE" ANSWER IDENTICALLY**, so probing ids reveals nothing about which conversations exist or who is in them. **THE MACHINE-CHECKED PURGE REGISTRY EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN**: `IDENTITY_REFERENCING_COLUMNS` failed the build BY NAME the moment `message_hides.identityId` existed, and it is declared `cascade` — purely theirs, visible to nobody else, describing a view about to stop existing, and unlike an `attachments` row deleting it cannot make anything MORE readable since the rows it names are other people's messages either way; a test asserts the declaration AND that the cascade really performs the delete, so a declared-but-not-done entry cannot read as covered. **A GUARD I TRIPPED WITH MY OWN PROSE, AND MADE STRICTER RATHER THAN LOOSER**: `contacts.test.ts` forbids destructive DDL in the boot migrator by sweeping the whole function for `/\bDELETE\b/i`, and the comment naming the "delete for me" feature tripped it in a function containing no DELETE statement at all — scanning prose as a proxy for SQL. The sweep is now case-SENSITIVE (every DDL string in the file is upper case) and matches destructive STATEMENT forms (`DELETE FROM`, `DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `RENAME`) rather than bare words, plus a new assertion that every `CREATE TABLE` is `IF NOT EXISTS` — **strictly tighter**, verified by planting a `DROP COLUMN` DDL and an unguarded `CREATE TABLE`, both of which the rewritten guard catches. **AND THE TRAP FOR THE TWELFTH TIME, IN THE FIX ITSELF**: that new `CREATE TABLE` assertion matched v2.102.0's comment "the CREATE TABLE never re-runs" and failed; it now runs on stripped SQL, like the sweep beside it. `server/messageHide.test.ts` (21); **all 26 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups and a confirmed-GREEN baseline. **ONE SURVIVOR, AND IT WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE**: the assertion that the unread recompute is scoped to one participant matched the SELECT's copy of the clause while the mutation stripped it from the **UPDATE** — an unscoped UPDATE rewrites every member's badge in the conversation to this person's count; now pinned on the write specifically, with the count asserted so a missing clause on either side is caught rather than masked. One additive table, no new dependency, no new env var. 3091 tests.) **the header disc also shows the group's own photo**, having drawn the generic glyph even for a group WITH a picture, so the thread row and the conversation's own header disagreed about the same group. **NOTHING IS OPTIMISTIC**: it writes a row other people are looking at, so a failure already painted as success would leave this member believing they renamed a group everybody else still sees under the old name; Five pre-existing pins repointed at the shared picker, expected fallout from the extraction and strictly better since they now name the one place the rule lives. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 3070 tests.) (v2.102.0 — **A GROUP GETS ITS OWN 6-DIGIT ID, AND THE THIRD NUMBER TABLE NEARLY GAVE IT AWAY** (owner, #89: a group should have a 6-digit GROUP ID, a group avatar, a group status, and a groups section). **THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING IS NOT THE FEATURE — IT IS WHAT A THIRD NUMBER TABLE BREAKS.** `number_reservations` is the ledger that stops a handed-out number ever reaching a stranger, and BOTH of its deleters guard with `NOT EXISTS` subqueries naming `identities` and `party_lines` **ONLY** — so a group number, living in neither, would have looked *unclaimed* to `reapUnclaimedReservations`, whose own predicate is `claimedAt IS NULL`: the reaper would delete a LIVE group's reservation and the id could later be reissued to somebody else. `releaseUnusedNumberReservation` had the same blind spot, so a failed create elsewhere could un-reserve a bound group id. This is **the exact trap v2.100.0's purge hit, in a second place** — there the fix was to INSERT the number with `claimedAt` stamped, here it is a third `NOT EXISTS` conjunct on all three call sites, each pinned. **ONE ALLOCATOR, THREE CALLERS, AND THE COUNT IS ASSERTED**: `allocateGroupNumber` is four lines that delegate to `allocateSharedNumber`, so a group inherits the cross-table `numberTaken` check, the atomic reservation claim that closes the NEW-vs-NEW race, and the global mint budget; a test asserts the 40-attempt search loop occurs exactly ONCE in the file and that exactly three functions call the shared allocator, because a parallel allocator is precisely the cross-table collision v2.99.30 closed. **`numberTaken` NOW CHECKS ALL THREE TABLES**, wrapped per-table so a pre-migrator boot reads *free* rather than throwing — the same shape the party-line check has had since v2.89. **BOTH MACHINE-CHECKED REGISTRIES GAINED AN ENTRY, WHICH IS THE POINT OF HAVING THEM**: `conversations.number` is declared **`not-a-person`** in `NUMBER_BEARING_COLUMNS` (a MEMBER renumbering must never move the group's id — the id belongs to the group, not to whoever created it, the same rule a party line already has), and `conversations.ownerIdentityId` is declared **`keep-safer`** in `IDENTITY_REFERENCING_COLUMNS` with the reason stated: a purged creator's id is left pointing at a deleted row ON PURPOSE, because nulling it would be a silent ownership change for members who did not ask for one and are not told. Both registries scan `drizzle/schema.ts` and fail the build on an undeclared column, so these were not optional additions — the suite named them. **THE ID IS ALLOCATED BEFORE THE TRANSACTION AND RELEASED IF THE ROW NEVER LANDS**, or every failed create would leak one of ~980,000 ids; and an EXHAUSTED allocator degrades to a group with `number = null` rather than a failed create, because a group is reached through its thread and the id is for identifying and sharing it, not for reaching it. **THE UNIQUE INDEX IS ADDED BY THE BOOT MIGRATOR, not the CREATE TABLE** — `conversations` exists on every deployment so the create never re-runs; MySQL tolerates repeated NULLs under a UNIQUE index, so every DM and every pre-release group is untouched. **`setGroupProfile` PUTS THE MEMBERSHIP CHECK INSIDE ITSELF**, never in options a caller passes: it writes a row several people share, so "who may change it" IS the safety argument and must not be something a call site can forget (the same reasoning that put the purge's guard inside `claimIdentityForPurge`). Any member may edit — a group has no owner role today and inventing one here would be a permission model nobody asked for. It REFUSES a DM outright (a DM borrows the peer's name, photo and status; it has none of its own), each refusal is NAMED because "not a member" and "that's a direct chat" need different next steps, and the avatar URL goes through the SAME `keyInOwnerNamespace` gate an identity's photo does, matched with `lastIndexOf` so the absolute form is covered too (v2.98.4/F2 plus v2.99.26/H5) — without it a group could be pointed at a stranger's private attachment and the proxy would serve it. **NO PRESENCE IS DERIVED FROM A GROUP'S STATUS**, unlike an identity's: a group has no presence, so there is nothing for an availability to describe, and a test pins that `statusOverride` is absent from the function. **THE STATUS VOCABULARY IS THE ONE FROM v2.101.1, NOT A SECOND ONE** — `shared/profileStatus.ts` normalizes and formats it, so a group's status and a person's cannot come to read differently. **THE WIRE FIELDS ARE NAMED `group*`, NOT REUSED `peer*`**: a group is not a peer, and one field meaning two things is how a surface comes to render a group's id as a person's; they are threaded explicitly out of `listThreads` rather than spread, so a new column cannot reach the browser without a decision. **A GROUP IS NOW FINDABLE BY ITS OWN ID**, which is most of what having one is for, and the thread row shows it in the same place a person's sits, `dir="ltr"` so an RTL locale cannot reorder the digits; a broken group photo falls back to the purple glyph rather than the browser's broken-image icon, the rule `PeerAvatar` already follows. **THE GROUPS SECTION ALREADY EXISTED and is CONFIRMED rather than rebuilt** — Messages has grouped threads under Direct / Groups / Notes since the v2.99.98 sectioning, so the fourth item on the owner's list needed nothing. **SHIPPED HALF, SAID PLAINLY** (the owner authorised this split): the id, the allocator wiring, all three ledger guards, both registry entries, the columns, the guarded write endpoint and every READ surface are here; **there is no editor UI yet** — nothing in the app calls `setGroupProfile`, so a group's photo and status can be set by an API caller and will render everywhere, but a member cannot yet pick them from a screen. That plus the group story ring (#96, which was blocked on exactly this data) is v2.102.1. `server/groupIdentity.test.ts` (27), the allocator delegation / the three ledger guards / the registry entries tested against the REAL exported registries rather than a copy; **all 32 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups with the mutator aborting unless its target occurs exactly once. **THREE MUTATION SURVIVORS, all real weaknesses in my own tests and each fixed then re-verified**: the "allocated before the transaction" case passed with the allocation moved into an UNUSED CLOSURE, because the text still appeared before the transaction — it now pins the try block's body exactly; the avatar-gate case passed with the condition replaced by `if (false)`, the pin-the-TEXT-while-the-PATH-dies shape, so the condition itself is now asserted and a constant-false one forbidden; and a `not.toMatch(/border-b/)` meant to forbid a bottom border matched inside `border-border` on the group avatar's ordinary ring, so an unrelated correct line failed a pin — bounded to `/border-b(?![a-z-])/`. **AND THE PROSE TRAP FOR THE TENTH TIME**: `setGroupProfile`'s own comment names `statusOverride` in order to say it is NOT derived, which the `not.toMatch` guarding that very property matched. **FIVE PRE-EXISTING PINS UPDATED**: `chooseNumber.test.ts` froze the registry list (I first inserted the new entry in the wrong position and the test said so), `adminToolParity.test.ts` needed the new table in its SQL map, and three Messages pins — one of which, `messagesRowRedesign.test.ts`, had frozen `t.peerNumber.slice(...)`, i.e. it asserted the 1:1-only rule this release deliberately widens. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A DATABASE, said plainly**: no MySQL is reachable here, so the third `NOT EXISTS` conjunct is proven CORRECT by reading and pinned at all three sites, but no reservation has been reaped and no id observed surviving one. Five additive nullable columns and one additive unique index, no new dependency, no new env var. 3045 tests.)
