So the label is STORED and the availability it implies is **DERIVED** by `overrideForStatus` in EXACTLY ONE PLACE at write time; a test counts that call across the whole server and asserts it appears ONCE, because two places computing an availability from a label is how the label and the dot come to disagree. There is nothing to keep in sync, because one is a function of the other. **THE DERIVATION IS PROVEN CLOSED, not merely written**: every value it can return is fed back through the REAL `sanitizeStatusOverride` and the REAL `effectiveStatus`, and asserted to land inside the four display states every surface already knows — so a label can never produce a fifth state. **"WORK" DERIVES AUTO, and that is a decision rather than an oversight**: somebody at work is usually AT their computer, so marking them away would make the LED lie about the most reachable state on the list; vacation and travel both derive `travel` (the badge already exists) and busy derives `away`, which is the whole point of saying busy — people know before they dial. **CLEARING IS WRITTEN UNCONDITIONALLY**: the override is set even when the resolved label is null, or somebody back from vacation would still read as travelling with no label left on screen to explain why. **COLOUR IS REINFORCEMENT, NEVER THE CARRIER, and that is why these five hues needed no contrast measurement**: the emoji names the status and the label renders in the ordinary foreground colour, with the hue on a tint and a border — unlike the `--relay-*-text` tokens, which DO carry small coloured text and were measured for exactly that reason (v2.99.94, where the obvious token reuse computed to 3.72:1 and failed AA). Both the picker's selected state and the chip apply their hue via an INLINE style, never a runtime-composed Tailwind class, because the JIT compiler cannot see a class name assembled at render time and `border-[${color}]` comes out unstyled — the trap recorded for the tab-bar accents. **TAPPING THE CURRENT STATUS CLEARS IT**, so the picker is its own "none" control rather than needing a sixth button whose only job is to undo the other five; the note appears only ALONGSIDE a status, because on its own it is a caption for nothing, and a refetch cannot erase a note being typed (the field follows the server only while unfocused). **THE NOTE COLLAPSES NEWLINES** rather than storing them, since the chip is one line on every surface and a stored newline would be swallowed on one and break a layout on another. **THE LABEL IS WITHHELD WITH PRESENCE**: a guest inactive over a day has presence suppressed for privacy (v2.95), and "On vacation · back Monday" leaks exactly what the suppression withholds — in words, which is worse than a dot; a party line carries none at all, because a line is not a person. `normalizeProfileStatus` FAILS TO NULL rather than to a default, for the same reason `normalizeLoginMethod` does: this label is a claim somebody makes about themselves, shown to everybody who looks them up. **ONE CHIP COMPONENT, TWO SURFACES** (the popup and the full profile), asserted by count, since two copies is how the two come to describe one person differently. `server/profileStatus.test.ts` (36), the derivation and the normalizers tested BEHAVIOURALLY through the real presence functions; **32 tripwires verified by MUTATION, and ONE SURVIVED — a real gap**: the case-folding case used `"AWAY"`, which is not a status in either direction, so it never exercised the fold at all; `"WORK"` is the input that distinguishes them, and refusing it is right because lowercase keys are the only thing this code ever writes. Two additive nullable columns, no new dependency, no new env var. 3017 tests.) (v2.101.0 — **STORY AND STATUS STOP BEING THE SAME WORD** (owner, correcting this for the THIRD time: *"For the story is the one on the message where you can post video, voice, text, image… The status will be showing on your profile, and it will give you, like, you are in work, vacation, travel, free, and you can put some notes on it… So fix the pronouncing properly everywhere"*). A STORY is the ephemeral post on Messages that people react and reply to, signified by the avatar ring; a STATUS is the profile label. Every user-facing string that meant the ephemeral post now says story — the ring's tooltip and aria-label, the top-bar pip, the strip title on both shells, the composer heading and placeholder and Share button, "My story", the delete toasts, the reply aria-label, the story-reply chip in a chat bubble and its four kind labels, and the audience row that used to read "Status privacy" while naming a completely different feature. **THE RENAME IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL, and saying which way is most of the value**: the Profile pane that opens the away/travel picker IS a status and keeps its name — renaming it too would have swapped one wrong word for another. **THE API KEEPS ITS NAMES, DELIBERATELY**: the `statuses` table, the `status.*` router and the `relay:open-status` event are untouched, because a half-renamed API is worse than a consistently-misnamed one — a caller who learns that `status.feed` returns stories has one thing to learn, whereas a codebase where some story paths say story and others say status has a trap in it; that decision is asserted so it reads as a choice. **THE LOAD-BEARING TEST IS A SWEEP, NOT A LIST**: it extracts every `title` / `placeholder` / `aria-label` / `toast` string from six surfaces and fails if ANY of them says "status" to a person, so the next story string somebody adds with the wrong word is caught rather than counted — comments stripped first, since a comment explaining the distinction legitimately uses both words. **THE AVATAR MENU IS REBUILT TO THE OWNER'S OWN LIST** (*"open story / add story / add status / profile / log out"*): Open-my-story renders only when there IS one, but **ADD is no longer the else-branch of OPEN** — it used to be either/or, so somebody who already had a story had no way to post a second from here. **"SET MY STATUS" NEEDED AN OUT-OF-BAND INTENT, and the reason is recorded rather than worked around**: Profile's panes are LOCAL STATE because wouter's `useLocation` returns `pathname` only, so a `#pane` navigation re-renders nothing — the tap would do nothing with no error to explain why (v2.99.89) — and a real sub-route per pane would put ten entries in the app's history for one screen. New `client/src/app/profilePane.ts` carries the request in `sessionStorage` rather than a module variable, because Profile is a LAZY route whose module may not have evaluated when the intent is set; it is ONE-SHOT by construction (the read clears it, so returning later cannot reopen a pane somebody shut) and every storage access is guarded, since a blocked `sessionStorage` must degrade to landing on the hub rather than throw on the way to a page. **THE PANE SET BECAME A RUNTIME ARRAY WITH THE TYPE DERIVED FROM IT**, so an out-of-band request can be validated against the real set and a pane added later cannot become un-requestable with nothing to say so; an unknown value lands on the hub rather than putting the page into a state it has no branch for. `client/src/app/storyVsStatus.test.ts` (16); **24 tripwires verified by MUTATION**. **A BAD MUTATION OF MY OWN, reported rather than counted**: swapping `requestProfilePane` and `navigate` inside one handler survived — and it was RIGHT to, because both calls are synchronous and Profile mounts in a later render either way, so the order carries no behaviour; widening that is exactly what CLAUDE.md warns against ("a third meaning would make colour stop carrying information"), so the new label needs its own column and a derivation rather than being crammed into the presence state. **A COLLISION FOR THE OWNER TO SETTLE, flagged rather than silently resolved**: the avatar ring means "this is you" in the top bar and "unseen story" on `PeerAvatar` — one shape, two meanings. 2981 tests.) A row with an IP and no country is the HONEST degraded state, and on a LAN, behind a VPN or on a GeoIP miss it is the ordinary one. **THE IP COMES FROM `pickClientIp`**, which trusts the hop the proxy APPENDED rather than the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry (v2.98.4/F4) — read the other way, anybody could write their own "where from" into the owner's security notice. **ONE GEO IMPLEMENTATION, SHARED WITH THE TOP BAR'S FLAG CHIP**: `resolveGeoForIp` is extracted out of the `geoSelf` procedure and a test asserts `ipapi.co` appears in the code exactly ONCE, because two copies of "which country is this IP" is how a login notice and a flag come to disagree about the same person — the divergence class v2.99.77 and v2.99.96 were both about. **THE LOGIN METHOD IS RECORDED, NEVER INFERRED**: a session row looks identical however it was created, and `accountExisted` is the only thing distinguishing a first registration from a sign-in — so `code` / `register` / `pin` are stamped at their own three call sites, and `normalizeLoginMethod` FAILS TO NULL rather than to a default, because "signed in with a passcode" when it was really an email code is worse than saying nothing. **ONE PROJECTION, THREE SURFACES**: `pendingSessionWire` builds the approval prompt, the notification-centre row AND the Devices list, since three projections of one event is how three screens come to describe a single login differently; the phrasing itself lives in a pure `server/loginOrigin.ts` and a standing guard fails if any surface hand-rolls a place string or a method label. **`describeLogin` EMITS NO DANGLING SEPARATOR** — an interpolation that always writes " · " is how a card ends up reading "Dubai, AE ·" with nothing after it. **THE IP IS SHOWN, and that is a decision rather than an oversight**: it is the account owner being shown their OWN sign-in, it is the one detail that survives a geo failure, the owner named it explicitly, and every procedure carrying it is scoped to `ctx.user` so it reaches nobody else; rendered `dir="ltr"` so an RTL locale cannot reorder it. **THE NOTIFICATION CENTRE NAMES THE SIGN-IN ONLY WHEN THERE IS EXACTLY ONE** — with two waiting, naming the newest would describe one and imply both — and the prompt now ends with what to actually do ("If this wasn't you, decline it"), which is the sentence that makes the details useful rather than merely present. `server/loginOrigin.test.ts` (33), the formatting and every normalizer tested BEHAVIOURALLY because a source pin cannot tell you whether a login with a city and no country reads correctly; Four additive nullable columns, no new dependency, no new env var. 2965 tests.) (v2.100.0 — **DELETING A PERSON: ONE CASCADE, TWO CALLERS, AND THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE** (owner, twice: *"if I click delete, it will delete him completely. This is v2.98.4/F3 in a second place, where the fix was likewise to KEEP the row on a view-once burn; the row is what holds the object shut. Their OWN address book (`contacts.ownerId`) goes in full. (3) **THE 6-DIGIT NUMBER IS TOMBSTONED, NEVER RELEASED**, and this is the one place the obvious implementation is silently wrong: `number_reservations` only exists from v2.99.30, so an older identity may have NO row, and `reapUnclaimedReservations` deletes any row whose number is absent from both number tables — *precisely the state a purge creates*. So step ZERO of the cascade INSERTs the number with `claimedAt` stamped (the reaper's own guard is `claimedAt IS NULL`), before anything is destroyed; without it, purging a pre-ledger guest would put a written-down number back in circulation for a stranger. Order asserted, not merely presence. **THE CLAIM IS ONE STATEMENT DOING TWO JOBS** — a conditional UPDATE of the new nullable `identities.purgeStartedAt` whose `affectedRows` decides which of two instances owns the purge (the `claimMissedCallEmail` pattern), and which in the SAME statement NULLs all three handles that could resurrect the row: `guestToken`, `deviceId`, `recoveryHash`. **THAT IS ALSO HOW EVERY GUEST RESOLVER IS CLOSED, STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY EDITING FOUR HOT AUTH PATHS** — `getIdentityByGuestToken`, `getIdentityByDeviceId` and `findRecoverableGuestIdentity` each look a guest up BY one of those handles, so nulling them closes all three at once and no fourth can be forgotten; adding a `purgeStartedAt IS NULL` conjunct to each was the alternative and it is exactly where v2.99.49's data-loss bug lived. A test ENUMERATES those sites and asserts each still keys on a destroyed handle. Holding a long write lock instead would have blocked `messages.send` for everybody meanwhile. **ORDER IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY, NOT CONSISTENCY**: there are ZERO foreign keys in this schema, so nothing cascades and nothing detects an orphan — the steps are ordered so every intermediate state leaves the person strictly LESS reachable than the step before (presence, push, watches and the signaling mailbox first), and `identities` is deleted LAST with the claim restated, because killing it first means no later pass could ever find the wreckage. **A DM GOES WHOLE, A GROUP DOES NOT**: the branch with the real blast radius is a pure planner, because getting it wrong either destroys a six-person group over one lapsed guest or leaves a thread half-visible in somebody's inbox — a DM is between two people and one of them is going, a group survives while anyone remains, and an unknown `kind` is treated as a DM (failing toward not stranding a thread). A survivor's reply is unhooked BEFORE the quoted message is deleted, and `unreadCount` is **RECOMPUTED, never decremented**, since a decrement is not idempotent and a retried sweep would drive a stored counter negative (v2.99.74). **A CONFERENCE LOG BELONGS TO THE SURVIVORS TOO**, so the shared row stays and this person's roster entry is scrubbed — matched on `identityId`, falling back to the number ONLY for an entry that carries no id, because a renumber can put one number on two entries across time and matching it would delete a stranger from somebody else's call log. **THE `users` ROW GOES LAST OF ALL on the admin path**, or a "delete" lasts until the person signs in again with the same email and is handed a fresh identity. **THE LOAD-BEARING TEST IS NOT ABOUT THIS RELEASE** — it is about the next table somebody adds: `IDENTITY_REFERENCING_COLUMNS` declares every identity-naming column and its disposition, and the test SCANS `drizzle/schema.ts` and fails the build if any has no entry, the contract `numberContinuity.test.ts` has enforced for the number since v2.99.54; verified by planting a fake column and watching it fail BY NAME, plus the reverse direction so a rename cannot leave a stale entry reading as covered. **OFF BY DEFAULT, WITH A DRY RUN IN BETWEEN**: `RELAY_GUEST_PURGE` is one variable with three states, the gate is the FIRST thing the sweep does (ahead of `getDb`, so a disabled sweep costs nothing at all), and `dry` logs ids and numbers — never a display name — because nobody can count the eligible rows from outside production and the first honest figure has to come from a log rather than a design document. The interval is registered unconditionally so arming it is one env var and a restart. **THE COUNTDOWN BESIDE THE BLUE BADGE** reads the server's own `guestExpiresAt` rather than a day count written into the copy, is NULL (the field OMITTED, never 0) for anyone who is not an expiring guest, renders from ONE component on both the popup and the full profile, and says the clock RESETS on every visit — true (`touchGuestExpiry`) and the part that makes the figure non-frightening, since a bare countdown implies one nobody can stop. **THE ADMIN PANEL CONFIRMS BY TYPING THE NUMBER, not with a Yes/No**: the list shows several people at once with a Delete button in the same place on each, so a plain confirm protects against hesitation but not against acting on the wrong row — which is the mistake that actually happens here. It also states what SURVIVES, so "everything" is not a promise the code cannot keep. **A CLAIM FROM MY OWN DESIGN REVIEW, CORRECTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED**: the review held that deleting the identity makes their profile photo MORE readable; read against `storageProxy`, that is wrong — an avatar has ALWAYS been served to any signed-in caller (it renders on the incoming-ring card, and the code says so), so the purge neither widens nor narrows it. What IS true is that the bytes are not erased, because this codebase has no storage-delete path at all, and the panel says so in those words instead of claiming an erasure. **SELF-DELETION IS REFUSED**, for the same reason a self-demotion is: the one account nobody else can restore for you is your own. `server/identityPurge.test.ts` (62), the planners / roster redaction / countdown / env switch tested BEHAVIOURALLY; **38 of 39 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups with the mutator aborting unless its target occurs exactly once. **A BAD MUTATION OF MY OWN, reported rather than counted**: the reply-unhook ordering case appended an inert `void 0;`, which changes no order at all — replaced with one that genuinely moves the statement after the delete, which bit. **AND A REAL WEAKNESS IT FOUND**: "reachability is severed before content" compared `indexOf` results, so DELETING the `onlineWatches` sweep outright left it green — `-1` is less than anything — meaning a purged person could still fire a "they're back online" push at somebody; existence is now asserted first, and all three severing steps re-verified. One pre-existing pin updated: the admin panel's capability set, which turned red on the new procedure exactly as designed. **NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A DATABASE, said plainly**: no MySQL is reachable here, so the statements are proven CORRECT and the ORDER proven, but no row has been deleted and no race observed — which is why it ships off by default with a dry run. One additive nullable column, no new dependency, no new required env var. 2932 tests.) defaults OFF. **THE GROUPING KEY IS THE IDENTITY, NEVER THE NUMBER** — the number moves and the identity does not, so keying on the number would file one person's calls under two headings the moment they renumber, the class v2.99.95 had just fixed three rows above; derived from the same filtered list as every other section so a search applies identically, and hidden when nobody is online. **EVERY HEADER CARRIES TWO NUMBERS**: total in muted, then how many are online in green, with a green ZERO withheld because it spends attention on the one answer needing none; the Online section shows ONE number since its total IS its online count and "5 · 5" would be noise; both `tabular-nums` so the column cannot jitter. **THE GREEN IS THE AA-MEASURED TEXT TOKEN, NOT THE LED GREEN** (the LED green is 4.46:1 on the light card and fails AA at this size — measured in v2.99.86). **ONE PREDICATE ANSWERS ALL THREE QUESTIONS** — which rows the section holds, what the count says, whether the header marks anything — because three copies of "is this person online" is how a section lists four people under a header that says three (the class v2.99.95 had just removed from History); the purge must be BUILT, is irreversible, and reaches other people's data, so the semantics went to the owner, who chose a FULL CASCADE DELETE and to KEEP the 30-day hold, shipping as its own release with its own review rather than bolted onto a UI change. `client/src/pages/app/contactSections.test.ts` (18), the online rule tested behaviourally because the two ways a count can silently lie are suppression and being on a call. (2) the number was NOT DIGIT-FOLDED on Contacts or the group picker, which compared the RAW query to the raw number, so typing back the `777-777` those very rows DISPLAY matched nothing; (3) NO DIACRITIC FOLDING anywhere, so "jose" missed "José"; (4) EACH SURFACE SEARCHED A DIFFERENT NAME — Contacts the frozen saved one, History the live one — so somebody saved as "Dad" was findable in Contacts and not in History, and their real name vice versa. **AND THE ONE NOBODY WOULD HAVE GUESSED, found by an adversarial review of the diagnosis: A MATCH INSIDE A COLLAPSED SECTION WAS FILTERED IN, COUNTED IN THE HEADER, AND NEVER RENDERED** — all three list screens gate their bodies on collapse state and none opened on a query, so a search could put "1" beside a heading and draw no rows; the match was found and then hidden, which is as close to the literal complaint as it gets. **ONE MATCHER, FOUR CONSUMERS** (`client/src/app/searchMatch.ts`): every query token must match SOME field and different tokens may match DIFFERENT fields, so "khalifa 777" works; **THE FIELDS ARE COMPARED SEPARATELY, never pre-joined**, because History used to glue every field together and strip non-digits from the whole string, so a digit run SPANNING two fields matched. **INFIX IS DELIBERATELY KEPT, not narrowed to word-start**: the v2.99.93 suggestion list is word-start only and adopting that here would REGRESS the main lists (today "hammadi" finds "Alhammadi"), so loose is the safer direction against an under-matching complaint — and it does mean "ali" also matches "Khalifa", accepted out loud. **THE TEXT PRIMITIVES NOW EXIST IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE**, promoted out of `contactSuggest.ts` and re-exported, because two implementations of "fold this name" is how two screens come to disagree about one query. **A REAL OVER-MATCH CAUGHT BY THIS RELEASE'S OWN TEST**: the digit rule first pulled digits out of ANY token, so "7th" extracted "7" and matched every contact whose number contains a seven — a name search returning the whole list is worse than one returning nothing (the v2.99.80 trap), so it now requires a digit-SHAPED token. **A REDUNDANCY THE MUTATION RUN EXPOSED, and the fix was to DELETE code rather than add a test**: the first cut had TWO number mechanisms (a whole-query digit compare and a per-token one) and removing EITHER changed no behaviour because each covered the other — three survivors from one design flaw; two individually-removable mechanisms are not defence in depth but dead weight that reads as load-bearing, so the redundant branch is gone and the remaining one now bites. **HISTORY EXCLUDES THE VIEWER from the roster it searches** (your own name is on every conference row, so searching for yourself matched every call) and now also searches the SAVED contact name; the server sends a search-only `liveName` on `contacts.list` from identities it was already fetching, while the row still DISPLAYS the name you chose. `client/src/app/searchMatch.test.ts` (30), tested BEHAVIOURALLY against the owner's own cases because a source pin cannot tell you whether "khalifa ali" finds Khalifa Mohamed Ali; **all 23 tripwires verified by MUTATION**. **THREE PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN TO THE PROPERTY**: `searchEnhancements.test.ts` froze the exact `.toLowerCase().includes(q)` expression and the `searchTextOf` joined haystack — so frozen, it asserted the defect. **NOT DONE, said plainly**: History filters over a TRUNCATED window (both call payloads are capped at 100 rows server-side), so an older call cannot be found however good the matcher is — that is a paging change, flagged rather than quietly bundled; and message search is still scoped to one already-open conversation. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 2815 tests.) Still, this glitch is happening with several users."*). **THE SCREENSHOT CONTAINED THE PROOF, and it is none of the three things this was assumed to be**: the one History row with a green LED reads **Incoming** and the two grey ones read **Outgoing**, and that pairing is the whole diagnosis. **ROOT CAUSE** — there is exactly ONE shared `conference_history` row per room and the CALLER seeds `dialedNumber` with the number they dialled, so on the RECIPIENT'S screen that field holds the RECIPIENT'S OWN number; the row's LED was keyed on `dialedNumber` FIRST with the peer only as a fallback, so an answered incoming call asked `presenceMany` for the viewer's own presence — online by definition while looking at your own call log — and painted it on the caller's avatar. Permanently green, per-row rather than per-person, affecting everyone who ever called the owner and was answered; Contacts, keyed on the real identity, was right all along, and OUTGOING rows were right too, which is exactly why this stayed invisible. **A SECOND SYMPTOM FROM THE SAME EXPRESSION**: `callBack` used the same key, so Message/Video/Call on an answered incoming row dialled the VIEWER — refused by signaling as `error{self}`, i.e. a button that silently does nothing. **THE RULE NOW LIVES IN ONE PURE FUNCTION** (`conferenceRowKeys`) that each row calls to derive its OWN key rather than the call site guessing which of a row's numbers it is about — that guess WAS the bug, so removing the guess is the fix; exported so the rule could be tested against a row shaped exactly like the owner's screenshot, and so the coming per-peer grouping keys on the same thing instead of re-deriving it. **A PARTY LINE IS THE ONE PLACE `dialedNumber` IS RIGHT** (there it is the LINE, not a person, and redialling it rejoins the room without ringing anybody — v2.89), so the exception is explicit and tested. **THE VIEWER'S OWN NUMBER IS NO LONGER IN THE PRESENCE BATCH AT ALL**, belt-and-braces: no History row should ever need it, and a self entry also made the busy set probe `directory.liveRoom` for our own number; `dialedNumber` is gone from the batch too (outgoing already had it via the roster, incoming was the self entry). **A GROUP ROW NOW DRAWS NO LED** — the disc is a generic `Users` glyph standing for N people, and N people do not have one presence, so an arbitrary member's is a guess presented as fact and grey is equally wrong. **THE SECOND, INDEPENDENT DIVERGENCE IS CLOSED AT THE FUNNEL**: `presenceMany` has carried `idle` since v2.99.92 and History threw it away, so a BACKGROUNDED person read full-strength green here while Contacts said "away"; History's `PresenceLed` and the group-call picker's dot were the last two inline copies of the colour rule (4 of 6 sites shared it) and both now defer to `presenceDot`, with a standing guard failing if any of them branches on `isOnline` for a colour again — v2.99.77 was precisely that bug. **THE STORY THAT WOULD NOT DELETE — a real, previously-undocumented defect found while investigating**: v2.99.86 started routing "See my status" through `openPeerStatus(me.number)`, which fires into `PeerOverlaysHost`; The feed and whoami are cached separately so their idea of your number can disagree for seconds, and a renumber opens exactly that window; `isMe` is now derived. **SAID PLAINLY ABOUT THE OWNER'S PARTICULAR ROW: IT REMOVED ITSELF** — `statuses.expiresAt` is notNull and always `now + 24h`, an identity-agnostic reaper runs every 10 minutes, and theirs showed "16h ago", so no story can persist beyond a day and there was never a stuck row to delete; an earlier draft claimed `deleteStatus` could report success while the row survived and **that was wrong and is recorded as such** (its SELECT and DELETE carry identical predicates and the DELETE is not catch-wrapped, so a failure throws rather than lying). Their screenshot also predates v2.99.87 — the older top bar, signed in as 235-680 rather than 777777. **A WEAKNESS OF MY OWN CAUGHT BY THE MUTATION RUN, TWICE, both the same class** — pinning a rule's DECLARATION instead of its USE: the LED test asserted `presenceDot` was called and the old classes were gone, so a mutation that called the rule for its label and painted a hand-rolled colour anyway stayed GREEN; and the lookup test used a bare `toMatch` for `presenceOf={presenceOf}`, which ONE of the two row kinds satisfied while the other had been cut off from presence entirely. it rides a WRAPPER because two animations on ONE element do not compose, the later declaration simply winning (v2.99.85), so scale and opacity must live on different elements or one silently stops. **"EVERY 30 SECONDS" COSTS NO TIMER**: both wordmark animations run a 30s cycle whose visible portion is only its opening fraction — measured in motion for 4.7% and 7.2% of it, ~1.4s and ~2.2s of movement then ~28s of rest — with nothing to arm or leak, inside the existing reduced-motion gate; the v2.99.86 sheen is RETIMED from 5.5s rather than joined by a second animation, because keeping both cadences would have buried the slower event under the faster one, and its pin (which froze the 5.5s duration and the 38% hold) is rewritten to the PROPERTY. **THE CONNECTION LINE REPORTS THIS DEVICE'S OWN REALTIME HEALTH, and that is the whole design** — reading my own presence row back from the server cannot work for the one case the line exists for, since if the connection just died the round trip that would tell you so is the thing that fails. **THE MIDDLE STATE NEEDS POSITIVE EVIDENCE**: `isSseConnected()` starts false and flips only on `onopen`, so "not connected ⇒ idle" would paint amber for the first few hundred ms of EVERY load and then snap to green — a flicker that reads as a bug — so a SECOND flag starts FALSE and is set only when the stream actually fails, both written from the SAME two handlers so there is one owner of the truth and no chance of the pair drifting (v2.99.50, v2.99.71). **GREEN IS NEVER A LIE**, which is why the stream is consulted at all: `navigator.onLine` only reports that an interface is up, so a captive portal still reads true and would paint "online" over a connection carrying nothing. **NO NETWORK OUTRANKS A DEGRADED STREAM**, because a dropped stream is a SYMPTOM of no network and reporting the symptom sends somebody looking in the wrong place. **"IDLE" IS THE HONEST WORD**: a backgrounded tab is precisely a tab whose EventSource the browser throttles, the same condition the server records as `presence.idle` (v2.99.92) — said plainly, you cannot watch your own idle label while the app is hidden; new `--relay-amber-text` (5.16:1 / 9.91:1) and `--relay-red-text` (5.61:1 / 5.96:1), both within a hair of the green text's 5.91:1. the safe-area inset itself STAYS, since on an iPhone the home indicator sits exactly there. **ONE `<BrandMark>` INSTEAD OF TWO** (the wordmark's 390px rule moved inside the component; two mounts meant two subscriptions to the connection store and the breakpoint restated twice), with the pin that froze the two call sites rewritten to the property. **A HARNESS BUG OF MY OWN, reported rather than counted**: the first geometry run reported 25/25 FAILING and I was one step from "the layout is broken" — `find(f => f.endsWith(".css"))` had picked **`Docs-*.css`** (29KB of markdown styles) instead of `index-*.css` (602KB), so it measured a page with no Tailwind at all and the 4px "gap" was inline-block whitespace between two un-flexed buttons; the harness now names the app stylesheet AND **aborts** unless it can prove the CSS is in force (header computes to `display:flex`, bell exactly 36px, phone media query agrees with the emulated width) — the gate v2.99.84 added after measuring a phone at desktop width. **THREE OF MY OWN TEST BUGS, all fixed before shipping**: the recurring UNBOUNDED-SLICE fragility (a percentage assertion sliced from a keyframe's start to the end of the file and read `relayHueB`'s 94% while claiming to check `relaySheen` — now BRACE-MATCHED to exactly one block); a needle (`RELAY</span>`) the multiline JSX does not contain; and **the prose trap for the EIGHTH time** — `not.toMatch(/fixed/)` matched the comment saying the bar is NOT `position: fixed`, which the line-based `codeOnly` cannot catch because a JSX `{/* … */}` block's continuation lines begin with ordinary words, so this file's version strips the block forms as SPANS and the assertion is scoped to the element's own `className`. **A WEAKNESS THE MUTATION RUN FOUND IN A PIN I HAD JUST WRITTEN**: "the bell comes before the avatar" asserted DOM order only, and a `flex-row-reverse` paints them the other way round while leaving the source order untouched. `client/src/app/topBarStatus.test.ts` (42), the three-way rule tested BEHAVIOURALLY because a source pin cannot tell you whether losing the network turns the line red; **all 37 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups and a confirmed-GREEN baseline. **NOT VERIFIED ON A DEVICE, said plainly**: geometry and animation cost are measured headless against the real built stylesheet, but how the pulse and the 30-second flourish LOOK on the owner's phone is not. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 2765 tests.) (v2.99.93 — **THE PENDING-TASK BATCH: FIND A CONTACT BY DIGIT *OR* LETTER, ICONS ON THE PROFILE ROWS, AND AN HONEST GUEST NOTICE** — three items closed and the rest of the list triaged out loud rather than left ambiguous. **#91**: the New-conversation field ran `replace(/\D/g, "")` on the way in, so **a name could not be typed at all** and you had to know the six digits by heart; both fields (DM and group member) now take a query and a suggestion list resolves it. **TWO RULES, PICKED BY WHAT WAS TYPED**: digits match the START of the number — never an infix, since a 6-digit number has no meaningful interior and `55` matching 155234 would put a stranger above the person being dialled — while letters match the start of ANY WORD, so a SURNAME works (people search "Alhammadi" as readily as "Khalifa"), with a first-name match outranking a surname one. **NEVER AN INFIX ON A SHORT QUERY**, because one or two letters inside a word matches most of a contact list and is indistinguishable from no filter (the v2.99.80 emoji lesson); case and diacritics fold, so "alv" finds "Ålvaro". **THE SUBMIT PATH STILL ONLY EVER SEES SIX DIGITS, and `digitsOf` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH**: stripping non-digits reads `7a7b7c7d7e7f` as `777777`, so a typo would open somebody else's thread — the button is gated on the digit count AND on the query being number-SHAPED (the v2.99.75 `normalizeDesiredNumber` reasoning), and `isNumberQuery` requires the WHOLE query to be digits and grouping so "7th floor" is a name search, while accepting the `777-777` grouping the app itself displays. **A CONTACT YOU BLOCKED IS NEVER SUGGESTED** (offering to message somebody you deliberately blocked is a mis-suggestion; unblocking is a decision to make in Contacts, on purpose), a malformed stored number is skipped rather than offered-then-refused, and the group list withholds members already added because a suggestion that does nothing when tapped reads as broken. An empty field shows favourites then whoever is online; an empty RESULT renders NOTHING rather than a "no matches" row, since the field still works by number; the contact list is fetched only while the sheet is open; and the suggestion's number is `dir="ltr"` + bidi-ISOLATED (v2.99.77). **#90 (icons)**: a mail glyph on Email, a phone on Mobile numbers, and a PER-PLATFORM glyph on each social link — **the labels STAY**, because four platforms is where icon-only becomes a guessing game and an icon alone gives a screen reader nothing, with every glyph `aria-hidden` so it is not announced twice; `SocialIcon` has an exhaustive switch with a NEUTRAL FALLBACK, so a fifth platform added without an icon degrades to a link glyph rather than rendering nothing. **#90 (notice)**: how long a guest number is held, read from the server's own `guestExpiresAt` rather than a day count written into the copy so the two cannot drift, and it says out loud that **the clock RESETS every time you open RELAY** — true (`touchGuestExpiry` pushes it forward on every visit) and the part that makes the figure non-frightening, since a bare "expires in N days" implies a countdown you cannot stop. **AND IT NEVER CLAIMS THE DATA IS DELETED, because nothing deletes it** — established by reading the code: `guestExpiresAt` gates only the guest COOKIE lookup and NO reaper touches guest identity rows, the only `.delete(identities)` being Adopt-and-Retire's provably-empty retire, so after expiry the number, contacts and messages are still there and this browser can reclaim them with the recovery key (v2.99.68). `client/src/app/contactSuggest.test.ts` (36), the ranking tested BEHAVIOURALLY because a source pin cannot tell you whether typing `7` surfaces 777777; **all 28 tripwires verified by MUTATION**. **A WEAKNESS OF MY OWN CAUGHT BY THAT RUN**: the first-name-outranks-surname case used "Zain Ali"/"Ali Hassan", where the ALPHABETICAL tiebreak happens to give the same order, so deleting the rank comparison left it green; rewritten with "Ahmed Ali"/"Ali Hassan", where the rank-1 match sorts alphabetically FIRST so only the rank term can produce the expected order. **#96 RESOLVED WITHOUT BUILDING IT, reasoning recorded rather than the task quietly dropped**: the ring already covers every surface the owner named that exists (Contacts, thread rows, chat header, History, via `PeerAvatar`); call tiles were NOT in that list, and a ring there costs paint on the app's most expensive surface — six tiles of live video, where v2.99.84 measured 14 repaints out — for an indicator that cannot safely be tapped, since opening a full-screen story over a live call is not a thing to offer; GROUP rows are the real gap and are blocked on #89, because a group has no avatar or status yet for a ring to mean anything. **#75 RE-AUDITED AND HANDED BACK WITH EVIDENCE**: the MIME is clean line by line (`Date`, `Message-ID` on the From domain, `MIME-Version`, multipart/alternative with BOTH parts, RFC 2047 subject encoding), so spam placement is SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment and domain reputation — DNS and SES, owner-side; deliberately NOT shipped were speculative header tweaks dressed up as a fix (`Precedence: bulk` would actively HURT a transactional message, and a `List-Unsubscribe` on somebody's own login code is wrong). **#44 STILL BLOCKED**: live verification needs to reach `your-chat.io` and this sandbox's outbound network refuses it (`curl` exits 56). No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 2724 tests.) (v2.99.92 — **MINIMISING THE APP IS IDLE, NOT OFFLINE** (owner: *"Whenever you minimize the app, the user showing offline, not the idle."*). `PresenceManager` fired the go-offline BEACON on `visibilitychange → hidden` as well as `pagehide`, so switching apps for five seconds told every contact you had left; now hidden → idle (a slow 60s beat), visible → the ordinary heartbeat which clears idle in the same write, pagehide/beforeunload → the beacon as before. **THE HARD PART WAS NOT THE THIRD STATE — IT IS THAT `isOnline` ANSWERED TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS**: "what LED do I draw" and "should I push, because they cannot see this in the open app" were the same boolean, so keeping `isOnline` true while backgrounded would have **SILENTLY STOPPED NOTIFYING A MINIMISED APP** — making the complaint worse in a way nothing on screen would show. New shared `presenceNeedsNotification` (`!isOnline || idle`) is used at every site asking the second question, FAILS TOWARD telling somebody (unknown identity ⇒ notify, because failing the other way loses the message rather than a moment's quiet), and a test ENUMERATES the sites so a fourth has to come through it. **THE AUTO-REPLY DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE IT**: it posts a line in somebody else's name saying they are away and will reply later, and somebody who switched apps for ten seconds may reply immediately — firing it on idle would make the auto-reply a lie, the same over-reaction in message form; pinned as a deliberate exception. **ONE NEW NULLABLE COLUMN, `presence.idleSince`, and NULL is exactly the reading every existing row needs**, so the additive migration is a no-op until a client reports idle; a TIMESTAMP rather than a flag because the offline-message email asks "have they really been away a while" and `lastSeenAt` can no longer answer that — a backgrounded app keeps beating, which is precisely what stops it decaying to offline in two minutes, so `awayForMs` measures from `idleSince` while idle. **`markIdle` KEEPS `isOnline` TRUE and that is the truth, not a convenience** (the SSE stream is open and a call still rings); it records the FIRST idle moment via `COALESCE`, since a bare `now` would reset the clock every beat; `markOnline`, `markOffline` and the reaper all CLEAR it, because an offline row carrying an idle timestamp is a contradiction — harmless today and a trap the moment anyone reads the column alone. **IT IS A SEPARATE ENDPOINT FROM `heartbeat`, NOT A FLAG ON IT**: `heartbeat` calls `markOnline`, which clears idle AND can fire the "back online" watcher push, so an idle beat built on it would have reintroduced the v2.99.25/H6 bug; it also fans NO presence SSE event, since `isOnline` has not changed (publishing `true` again is a no-op costing an audience query per app switch, and `false` would be the bug). **`idle` IS DERIVED IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE** — every router presence read already funnelled through `getPresenceForIds`, so the rule there reaches all of them and no consumer sees the raw pair to combine wrongly; guest-privacy suppression covers idle too. **IT MAPS ONTO THE `away` THE APP ALREADY HAS** rather than inventing a display state, a MANUAL override still wins (somebody who set travelling said so on purpose), and `idle` DEFAULTS TO FALSE so an untaught caller degrades to online rather than to the wrong-way failure of showing somebody offline. **AN AUTOMATIC IDLE IS NOT LABELLED AS A CHOSEN STATUS** — the dialer's chip now reads the OVERRIDE directly, because both resolve to `away` and reading the chip off the resolution would put a label in somebody's mouth they never selected. **ONE LED RULE FOR EVERY DOT** (new `client/src/app/presenceDot.ts`): eight dots across four screens had to learn the third state, and eight copies is how two surfaces end up disagreeing about one person (v2.99.77 was that bug); the colour vocabulary is NOT widened — idle is the online green FADED with no glow, not a new hue, since amber already means "on a call" and "Do Not Disturb" and a third meaning would make colour stop carrying information. `onLeave`'s dead branch DELETED (its one false caller now marks idle). **THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN**: on mobile Safari a real tab CLOSE often fires only `visibilitychange`, so such a close now reads "away" for up to two minutes — the trade against a wrong "offline" every time somebody checks another app; the reaper converges it, and "online now" on the landing page becomes MORE stable since minimising no longer decrements it. `server/presenceIdle.test.ts` (30), the rule / `effectiveStatus` / the LED tested BEHAVIOURALLY because a source pin cannot tell you whether a backgrounded app still gets its push; **all 28 tripwires verified by MUTATION**. **TWO WEAKNESSES OF MY OWN CAUGHT BY THAT RUN**, same class: the markIdle assertions matched `isOnline: true` / `lastSeenAt: now` ANYWHERE, and since it is an upsert each occurs twice — so breaking the UPDATE path (the half that keeps a minimised app out of the reaper's way) left the test green; now COUNTED, insert and update asserted separately. **A BAD MUTATION OF MY OWN, reported rather than hidden**: the markOnline case inserted a COMMENT line, changing no behaviour. **NINE PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN**, six for the SAME structural reason rather than a changed property — `ownerUiBatch2`, `qaBatch3`, `qaBatch10` (×2), `statsFeed` and `presenceReaper` each sliced a FIXED character count from an anchor and this release's comments pushed the code out of the window (the recurring v2.99.78 fragility), all now bounded by the function's own end; the rest were real intent changes (`statusReply`/`roundsGaps`/`emailNotifyPrefs` pinned the bare `!isOnline` check, i.e. they would have pinned the silent regression; the Contacts/Messages LED pins froze inline ternaries that moved into the shared helper). **AND THE PROSE TRAP FOR THE SEVENTH TIME**: a `not.toMatch(/onLeave\(/)` matched MY OWN COMMENT explaining that call's removal. **NOT VERIFIED ON A DEVICE, said plainly**: the state machine is tested, but nobody has watched a real phone minimise and seen a contact's dot fade — and the client half rests on `visibilitychange` firing as specified, which is exactly where mobile Safari is inconsistent. One additive nullable column, no new dependency, no new env var. 2688 tests.) (v2.99.91 — **WHY A NOTIFICATION DID NOT ARRIVE** (owner: *"Can you check the Firebase configuration as still the notification for the front mobile apps for Android? It's not showing or it's not active."*). **A NATIVE PUSH CROSSES FIVE LINKS AND EVERY ONE FAILS THE SAME WAY FROM THE PHONE — nothing happens**: the shell posts a token into the WebView, `push.subscribe` stores it under a routable kind, the transport is configured on the fleet, the recipient has not turned push off, and something actually SENDS for the event being tested. The admin panel now reports them SEPARATELY and can fire a real send, so the owner can run it against production in ten seconds. **THE ANSWER AVAILABLE WITHOUT THE FLEET, and the most likely explanation: NO CODE PATH SENDS A PUSH FOR AN INCOMING CALL** — `kind:"incoming-call"` was removed in v2.99.11 at the owner's own explicit request and nothing has sent it since (re-verified by scanning every `sendPushToIdentity` site), so "call the closed app" can never ring however Firebase is configured; what DOES push is a message, a missed call, a voicemail and a back-online alert, and a test **cross-checks that claimed list against the kinds the code really passes**, because a hard-coded list that drifts is worse than none — it sends somebody looking in the wrong place. **THE SERVER CHAIN WAS AUDITED RATHER THAN ASSUMED and is COMPLETE**: the fan-out covers Expo / raw device token / Web Push, the shape decides the transport, `push.subscribe` refuses an unclassifiable token, and the WebView bridge is mounted for every signed-in session — what cannot be checked from here is the EXTERNAL Expo app, which must post the exact `{type:"SET_PUSH_TOKEN", token}` envelope (a bare token is refused by design, since a listener that registers whatever arrives is a hijack primitive — the v2.99.49 R1 class). **`admin.pushDiagnostics` IS READ-ONLY AND NEVER RETURNS A TOKEN**: an FCM token plus the project key, or an Expo token alone, can push to that handset, so a device is kind + length + a 12-char prefix — enough to tell two devices apart, not enough to address either; the Firebase key is reported as *whether it parses*, and tests forbid every leaking shape. **IT REPORTS THE STORED KIND *AND* THE SHAPE-DERIVED KIND, which is the whole point**: the sender routes by the STORED kind, so an Expo token filed as `fcm` goes to FCM and is dropped with NO error anywhere — the one failure in the chain with no other symptom, invisible unless both are printed together; a legacy NULL kind reads as `webpush`, the same reading the sender takes, because calling it "unknown" would invent a problem. **A DB FAILURE AND AN EMPTY LIST ARE REPORTED DIFFERENTLY** — "no devices" and "we couldn't look" need different next steps. **`admin.sendTestPush` GOES THROUGH THE REAL `sendPushToIdentity`** — a parallel test sender is the worst possible thing to build here, since it could pass while production was broken; tests forbid bypassing via `sendFcmData`/`sendExpoPush`/`webpush.sendNotification`. It is `directoryGate`-limited EVEN FOR AN ADMIN (it writes to a third party's device), the body is content-free and says it is a test, the trace carries ids only, and a delivered count of ZERO reads as "nothing was reachable" rather than a generic error. **THE PANEL DID NOT QUIETLY WIDEN**: a test enumerates every `trpc.admin.*` call the page makes and asserts the exact set, so a sixth capability must be a deliberate act; both procedures re-derive admin from the `users` row with the gate asserted to precede every read and write, refusing uniformly so the endpoint is no oracle. `server/pushDoctor.test.ts` (21), `classifyNativeToken` tested BEHAVIOURALLY; **all 19 tripwires verified by MUTATION**. **NOT VERIFIED FROM HERE, said plainly**: the sandbox cannot reach `your-chat.io` (`curl` exits 56), so the live `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` was not read and no live push was sent — which is exactly why this ships as a panel the owner runs against production rather than a claim about it. **STILL OPEN, the other half of the owner's message**: minimising marks the person OFFLINE rather than idle — diagnosed (`PresenceManager` beacons offline on `visibilitychange → hidden`) and shipping next; the fix needs a third presence state plus care at the three sites where `isOnline` decides whether to PUSH rather than what LED to draw, since a backgrounded app must keep getting notifications. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 2658 tests.) the timer is armed on `idxs.length` NOT the array, since depending on the array re-arms the interval every render and the walk would never advance. **EACH TYPER GETS THEIR OWN COLOUR AND TWO ARE STAGGERED**, so "two three people typing" reads as two names rather than one blinking blur; (v2.99.84 — **THE CONFERENCE STOPS COOKING THE PHONE, AND THE VOICE SURVIVES IT** (owner: *"my phone become verry hot whenever we have conference call multiple parties. I think because of the video or because of what? Make sure that the length of the sound to be very clear and good latency for both video and voice."*). **THE TRANSPORT DECIDES THE ANSWER AND IT IS THE MESH — established, not assumed**: LiveKit needs three env vars an operator sets and appears nowhere in this repo but as a commented-out optional in the deploy doc, so the fleet runs the WebRTC mesh, where every phone in an N-party call runs **N-1 independent video encoders and N-1 decoders** — five of each at the 6-cap, on a handset. That is the heat, and it is structural rather than a bug. **THE CANVAS PIPELINE WAS RULED OUT BY READING IT** rather than trusting its comment: both `ensurePipeline` call sites are gated on `activeFilter !== "none"`, so a 30fps main-thread canvas paint is NOT part of the default cost (it was the first suspect, so it is named). **FRAME RATE WAS NEVER CAPPED — the largest CPU lever left**: bitrate and resolution have scaled with party size since v2.80, framerate did not, so five encoders ran at the camera's native 30 and did roughly twice the work of five at 15; the new ladder is **30 / 24 / 15** at 1 / ≤3 / >3 peers, and 1:1 is unchanged in effect while being a REAL value rather than an absent field, because the party can SHRINK 6 → 2 and an undefined cap is not reliably cleared by every engine. **`degradationPreference:"balanced"` GOES IN ITS OWN `setParameters` CALL AND THE SEPARATION IS THE POINT** — it is a TOP-LEVEL field some engines reject outright, and a rejected `setParameters` discards the ENTIRE object, so folding it in would silently lose the bitrate AND framerate caps on exactly the browsers that most need them; "balanced" rather than the common maintain-framerate default, which keeps frames and sheds nothing else — precisely wrong on a thermally throttled phone. **THE AUDIO ASK IS ANSWERED BY THE VIDEO FIX, said out loud rather than met with a separate knob**: a throttled phone starves its AUDIO encoder too, heard as choppy, unclear sound, so capping video is what protects voice — there is no clarity setting that survives a hot CPU. **AUDIO IS PROTECTED, NEVER CAPPED**: marked `priority`/`networkPriority` high so the engine sheds VIDEO and keeps the voice, with deliberately NO audio bitrate cap (a rounding error beside video, and capping it is the opposite of the ask) and a missing `encodings` array left ALONE rather than fabricated — for video an empty array is filled in because the cap is the point, but inventing an encoding purely to stamp a priority risks disturbing a working track for no gain; its branch `return`s so it can never fall into the video path. **THE MICROPHONE IS MONO** (`channelCount:{ideal:1}`) — a voice call carries no spatial information, so stereo doubles the encoder's sample work for nothing on the very path where N-1 encoders are the problem; **`ideal`, not `exact`**, because `exact` throws `OverconstrainedError` on a stereo-only device and would cost that person their microphone. **THE GRID WAS REPAINTING ITSELF 14 TIMES A FRAME OVER LIVE VIDEO**: `relayWave` animated **height** (five bars per speaking tile), `relaySpeakPulse` animated the tile's own **box-shadow** (a full-tile repaint) and `relayAvBreath` a colour-cycling box-shadow — and a tile's backdrop is live video, so nothing can ever be cached (the class v2.99.70 measured). Wave → `transform:scaleY`; pulse → a `.spk-glow` overlay carrying the glow as a STATIC box-shadow with only its OPACITY animated (identical look, static markup, still driven by `.speaking` alone so no JS toggles it); the avatar breath keeps its colour cycle on DESKTOP, where a GPU handles it free, and runs a transform-only `relayAvBreathLite` on phones. **THIRTY-SIX BLUR LAYERS OVER LIVE VIDEO, and the existing cap covered NONE of them** — it named exactly two elements (`.ctrl-bar`, `.filter-dock`) while every TILE carries six blurred chips, so at the 6-cap a phone composited 36 `backdrop-filter` layers each re-blurred EVERY frame; suppressed on phones with the backgrounds taken opaque in the same breath, desktop keeps the glass. **THE OVERRIDE'S POSITION IS LOAD-BEARING and the measurement is what proved it**: equal-specificity overrides are decided by ORDER and four of the six base rules are declared LATE, so in its natural home the rule measured as doing **nothing at all** (36 layers before AND after) while reading as correct — it now sits last, with a test that fails if any of those six base rules moves after it. **MEASURED, not asserted**: headless Chromium against the real stylesheet, six tiles two speaking, emulated 390px phone — repainting animations **14 → 0** (compositor-only 0 → 14), blur layers over live video **36 → 0**, no horizontal overflow; re-measured at 1440 desktop and deliberately UNCHANGED at 36 with the colour cycle intact, so the trade is confined to phones. **A HARNESS BUG OF MY OWN, reported rather than counted as a result**: the first run showed 36 → 36 and I nearly recorded the override as ineffective for the wrong reason — `page.setContent` without a `<meta viewport>` leaves the emulated page on the **980px default layout viewport**, so every max-width query silently fails to match (`innerWidth` was 980, not 390); the harness now emits that meta AND **aborts** if the phone query does not match, so it can never again report a phone measurement taken at desktop width. The cascade bug was real and separate — it only became visible once the harness was honest. **THREE MISTAKES OF MY OWN IN THE TESTS, all found by the mutation run and all fixed rather than counted as passes.** Two were the recurring shape of pinning the DECLARATION instead of the USE: one asserted the bitrate LADDER existed while deleting the line that APPLIES it stayed green, and the other COUNTED `setParameters` calls, which says nothing about which OBJECT carries `degradationPreference` — the one property that matters. The third is worse and is recorded plainly: my replacement counted the bare identifier, which also matches the COMMENT above it and the type annotation, so it read 3 and **the test was RED** — and an already-red test fails for every mutation, making that mutation's "bit" a **false positive**. It now counts ASSIGNMENTS with comments stripped, and the whole sweep was re-run from a confirmed-GREEN baseline so no result rests on a test that was failing anyway. `client/src/lib/conferenceCost.test.ts` (19); all 20 tripwires verified by MUTATION from a green baseline. **NOT MEASURED, said plainly: no encoder change was tested on a real phone in a real 6-party call** — there is no handset here, so the framerate, priority and mono changes rest on how WebRTC is specified to behave, not on a thermal reading; the CSS half IS measured, and the ladder is one line to retune if the video reads softer than the owner wants. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, no server change. 2500 tests.) I think there is a glitch or, you know, not for this user. Check it generic."* The dialer said **"Mohamed Idris · Registered · online now"**; the call answered **"Mohamed Idris is offline right now."*** **ROOT CAUSE — RELAY NAMES A PERSON TWICE AND ONLY ONE OF THE TWO MOVED**: presence is a DB row keyed on `identityId`, while the signaling registry — the thing that actually ROUTES a call — is in memory and keyed on the **6-digit PIN**. `regenerateIdentityNumber` moved the database and every stored copy inside one transaction and touched the registry **NOT AT ALL**, so a person signed in when their number changed stayed registered under their OLD pin: unreachable at the number they now own, still occupying one that no longer exists. This is the v2.99.54 identity-continuity story with the one layer missing that is not in the database. **THREE MORE OWNER-REPORTED SYMPTOMS WERE THE SAME BUG**, said plainly rather than chased separately: the in-call **"Add to contacts" pill reappearing for somebody already SAVED** (the roster names the old pin while `contacts.number` was rewritten, so the saved-set lookup misses) and **Contacts showing them plain "online" instead of "on a call"** (`pinsInCall` reports the old pin) — the owner reached that diagnosis themselves (*"I think this glitch ... is because they changed their number"*) and was right. **A HOOK, NOT A SECOND WRITER**: `identities.number` has exactly ONE writer and a test pins it, because propagation is the whole difficulty of renumbering and a parallel implementation is precisely how History’s copies came to rot before v2.99.54 — so `setNumberChangeHook` fires from INSIDE that writer at the commit point (immediately after `confirmNumberReservation`), a hook rather than a direct call because `v2db → relay` would close the cycle `v2db → relay → _core/context → v2db` (`setPresenceChangeHook` is the precedent). **`rebindRegisteredPin` MOVES TWELVE PLACES IN ONE SYNCHRONOUS PASS, and the synchrony is the design**: the registry is plain Maps dispatched from one event loop, so a function with no `await` cannot be observed half-done — and a HALF-renamed registry is worse than a stale one, since the person would be in a room under one pin and addressed under another. **`cidToPin` IS SEVERED FIRST, the single most dangerous omission in the whole rename**: that reverse index BEATS the client’s requested pin in the register handler, so until it moves a concurrent re-register is misclassified as an **identity switch** — whose body deliberately DESTROYS the live call (it exists to stop a cross-user hijack on a shared browser) — meaning a late move would let a routine SSE reconnect drop the very call this saves. **THE OLD NUMBER IS RETIRED, NEVER ALIASED**: an alias would re-create two addresses for one person (the split being removed) and would silently bypass the block-follows-you property, since `contacts.number` moved in the same transaction; nobody is put at risk, because the reservation ledger is MONOTONIC so the old number never reaches a stranger. **A VERIFIED HOLDER OF THE NEW PIN IS NEVER EVICTED** — an unverified `genPin` squatter is (such a registration is already un-ringable via `pinIsAddressable`), but evicting a verified holder would be the v2.98.4/F1 seizure class in reverse, so the rebind REFUSES and the client self-heal converges it. **`verifiedPin` IS SET EXPLICITLY**, because left false the person is un-ringable and un-rejoinable — an "offline" INDISTINGUISHABLE from the bug being fixed. **THE CLIENT IS TOLD, NOT MADE TO RE-REGISTER** (that is read as an identity switch and drops the call): `registered` is re-sent with a new `renumbered: true`, and the client’s existing handler already adopts and persists it, so an older client needs no change. **THE NEW `number` SSE EVENT IS DECLARED IN BOTH PLACES, which is not bookkeeping**: `KNOWN_V2_EVENT_KINDS` gates the RECEIVE side of the Redis bus, so an undeclared kind is delivered locally and **silently DROPPED whenever the recipient is on the other instance** — most of the time on a two-instance fleet, and single-instance dev would have looked perfect (the v2.99.74 `delivered` bug, avoided by having been bitten once). **A CLIENT-SIDE SELF-HEAL, because one real path fires no hook at all**: `scripts/admin-tool.mjs` runs as bare `node` on EC2 and writes straight to MySQL — it CANNOT import the TypeScript writer, so no hook fires and no event is sent; `useIdentity` now sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, the only backstop covering that path, and the script says so in its header and prints it after an apply. Clustered mode forwards a `__renumber` frame to the leader rather than mutating a registry it does not own. **A REAL BUG IN MY OWN CODE, CAUGHT BY THIS RELEASE’S OWN TEST**: step 11 called `socket.send(JSON.stringify(…))`, but `RelaySocket.send` takes an OBJECT — the transport serializes — so a pre-stringified frame arrives as a JSON *string* with no `.type` and the client’s dispatcher silently drops it; the whole step would have been a no-op that reads as working. **THE CATCH IS DESTRUCTIVE-BUT-SAFE ON PURPOSE**: the hook swallows throws (the renumber is already committed and must never report failure), so a throw here would be INVISIBLE — a failure therefore retires the old registration, ending the live call, because a dropped call is recoverable while a split identity is the bug being fixed. `server/renumberRebind.test.ts` (26) is **behavioural against the REAL registry** — a source pin cannot tell you whether a call connects after a rename and that is the entire feature; **all 18 tripwires verified by MUTATION** from byte-exact backups. **THREE HARNESS BUGS OF MY OWN, fixed rather than reported as results**: `reg.connections` is seeded by the HTTP layer and not by `handleMessage`, so a correct rebind read as broken (the harness now mirrors `attachRelay`’s STABLE connection object — load-bearing, since a snapshotted pin would report success while the next message still carried the old number); a bare `{type:"accept"}` cannot be authorized (it must name the room the ring carried — v2.99.43/M45), so every accept was silently doing nothing; and `pinsInCall` reads a module global and takes a pin LIST, so it is now driven through `_setActiveRegistryForTests` with an `afterEach` so it cannot leak. **ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS VACUOUS AND THE MUTATION RUN CAUGHT IT** — the `verifiedPin` test re-read the value after a rebind, but this harness registers over the non-HTTP path where `verifiedClaim` is true by construction, so it passed whether the assignment existed or not; it now forces `false` first and asserts the CONSEQUENCE, and it is recorded honestly that an unverified record is not reachable through the front door today (an unverified registration gets a random `genPin` unrelated to its identity, which no renumber event can name), so that line guards an invariant rather than reproducing a live case. **A SILENT-SKIP TEST OF MY OWN REMOVED**: the held-room case had a conditional `return` when nothing was parked, so it could pass by doing nothing — worse than no test, because it reports safety. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var, and the no-op path (a renumber while signed out, the common case) resolves no residue and returns immediately. 2481 tests.) (v2.99.82 — **THE CALL TILE SAYS EACH THING ONCE, AND ADD-TO-CONTACTS HAS ONE HOME** (owner, asked TWICE — the second time with a screenshot circling all three renderings of one name on a single tile: *"you mentioned the name in two places ... You don't need to repeat the name. You need to put the profile picture or the avatar, and below it, you put add to contact if he was not in your contact. and at the bottom of the border of the frame of the user where you put the flag and you put his first name only, and beside, you put the PIN number, the six digits without mention PIN"*; recorded plainly, this was mapped rather than shipped on the first ask, which is why it needed a second). **THE NAME NOW APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE**: `.ph-name` is gone along with two CSS rules, one of which was ALREADY dead (nothing ever put a flag inside it). the first pass DID truncate "Mohamed" → "Moha…" in a 2-up, so gap/padding were tightened and re-measured. **ADD-TO-CONTACTS HAS ONE HOME** — the top-left `InCallSaveContacts` chip is UNMOUNTED, and nothing is lost while three things improve: it only ever offered the FIRST unsaved peer (a `roster.find`) where the pill is per-peer, it polled every 3s, and it derived a SECOND saved-set from `contacts.list` that could disagree with the engine's own. **ONE BUILDER FOR EVERY TILE**: `addSelfTile` hand-rolled the same DOM, which is exactly why it kept its duplicate name after the remote tiles lost theirs — it now calls the shared builder with no `pin` (no menu, no maximize, no Add, no digits) plus a new `avatarName` so the band reads "You" while the disc shows the person's own initials. `callTileIdentity.test.ts` (15); rewritten as a mutator asserting the target occurs exactly ONCE, after which both bit. **TWO PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN**: one asserted `.ph-name{` EXISTS, i.e. it pinned the very thing the owner asked to remove; the other asserted the top-left chip was MOUNTED. **A BUILD TRAP THAT HAS BITTEN TWICE NOW HAS A NAMED GUARD** — the call stylesheet is a template literal, so a backtick in a CSS COMMENT terminates it (v2.99.16, and twice while writing this release, surfacing as syntax errors 300 lines away): there is now an explicit assertion that `RELAY_CSS` contains no backtick. **STILL OPEN, the more serious half**: a renumbered person stays registered in the signaling layer under their OLD pin, so the dialer says "online now" while the call says "offline" — the root cause of the Add pill reappearing for a SAVED contact and of contacts showing "online" instead of "on a call". 2455 tests.) (v2.99.81 — **THE EIGHT-ITEM SECURITY BATCH, EACH FINDING RE-CONFIRMED BEFORE IT WAS TOUCHED.** All eight had been sitting in the v2.99.57 REMAINING list; each was handed to an independent SKEPTIC briefed to REFUTE it, defaulting to refuted, and required to produce a concrete exploit before it counted. Six CONFIRMED, two PARTIAL — and **two of the original claims were wrong in ways that would have made a naive fix harmful**: the OTP finding was in the WRONG FUNCTION (`mintOtp` not invalidating priors is harmless, because superseding only SHADOWS — a burned newest row falls back to the older un-consumed one, and every mint mails the valid code to the victim's OWN inbox — so "make mintOtp invalidate priors" would DELETE that self-healing fallback and make an attacker's burn PERMANENT; the real defect is that `verifyOtp` has no per-address budget), and F3 rewrites `firstName`/`lastName` rather than `displayName` (`ensureUserIdentity` returns a pre-existing row untouched — but first/last is what `directory.lookup` returns and what the landing dialer PREFERS, so it was visible to strangers anyway). **F1 — A BLOCKED PERSON COULD STILL POST BY REPLYING TO AN OLD NOTIFICATION EMAIL**: the inbound handler checked membership and From, then called `sendMessage` DIRECTLY, inheriting none of the router's block rule; the reply address carries NO EXPIRY so a months-old email stays a usable credential forever, and a blocked person can mint a fresh one by not answering a call (the missed-call gate checks the other direction). Fixed 1:1 only to match `messages.send` exactly, fails OPEN (a bare await would throw into the outer catch, which answers 200, and the provider does not retry — destroying a genuine reply), answers 200 not 503 (a 5xx redelivers the same mail forever), and deliberately NOT pushed into `sendMessage`, whose other callers include the offline auto-reply. **F2 — DRAINING SOMEBODY'S SIGN-IN CODES WAS UNBOUNDED**: five wrong guesses burn a code and repeating drains every outstanding row until the victim's real code reports "expired" — with four wrong PIN tries that is a full unauthenticated lockout, because the email code is the PIN's own unlock path. New per-address budget claimed BEFORE the row is read, sized 20/10min so a real correction cannot lock anybody out. **F3 — A REGISTER CODE COULD SKIP NEW-DEVICE APPROVAL AND RENAME YOU**: `verifyOtp` read `wasRegistration = !!(row.firstName || row.lastName)` and skipped approval whenever the row carried a name — and `NameSchema` makes a name MANDATORY on register, so EVERY register-minted row set it; an attacker who could read the code got an immediately-usable session and the victim's online device was never prompted. Inferring "first device" from an attacker-supplied field was the defect; the short-circuit is DELETED, since `shouldRequireApproval` already answers the real question and a genuine first registration still never waits. The name is written only when the account did not already exist, captured BEFORE `createOtpUser`. **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE**: `register` still accepts an existing address — refusing would mirror the legacy path but create an email-EXISTENCE ORACLE where none exists, and with approval enforced the hole is closed; the paths still disagree, defensibly (a password on an existing account is a pre-hijack vector, a code proves ownership). **F4 — SIGN-OUT LEFT THE PUSH SUBSCRIPTION BOUND**: sign-out rotated the device id, channel and recovery key and never touched `push_subscriptions`, so the browser kept receiving the signed-out person's notifications; `push.unsubscribe` already existed and nothing called it. Called BEFORE the server sign-out (the scoping needs the caller still to BE that identity), drops the browser-side subscription too, best-effort throughout, and still keeps the per-browser push CLAIM. **F5 — DND DID NOT APPLY TO "X IS BACK ONLINE"**: the service worker early-returned before reading the prefs for any kind outside message/missed-call/voicemail, so `contact-online` buzzed with DND on while the same alert IN-PAGE honoured it — and a list of covered kinds exempts every FUTURE kind by default. Inverted: a RING is exempt explicitly, DND applies to everything else, MUTE stays message-only. **F8 — A 100-NUMBER BATCH COST ONE TOKEN**: `presenceMany`/`presence` had an enumeration throttle 100x/200x weaker than `lookup`'s and both drop unknown entries, so each element is an existence probe — the whole 10^6 space mapped in ~2.8 HOURS versus ~11.6 days. The limiter now takes an OPTIONAL `cost` defaulting to 1 (load-bearing: it also backs the OTP gates, status gate, mint gate, upload buckets, storage proxy and signaling flood guard), charged SUB-LINEARLY and before the dedupe so padding with repeats costs the same; the naive `cost = n` would have refused History's legitimate 100-number poll and throttled real presence LEDs, so a test drives 20 real polls through the actual limiter. **F10 — `+alias` BYPASSED THE PER-INBOX COOLDOWN**, the only bound on mail to one inbox that is not per-IP, turning it into an IP-bounded mail cannon aimed at a third party. New `canonicalRecipient` strips a `+tag` for THROTTLING ONLY; `normalizeEmail` is untouched because it is the identity key and merging aliases there would make `victim+work@` and `victim@` one account, breaking M35's one-email-one-row invariant; dots are NOT stripped (Gmail-specific, and global application would merge distinct addresses elsewhere); the exact-string cooldown is KEPT alongside, or an attacker could deny an alias's legitimate owner their own code. **F11 — TWO CONCURRENT RENUMBERS COULD STRAND EVERY SAVER PERMANENTLY AND SHED A BLOCK**: `oldNumber` was read up to three round-trips before the transaction opened, so both racers captured the same value; the loser's UPDATE blocks on the winner's row lock and under REPEATABLE READ its read view forms at the contacts SELECT, AFTER the winner committed — so it propagated against a number that no longer existed and left every saver on a number nobody holds and never will (the ledger is monotonic), and because `isNumberBlockedBy` keys on `contacts.number` it inverted the registry's own promise that a block FOLLOWS you. Fixed with a locking `.for("update")` re-read inside the transaction plus a no-op guard for old === new; a SELECT, not a second writer, because this file must contain exactly ONE writer of `identities.number`. `securityBatch2999.test.ts` (35), limiter cost and canonicalisation tested BEHAVIOURALLY; **all 17 tripwires verified by MUTATION**, sources byte-identical afterwards. **TWO WEAKNESSES OF MY OWN CAUGHT BY THAT RUN** and fixed rather than counted as passes, both the same class — an assertion that never reached the code it claimed to cover: the "does not strip dots" case used an address with no `+`, which returns EARLY, and the cooldown test pinned that the read EXISTS while saying nothing about whether it is used. **THREE PRE-EXISTING PINS REWRITTEN to the stronger invariant**, each predicted by its skeptic: one froze the `wasRegistration` lines, i.e. the DEFECT; one froze the sw.js early return whose comment claimed something weaker than what it did; one froze the one-argument `directoryGate(ctx)` shape. **HONEST LIMITATION**: the two new budgets are in-memory and per-instance, so the fleet-wide ceiling is double — bounded rather than unbounded; making them shared means Redis, a bigger change than these findings warrant. No schema change, no new dependency, no new env var. 2439 tests.) A band below the story carries six one-tap reactions, the full catalogue, and a reply input; either lands in the owner's inbox as a private message whose bubble says what it was about. **AN EMOJI AND A SENTENCE ARE THE SAME OPERATION**, which is what the owner described — a separate reaction counter would have been a second data model, a second notification path and a second privacy question for something asked to land in the inbox. **THE MARKER IS STAMPED SERVER-SIDE, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING DECISION**: the chip reading "replied to your status" is a CLAIM ABOUT PROVENANCE, and widening `messages.send`'s meta schema — the obvious shortcut — is unsafe, because that schema is a plain `z.object` which **STRIPS** unknown keys rather than rejecting them and `sendMessage` casts meta through unvalidated, so the key would let any client label any message a reply to any status including one they never had access to; `status.reply` stamps it instead (the `autoReply`/`viaEmail` pattern) and a test asserts `statusReply` appears nowhere in `send`'s input. **NO COPY OF THE STATUS MEDIA IS STORED, a promise rather than an omission** — a status is unreachable after 24h by design, so a stored `mediaUrl` would render a broken tile forever afterwards AND would quietly keep a durable copy of ephemeral media; the marker carries the KIND plus a ≤80-char text excerpt, seen only by the author being quoted their own words and the replier who was audience-authorised. **EVERY GUARD RE-APPLIED because the viewer's verdict lived in a different request**: `requireIdentity` on a **publicProcedure** so a GUEST can reply (guests have identities and can be in an "everyone" audience), `statusGate` BEFORE any DB work (each reply is a row plus an unread increment in someone else's inbox), `getActiveStatusById`, a self-reply refusal, then `statusAudienceAuthorized` — which also covers blocks in BOTH directions ahead of the "everyone" short-circuit, so a block outranks a public audience. **MISSING AND EXPIRED ANSWER IDENTICALLY** or the endpoint is an existence oracle over status ids; the honest reason is derived on the CLIENT from `expiresAt`, which is already on the wire. **REFUSING YOUR OWN STATUS is a real fix**: `getOrCreateDmConversation(me, me)` is a supported self-thread, so an unguarded self-reply posts silently into the user's own Notes. **REALTIME AND PUSH REUSE `kind:"message"`** — a bespoke SSE kind is dropped by `KNOWN_V2_EVENT_KINDS` whenever the recipient's stream is on the other instance (the v2.99.74 trap, and single-instance dev would look perfect), and the `relay-msg-<id>` tag is what makes DND and per-conversation mute apply in the service worker and what makes ten replies REPLACE one notification; the push body is content-free. **THE BUG THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE FEATURE INVISIBLE, caught before shipping**: a one-tap reaction is *precisely* an emoji-only message, and that branch renders a large bare glyph with NO bubble and therefore nowhere for the chip — the owner would have received a floating ❤️ with no indication what it referred to, which is the one thing they asked for; Propagation is the whole difficulty of renumbering and a parallel implementation is precisely how History's copies came to rot before v2.99.54 — so this is a `desiredNumber` PARAMETER on the existing writer, never a second function, and that pin makes any other shape unshippable (mutation-proven: a parallel writer that skips propagation fails the suite). The chosen number resolves to `newNumber` BEFORE the transaction, so the body it shares with a random allocation is byte-identical and inherits every copy. **TAKING A NAMED NUMBER SAFELY**: `normalizeDesiredNumber` accepts the grouping people actually type ("777 777", "777-777" — the app displays numbers that way, so refusing it would be rude) but strips ONLY spacing and grouping, never every non-digit, because `\D`-stripping would silently read "7a7b7c7d7e7f" as 777777 and turn a typo into a successful renumber of somebody's identity; it honours the same `RESERVED_PREFIXES` a random allocation does, or the reserved range would be reserved against the allocator and not against people; and it fails closed on a non-string. Availability is checked against BOTH number tables and then RESERVED in the shared ledger, which is what closes the cross-table NEW-vs-NEW race against a party line minted in the same instant. It spends the same **global mint budget**, because the drain backstop must not be sidesteppable by naming numbers instead of asking for them. Choosing the number you already hold is a **no-op, not an error**, so a double-tap or a retry after a dropped response is harmless rather than reporting "taken" about the caller's own number. **THE SUBTLE BUG I HAD TO REASON OUT AND THEN PIN**: the failure path must NOT hand the reservation back on a pre-flight refusal. `taken` means somebody ELSE holds it — possibly an allocation that has reserved the number but not yet inserted its row — so releasing there would un-reserve a stranger's in-flight number and let two people end up with it. The early return therefore precedes the release, and the ordering is mutation-verified rather than assumed; a genuine post-reservation failure DOES release, and `releaseUnusedNumberReservation` re-checks the number is absent from both tables so even then it cannot un-reserve a bound one. A lost race surfaces as `taken` (errno 1062) rather than a 500, and the OLD number is never released — the ledger is monotonic on purpose, or a number somebody kept written down would later connect them to a stranger. **REGISTERED ACCOUNTS ONLY, as policy not as a limitation**: a chosen number is first-come and permanent, and a guest identity is session-scoped, so a guest claim would squat a memorable number and then strand it the moment the browser closed. **FLAGGED HONESTLY: chosen numbers are FIRST-COME.** Nothing reserves 777777 for anyone, so the owner should claim it promptly; making it admin-only was considered and rejected because `users.role = "admin"` is granted by hand via SQL and may not be set on their account, which would have shipped a feature they could not use. UI: Profile now offers **"Choose my number"** beside **"Random number"** (the old button, renamed and behaviourally untouched — a test pins it still calls the no-argument path).
