This adds the missing transition. **THE RECIPIENT REPORTS IT, NOT THE SERVER** — the tempting version marks a message delivered when the server fans its SSE event, but an open stream proves a socket exists, not that the message reached an app that has it, and it would MISS the case the second tick exists for: somebody who was offline when it was sent and opens the app later without opening the thread. So the report is driven off the RECIPIENT's thread list, mounted in `AppShell` rather than in `Messages` for exactly that reason — opening the app is enough, opening the thread is not required. **DEDUPED ON THE THREAD'S NEWEST MESSAGE TIME**, which is load-bearing rather than an optimisation: that list refetches every 15s, so an undeduped report is a write over the conversation's messages every fifteen seconds forever, for a fact that has not changed — worse than the missing feature. A newer `lastMessageAt` is precisely the signal that something new arrived; the watermark never moves backwards (two tabs, or a stale cached list, must not re-fire); the claim is taken BEFORE the request, because the live `message` event and the refetch it triggers land in the same tick and would otherwise each fire their own write; a genuine failure UN-claims, because a blip must not cost the sender their tick until the next message happens to arrive; and one sweep is capped at 12, so opening the app on a large backlog is not a write storm (the remainder goes on the next sweep, proven by test rather than asserted). **THE RECEIPT CANNOT WALK BACKWARDS**: `markThreadDelivered` promotes ONLY from `sent`, so a late report cannot turn two blue ticks grey again, and excluding `failed` leaves a real failure visible instead of claiming it arrived. Membership-scoped and never delivering to your own messages — the S6 finding's shape, in a second place. **IN A GROUP, delivered means AT LEAST ONE member has it**, not all: the row is shared, so the first member to report flips it for the sender's view — not a shortcut introduced here, since `markThreadRead` has always worked exactly that way, so the second tick inherits the semantics the third already had rather than inventing a different rule for the same row (per-recipient receipts need a per-participant table). The read transition already accepted `delivered` as well as `sent` before this release, which is the one thing that would have silently broken the whole chain — a message that got its second tick could never have gone blue — now pinned so a future narrowing has to come back and think about it. **READING BACKFILLS THE DELIVERED TIME** (`COALESCE`), or the info panel would show a message read at 10:05 that was never delivered, which is not a thing that can happen and reads as a bug in the panel. **A BUG CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING, worth naming because it would have been invisible in testing**: the first cut cast the new event through `as unknown as` to avoid touching the union — but `KNOWN_V2_EVENT_KINDS` gates the RECEIVE side of the Redis bus, so an undeclared kind is delivered locally and **silently DROPPED whenever the sender is on the other instance**, which on a two-instance fleet is most of the time. Single-instance dev would have looked perfect. `delivered` is now a declared member of both, and a test asserts the cast is absent. **(2) THE ⋮ MENU** (owner: *"reply or put forward or delete or info"*): Reply / Forward / Copy / Info, plus Unsend on your own. **Forward RE-SENDS rather than re-pointing the row**, so the target thread gets its own message with its own receipts — which is what makes a forward behave like a send; the attachment rides by id and `messages.send` re-checks the sender may use it, so this cannot smuggle media the forwarder could not already see. Forward is **WITHHELD from a self-destructing message** in both directions rather than offered-then-refused: copying a view-once message into a second permanent thread breaks the exact promise it was sent under, and a menu item that cannot do its job should not be there (the action still refuses, as a backstop, not as the UI). (v2.99.69 — **ADOPT-AND-RETIRE: A GUEST CAN RECLAIM THE NUMBER A BROWSER CLOSE FORGOT.** The last structural data-loss path. v2.99.49 fixed the guest -> register transition and v2.99.54 welded the number to the person through a renumber; what stayed broken was simpler and far more common — **a guest closes their browser**. Both things that resolve a guest are session-scoped BY DESIGN (the device id in `sessionStorage`, the guest cookie a session cookie), so the number, contacts, threads, call history and statuses were stranded with NOTHING left in the browser able to name the row, and nothing reaps those rows either, so the data sat there intact and unreachable. THE DECISION THAT MAKES THE FIX SAFE: **automatic resolution is NOT loosened** — making the device id or the cookie durable would restore the previous guest AUTOMATICALLY, which on a SHARED browser drops the next person into someone else's account, and that session scoping was an explicit product decision rather than an oversight. So this adds a SECOND, DELIBERATE path instead of widening the first: a recovery key the browser keeps in `localStorage`, sent only when the person asks for their number back. Because recovery takes a tap, an explicit **sign-out** is enough to sever it (`forgetGuestRecovery()` on both sign-out paths), so the shared-browser property is preserved by the gesture that actually protects it; pinned that the device id is still sessionStorage and `guestCookieOptions` still adds no `maxAge`. Minted in the SAME insert that creates the identity, so there is no window in which a guest exists with no way back. EVERY EXISTING GUEST IS HEALED: a pre-release row has a NULL hash and would otherwise stay permanently unrecoverable, so `ensureGuestRecoveryKey` issues one on the row's NEXT visit from both of `startGuest`'s reuse branches — never overwriting an EXISTING hash (that would invalidate the copy the browser holds, turning a recoverable identity into a lost one), never touching a row with a `userId`, never throwing, verdict from `affectedRows`. THE SAFETY GATE, because this DELETES AN IDENTITY ROW: the row being retired must be **provably EMPTY** across all seven identity-referencing tables (`identityFootprint`), or adoption would just move the loss to the other row — there is deliberately **no override flag**, and an unreadable count is **-1, never 0**, because treating an unknown as empty is how you delete somebody's messages. The column list matches `scripts/recover-orphan-identity.mjs`: `contacts.ownerId` (NOT `ownerIdentityId`) and call history split into caller/callee, both wrong in that script's first draft and now forbidden by a test. THE RECOVERED IDENTITY KEEPS ITS OWN NUMBER — nothing in the adoption path writes `identities.number` (pinned), so `NUMBER_BEARING_COLUMNS` needs no new entry and nobody who saved the number is broken by its owner coming back. One transaction: retire FIRST (the per-account unique index blocks the claim while the old row lives), then claim, each statement re-stating its preconditions in the WHERE so a concurrent change LOSES instead of corrupting; a lost claim throws to roll the delete back rather than leaving the caller with no identity, reported as `race-lost`. A GUEST caller is rebound (device id + fresh guest token move over, so later requests resolve normally with no special case anywhere else); a REGISTERED caller has the row claimed by their account with the guest handles dropped; a visitor with NO identity skips the retire entirely, which is the PRIMARY path (reopen the browser, restore BEFORE typing a name). EMERGENT PROPERTY WORTH NAMING: this is also a **self-service fix for the owner's original bug** — if a registration ever fails to adopt the browser's guest row, that row stays `userId IS NULL` while the browser still holds its key, so the Profile card offers exactly the stranded identity and a registered caller can claim it without an operator touching the database. `identity.guestRecoveryPreview` (read-only) returns the number, name and footprint the prompt shows verbatim ("restore 601-586 · 14 contacts, 320 messages"), reporting `null` counts rather than a confident zero; `identity.adoptGuestRecovery` performs it. Both `directoryGate`-limited BEFORE any DB work (brute force is not the threat at 2^256 — an unmetered DB read is), both reject a malformed key without hashing it, and refusals are NAMED (`not-found` / `current-has-data` / `footprint-unknown` / `race-lost` / `unavailable`) because each has a different correct next step and `current-has-data` must never be silently resolved by discarding one side. Both rewrites verified to still bite. 2190 tests.) (v2.99.68 — ROUND 11: THE SIGNALING ROOM REGISTRY SURVIVES THE LOSS OF THE LEADER. Clustered signaling elects ONE leader that owns the whole call registry — rooms, members, roles, the pin→room index — in memory; kill that process and every active call's room is gone FLEET-WIDE, so nothing can be renegotiated and a relayed call cannot recover. Verified absent before building (`relay:room:*` and `rejoin-recreate` were both 0 occurrences). **A — DURABLE SHADOW** (`server/roomStore.ts`): every room mutation marks the room dirty, a coalesced next-tick flush writes it (the `touchBusyState` discipline, so a handler crossing several funnels mid-transition writes ONCE, settled), plus a 15s sweep so a mutation site nobody marked still converges. `relay:room:<id>` is ONE hash — `e` (epoch) + `d` (signed JSON) — because a single atomic HSET means a reader can never see a half-written room; `relay:rooms` is a SET index so hydration is one SMEMBERS, not a SCAN. THE PIN→ROOM INDEX IS DERIVED, not stored as `relay:pinroom:<pin>` per the spec: a pin is in at most its ACTIVE and its HELD room and BOTH always contain it, so a `held` flag per member rebuilds both maps on the SAME atomic write, where separate keys would be a second write that can land out of order. FENCED: a lease can expire while its holder is alive and still believes it leads, and two leaders both writing would interleave two registries into one record — so every write carries a monotonic epoch (`INCR relay:leader:epoch` on winning) applied by a Lua CAS that refuses a LOWER one (`>`, not `>=`, so a leader can overwrite itself); losing the lease sets the epoch to 0, stopping writes at the source. HYDRATION GATES SERVING — a new leader mints, reads back, and only THEN processes signaling (a leader answering `accept` for a room it had not hydrated would tell the caller the call is gone); 5s timeout then it serves ANYWAY, fail open, because a missing room degrades to "dial again" while a wedged signaling layer means nobody can call at all. **THE BUG THAT WOULD HAVE MADE ALL OF IT A NO-OP**, found by reasoning through the behavioural test before writing it: a hydrated room has NO connected members by construction, which is exactly the "room of ghosts" shape `sendRejoinIfInRoom` exists to dissolve — the FIRST peer back would have called `leaveRoom` and deleted the very call hydration saved. New `roomMeta.hydratedAt` + `HYDRATED_GRACE_MS` (45s) holds it until its owners re-register, after which a ghost room behaves exactly as before. Records are HMAC'd with the fleet key (they cross the same trust boundary as bus envelopes and hydration feeds them into the live registry); `busSecret` is now EXPORTED from redisBus and imported rather than re-derived — a second copy of "which env var is the fleet secret" is what caused the v2.99.49 identity bug. **B — `rejoin-recreate`, REWRITTEN AROUND A SIGNED CAPABILITY.** The spec had the client send `{roomId, selfPin, selfRole, knownMembers}` and the server recreate-and-admit; that is an authorization hole, because room ids are relayed to every participant, so naming a stranger's roomId would admit you to their live call and `selfRole:"host"` would hand you kick/mute/admit over it — the exact class closed by v2.99.43 (M45) and v2.99.57 (R-GENPIN). The client is asked for ONE thing instead: a capability THIS FLEET minted when it admitted that pin to that room (`server/roomCapability.ts`, `<exp>.<role>.<hmac>`, 12h). Subject pin from the CONNECTION, role from INSIDE the signature, claimed member list not read at all — membership converges because every returning peer presents its own; a signed `host` capability takes a VACANT host seat and never displaces one, so concurrent recreators cannot fight over moderation; no fleet secret ⇒ the path does not exist rather than existing unauthenticated. **C — CLUSTER HYGIENE** (review findings 26/27, both confirmed real first): `makeRemoteSocket` returned only `{send, close}`, so `!target.socket.alive` short-circuited TRUE for every remote peer. A per-instance heartbeat (`relay:sig:hb:<leader>`, 5s, ONE frame per instance carrying its cid list) now drives a real `alive()` that FAILS OPEN twice over — unknown cid, and an instance that has never beaten at all (an older build mid-rollout) — because reporting a LIVE browser as dead sends its calls to the leave-a-message card; a home that misses 20s hands its browsers to the ORDINARY `cleanupRegistryConn` grace, not oblivion, since it may just be restarting. On a leader change each instance sends its local browsers `{type:"resync"}` → re-register → `rejoin` from the hydrated rooms (old clients ignore the unknown type). SECOND BUG CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING: the change hook is deliberately silent when the new leader is US, so the instance that TOOK OVER would have repaired every browser in the fleet except its own — it now resyncs them at the end of taking over, after hydration. The client keeps the capability beside `roomId`, refreshed by every room ack in ONE place so a future ack inherits recovery for free, persists it in the rejoin snapshot, and DROPS it on hang-up/destroy, which is what stops the repair path resurrecting a call the user ended; the recreate is ARMED (1.5s), not sent, so it only fires when the room is genuinely gone. `server/roundEleven.test.ts` (35, driving the real registry) + `server/roomStoreLive.test.ts` (7, against a REAL spawned redis-server — the fence is Lua and Lua runs inside Redis, so a string check of the script is not evidence it works; a lower-epoch write AND a lower-epoch DELETE are both proven refused). 10 tripwires verified by mutation, reverting from byte-exact backups and aborting on a missing target (never `git checkout --` — that discarded uncommitted work under test in v2.99.56 and produced three false PASSes); two of my first mutations were wrong rather than the tests, and one property turned out to be defended by three redundant gates — recorded rather than quietly counted as a pass. NO OPS REQUIRED: `RELAY_CLUSTER=1` + `REDIS_URL` are already live and every new key self-expires. 2108 tests.) (v2.99.67 — **THE PHONE-HEATING FIX, A VANISHING CONFERENCE TILE, THE WRAPPED DIAL PAD, AND THE MISSED-CALL BANNER.** **(1) THE LANDING PAGE MADE PHONES HOT** (owner: *"when I open this website from the phone, the phone is heating"*). MEASURED, not guessed — an emulated 390px phone at 4x CPU throttle against the real built bundle. The page ran TWO uncapped `requestAnimationFrame` loops (the fx loop and the WebGL scene), repainted a FULL-VIEWPORT canvas at device pixel ratio EVERY frame, rewrote SIX gradient/box-shadow style strings 20 times a second (`fc % 3` at 60fps — each pass re-parsing two 1100px `radial-gradient`s plus three box-shadows over most of the viewport), and did none of it conditionally on the tab being visible. FIXED: a frame budget (30fps desktop, 20fps on a low-power device), an early return when `document.hidden` (with the rAF re-armed BEFORE the return, or the loop would die on the first hidden frame), the chrome tint throttled by TIME rather than frame count (~4.5/s instead of 20/s, so the cost no longer tracks the frame rate and the slowly-drifting hue looks identical), the matrix canvas dropped from DPR 1.5 to 1.0 and from a column every 18px to every 26px on a phone, and THE WEBGL SCENE SKIPPED ENTIRELY on a low-power device (`innerWidth <= 820` OR `hardwareConcurrency <= 4` OR Data Saver). RESULT, before -> after on that emulated phone: canvas repaints **59.1/s -> 16.6/s**, backing store **585x1266 -> 390x844**, i.e. canvas fill **~43.7 Mpx/s -> ~5.5 Mpx/s (~8x less)**. HONEST LIMIT: the WebGL saving is asserted from the source gate, NOT measured — this headless environment runs `--disable-gpu` and reported no WebGL context in EITHER run, so the probe could not observe the scene either way. The `prefers-reduced-motion` path is untouched. **(2) A PARTICIPANT WHO TOOK ANOTHER CALL CAME BACK WITH NO TILE** (owner: *"on the conference call, somebody got a line, when he answer and he returned back, he disappeared… he keep hearing [him], but his profile is disappeared"*). ROOT CAUSE: `onPeerHold` restored a placeholder tile ONLY under `livekitEnabled`, so on the MESH the tile stayed gone; and the coming-BACK branch only stripped the `.on-hold` class, so if the tile had already left with the peer's transport there was nothing to un-hold. `addTile` could not help — it requires a live `peers[id]` entry, which is exactly what the teardown removed. New `ensurePlaceholderTile` makes a name-only tile on EITHER transport, marked `data-ph` so `addTile`/`addLkTile` REPLACE it instead of appending a second element with the same id; called on hold AND on return. **(3) THE LANDING DIAL PAD WRAPPED ON A PHONE** (owner screenshot: five digits on one line, the sixth below). Six digits joined by spaces is 11 characters; at 30px monospace with `.28em` letter-spacing that is ~290px against ~285px of inner card width at 390px — so it wrapped, and only on a phone, which is why it shipped. Now `white-space:nowrap` (structurally one line) plus `font:clamp(19px,6.2vw,30px)` and `letter-spacing:clamp(.13em,.6vw,.28em)`, whose maxima are the original values, so desktop is unchanged. **(4) THE MISSED-CALL BANNER IS GONE FROM THE MAIN SCREEN** (owner: *"don't show it on the main screen as a side banner from up to down. Show it only on the notification center on the top… and also on the history"*). `AwaySummaryToast` is no longer mounted (the component is kept, the import cleaned up). Nothing is lost: the bell still counts missed calls AND unread messages, still blinks for them, lists them in its panel, and routes to History / Messages — pull rather than push. **STILL OPEN:** the group-call tiles are STATIC PHOTOS and the owner has now twice asked for people who look like they are talking. Lips cannot move on a still image — that needs short looping video per tile, which is an asset decision, so it is flagged rather than faked. `client/src/app/ownerUiBatch3.test.ts` (17); two pre-existing pins REWRITTEN to the new intent rather than relaxed — the v2.97.1 hold pin now asserts the transport-agnostic restore in BOTH directions, and the v2.99.12 away-card pin now asserts the banner is unmounted while the bell keeps the count, the blink and the routes. 2066 tests.) (v2.99.65 — TURN :443 DIAGNOSED TO ITS TWO REMAINING OWNER-ONLY STEPS, plus the code change that unblocks the better fix. `turn-fix` (v2.99.63) ran and established: both relays are EC2 instances in this account (`i-0ccd35acc6940c5dc` = 13.232.119.83, `i-0cf65f64e50fa4e3d` = 13.204.23.58) and they SHARE ONE SECURITY GROUP, `sg-063532b4c358d1513` — which explains why :443 is dead on BOTH identically and means the network half is ONE rule, not two. (v2.99.63 (v2.99.63 — `turn-fix`: find out WHY TCP/443 is dead on both TURN relays, and fix the part that is safe to automate. The v2.99.62 health check reported `turn:<host>:443?transport=tcp` DOWN on both relays while udp/3478, tcp/3478 and turns/5349 all allocate — which matters more than 2/8 suggests, because 443 is the candidate that exists for networks blocking UDP and non-standard ports: on exactly those networks the other three are also unusable, so those users get no relay at all. A timeout has two possible causes with different fixes (a security group dropping 443, or coturn not listening on it), so the action DIAGNOSES BY DEFAULT and `turn_apply` defaults to false — production networking is never changed on a guess. It reads TURN_HOSTS from the app fleet's own env (so it can never drift from what clients are told), resolves each to its EC2 instance BY PUBLIC IP rather than a tag (survives a rename), reports whether tcp/443 is permitted by each relay's security groups, and — if the relay hosts are SSM-managed — what is actually LISTENING on 443/3478/5349 plus their coturn listening-port lines. With `turn_apply=true` it opens tcp/443 on the relay security groups; that is the ONLY mutation it can make, gated behind the flag (pinned by a test asserting the gate precedes the write). It deliberately does NOT rewrite coturn's config: those hosts may not be managed by this role, and the better fix is TLS on 443 — `alt-tls-listening-port=443` + `TURN_TLS_PORT=443` — because TLS on 443 is indistinguishable from HTTPS and passes DPI, where plaintext TURN on 443 does not. (v2.99.62 (v2.99.62 — TURN HEALTH IS NOW A REAL, IN-VPC CHECK, AND MULTI-TURN IS LIVE. `TURN_HOSTS=13.232.119.83,13.204.23.58` + `TURN_TLS=1` were applied to the fleet via two `env-set` runs; the live `/api/relay/ice` went 3 → 6 → **8 URLs** (both zones × udp / tcp:443 / tcp:3478 / turns:5349). `TURN_TLS` had never been set, so the `turns:` candidate was not advertised even for relay 1 despite the cert being live — found by reading the live output instead of trusting the config. It prints no secret, and releases each allocation with a zero-lifetime Refresh so a repeated health check cannot accumulate them. The fleet now runs one coturn per AZ (13.232.119.83 in ap-south-1a, 13.204.23.58 in ap-south-1b, both TLS-live), but the server only ever told clients about ONE — the relay list is minted server-side at registration, so this was the single layer of the HA story infrastructure could not fix on its own: losing a zone took the relay path with it. (v2.99.60 (v2.99.60 — THE AFFINITY FIX VERIFIED LIVE + AN ORPHAN-IDENTITY RECOVERY TOOL. v2.99.59's proxy fix is CONFIRMED against production: the same probe that measured **12/24 POSTs returning 404** now returns **24/24 200s**. One consequence is recorded deliberately rather than discovered later — an instance that is not the home cannot distinguish 'homed elsewhere' from 'no such cid', so a DEAD cid now also gets 200 instead of 404. Nothing regresses (the client never acted on the 404; it retries blindly and the SSE close is what drives reconnect, and a dead channel's message was undeliverable either way) and it removes a cid-existence oracle, so the response is now uniform by design; the integration test asserts that shape so it stays a decision. Restoring the distinction would mean mirroring cid→home into Redis — ALB stickiness is the cheaper cure and stays the ops follow-up. ALSO: `scripts/recover-orphan-identity.mjs`, the recovery CLAUDE.md has described as 'designed but not yet built' since v2.99.54 — it moves a pre-v2.99.49 orphaned guest identity (the owner's 601-586) onto its account. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT; it refuses unless the orphan is genuinely unclaimed (`userId IS NULL`), the user exists, and the identity it would REPLACE is provably EMPTY across all seven identity-referencing tables — there is deliberately no override, because the only way this destroys data is by deleting a non-empty row. The write is one transaction whose statements re-check their own preconditions in the WHERE clause, so a concurrent change loses instead of corrupting, and re-running after success is a no-op. Two column names were WRONG in my first draft (`contacts.ownerId`, not `ownerIdentityId`; call_history splits into `callerIdentityId`/`calleeIdentityId`) — caught by checking the schema, and now caught automatically: a PREFLIGHT validates every table/column against information_schema before reading a single row, so a rename can never silently under-count the emptiness check. HONEST LIMIT: no MySQL was reachable here (docker client present, daemon not running), so only the argument/preflight guards were executed — the DB paths are unrun, which is exactly why the destructive half is opt-in behind --apply. 2013 tests.) (v2.99.59 (v2.99.59 — **HALF OF ALL SIGNALING MESSAGES WERE BEING DROPPED IN PRODUCTION.** Task #38 was a QA-sweep suspicion nobody had confirmed; it is REAL and I measured it against the live fleet: open one SSE stream, then POST 24 times for that same cid — **12 returned 404 `channel not found`**. The SSE stream and each `/api/relay/send` POST are separate HTTP requests, and the ALB round-robins them across the two instances with no stickiness, so the POST routinely lands on the box that holds no channel for that cid. `attachRelay`'s clustered POST path checked `localDelivery.has(cid)` and answered 404, dropping the message on the floor. `sendWS` retries 3× with backoff, so ~6% were lost OUTRIGHT and the survivors delayed up to ~3s — on the offer/answer/ICE path, which is call-fatal. This is very likely the substrate under a long tail of 'calls not ringing / dying seconds after dial' reports that earlier versions chased as client bugs. FIX: a misrouted POST is now PROXIED to the leader instead of refused (`clusterProxyInbound`). The proxying instance does not know the home and is not allowed to claim it — the frame carries `proxy:true` and the leader IGNORES the claimed `home`, routing the reply to the home it already recorded in `homeOf`. No recorded home ⇒ the frame is DROPPED rather than binding the cid to an instance with no stream, which would have black-holed every subsequent reply (that failure mode is its own test). The v2.99.49 anti-spoof rule (`f.home !== fromInstance` ⇒ drop) is untouched for normal frames, and a proxy frame is strictly safer because its claim is never read. `decodeInbound` normalises `proxy` to a boolean so a frame from a not-yet-updated instance is explicitly non-proxied during a rolling deploy. Pinned by an integration test that replays the exact production scenario — B's ACCEPT arriving as a POST on the wrong instance — and asserts the call still connects; **verified to FAIL against the pre-fix 404** before being kept. 2013 tests.) (v2.99.57 (v2.99.57 — 20-EXPERT SECURITY SWEEP: 46 CONFIRMED FINDINGS, 20 FIXED IN FOUR BATCHES (owner: "get me 20 securies expert and scan the whole web apps for bugs or errors and fix it without my approvals"). 20 experts, one per vulnerability class/surface, each briefed with a recon map of the ~55 already-closed classes and 16 accepted residuals — without it the report would have been mostly noise, since the prior panel refuted 19 of 22 candidates purely because they were already fixed. 65 candidates raised, each judged by THREE independent skeptics with distinct lenses (reachability / is-it-still-true / write-the-exploit), all defaulting to REFUTED: 46 survived, 19 killed, 217 agents. **HIGHS FIXED.** **R-GENPIN (1,8,45)** — `genPin` excluded only `reg.clients`, so an anonymous register could be handed a real identity's number whose owner just had no live stream: multi-device ring fanned that victim's dials to the squatter, `deliverPendingRing` handed over a ring in flight, `sendRejoinIfInRoom` dropped them into a live call with the roster and a LiveKit token, and the ring card rendered the VICTIM's name/avatar/badge (the caller is resolved BY PIN). Fixed in two layers — `genPin` now excludes `pinRoom`/`heldRoom` and uses `crypto.randomInt` (v2.99.20 #9 missed this second minting site), and `pinIsAddressable` makes an unverified registration un-ringable/un-rejoinable; the rejoin gate is `verifiedClaim(pin) || pin === effectiveOwned`, because `verifiedClaim` alone would strand an ordinary reload whose `createContext` hiccupped. **Finding 2** — the S2 gate counts a HELD room as shared and is evaluated from the SENDER's side, but the relayed frame carried no room: a peer whose call you PARKED could hand-craft a `signal`, land in `onSignal` with no matching peer, and have `createPeer` built around your CURRENTLY live stream — mic AND camera, since `createPeer` flips `callIsGroup` which makes `consentOk` true. A total mutual-consent bypass. The server stamps the authorizing room; the client routes on it via a new pure `signalDisposition` that deliberately does NOT gate the ACTIVE-room case on a client roster (the server already proved membership, and a roster check would refuse legitimate mesh offers arriving before `peer-joined`); unstamped frames fail OPEN. **Finding 7** — the boot-URL guard required a digit right after `/i/` while App.tsx strips EVERY non-digit, so `/i/x555555` was invisible to the guard and one-click dialable: M48 for the THIRD time, a guard parsing differently from the code it guards. Now uses the consumer's own normalization, with a test asserting the two AGREE on every input. **Finding 4** — ReDoS: M42 bounded the same quadratic regex in `parseInboundAddress` only, and `normalizeEmail` runs it over the same headers on a 5MB route; the cap now lives IN the function so a later caller inherits it. **Findings 3/5+9/6** — three surfaces had a RATE limit but no OCCUPANCY limit (media streams, contacts, push fan-out), any of which OOMs the `instances: 1` 1GB process that owns every call. Fixed with an in-flight ceiling released from ONE idempotent handler, a HEADER-PHASE-only upstream timeout (an abort signal also kills body streaming), an IDLE stall watchdog (wall-clock would break `<video>` seeking), an insert-RANK contact cap that never refuses an UPDATE (a user at the ceiling must still be able to BLOCK someone), a `listContacts` limit EQUAL to the cap instead of pagination (the client sorts over the whole list, so a short page would silently HIDE contacts), oldest-first push eviction gated on the row being ours, and a fixed-size send pool. **Finding 38** — `MAX_STREAMS_PER_IP = 25` was documented as "far above any legitimate device count" and was not: per-IP, two streams per tab, so ~12 tabs across a CGNAT population exhausted it and lost calling entirely; raised 10x with the open-rate limiter left as the flood defence, plus an off-by-one where a tab refresh was refused by its own superseded stream. **MEDIUMS FIXED**: moderation reaching HELD members and acting on their OTHER call (kick called `leaveRoom`, which acts on the target's ACTIVE room — dropping an unrelated call while leaving them a member here); no host succession when the host's SSE is grace-reaped (M53 covered `leaveRoom` only); `status.feed` missing "I blocked them" so a blocked person's status TEXT leaked while its media 403'd; over-cap view-once media burned before the size check and reported as success; `GET /api/auth/verify` mutating, so a mail security gateway detonating the link verified the account before the recipient opened it — plus M29's THIRD claim site, now clearing a credential set before the address was proven. LOWs: `deleteMessage` made an atomic claim (concurrent unsends each decremented other participants' STORED unreadCount, corrupting it permanently) and `messages.typing` block-gated per recipient. Eight stale pins rewritten to the stronger invariant; 41 new pins verified to FAIL against the pre-change sources. REMAINING, told plainly rather than quietly dropped: the OTP-register family, the two clustered-mode findings, `regenerateIdentityNumber`'s out-of-transaction read, the mint budget as a fleet-wide onboarding kill switch, the inbound-email block gate, `messages.list` byte budget, sign-out not removing the push subscription, DND on contact-online pushes, the FCM re-bind claim, `aws-ops.yml` pinning, and `directoryGate` charging one token for a 100-number `presenceMany` — all enumerated in todo.md. 2000 tests.) (v2.99.54 — **IDENTITY CONTINUITY: DATA IS WELDED TO THE PERSON, NOT TO THEIR NUMBER** (owner, after the v2.99.49 data-loss fix: *"what I care is that it should not be repeated again to any other users... if you were a guest and you have data and you decide to register, you should not lose your data. It will move with you whenever you are moving. You can regenerate the number, but you will not lose your data. But your number is hooked to other contact lists — it will be updated automatically. So you need a mature system, no glitches"*). THE STRUCTURAL INSIGHT: RELAY names a person TWICE. The **identity row** is referenced by numeric id — contacts, messages, thread membership, call logs and statuses all point at it, so they follow the person through every transition with nothing to migrate. The **6-digit number** is what OTHER people store, and every place it is stored is a COPY THAT CAN ROT. Registration lost the owner's data because the upgrade could not find their identity row (v2.99.49); renumbering rotted History because the propagation guarantee lived inside one function that happened to know about `contacts`. Same root cause, two symptoms. **(1) NUMBER CONTINUITY.** `conference_history.dialedNumber` is what `History.tsx:721` uses for the call-back button, so after anyone regenerated their number that button dialled a number they no longer owned (dead, never a stranger — the reservation ledger never recycles); the same stale value was DISPLAYED as "PIN NNNNNN" as if it were fact, the presence dot looked it up and stuck grey forever, and the avatar was resolved BY NUMBER so a renumbered person silently lost their photo from everybody's History. `conference_participants.number` and the JSON roster froze every participant's number at call time. New `NUMBER_BEARING_COLUMNS` in `server/v2db.ts` declares EVERY schema column holding a 6-digit number and how it stays correct (`identity` = source of truth, `renumber` = rewritten in the transaction, `live` = never rewritten but resolved from the identity at read time, `not-a-person` = a party line's own number, which a person renumbering must never touch); `regenerateIdentityNumber` now also moves `conference_participants.number` scoped by `identityId`; and `calls.conferenceHistory` resolves the roster BY `identityId` (live number, name, avatar) and maps the frozen `dialedNumber` through the roster to a live call-back target — so renumbers that ALREADY happened come out correct with no backfill. `server/numberContinuity.test.ts` reads `drizzle/schema.ts` and FAILS THE BUILD if any number-bearing column has no declared strategy (verified by planting a fake column and watching it fail, naming the column) — so the guarantee cannot rot the next time someone adds a table. **(2) THE AUDIT'S FINDINGS AGAINST MY OWN v2.99.49 FIX.** A 51-agent adversarial audit red-teamed it and three findings landed. **MY TESTS DID NOT TEST WHAT THEY CLAIMED**: the test named "the PIN / legacy sign-in path too" anchored with `indexOf("await ensureUserIdentity({")`, but that substring first occurs 17 characters INSIDE verifyOtp's own `const identity = await ensureUserIdentity({` — so it re-read verifyOtp and never looked at the PIN site 5,626 chars later. PROVEN by reverting the PIN path to the pre-fix cookie-only shape (the exact bug that cost the owner their data): all 20 tests still passed. A test that cannot fail when its bug returns is worse than no test, because it reports safety. Rewritten to ENUMERATE every `ensureUserIdentity` call per file, assert the COUNT as well as the contents, and — the guard that makes the per-file tests exhaustive rather than a hand-maintained list — walk every server source and assert the complete set of minting sites; each rewritten test was then verified to FAIL against its reintroduced bug. Also vacuous: "minting is the LAST resort" compared two `indexOf` results, and on pre-fix code the candidate loop was absent (-1) while allocate was at 959, so `-1 < 959` and it PASSED against the code it was written to reject (both indices are now required to exist first). **A FIFTH MINTING SITE WAS MISSED**: `/api/oauth/callback` still passed the cookie ONLY — the original bug shape on a still-mounted route — and was the worst of the five, because without `resolvedIdentityId` the stranded-guest warning could not fire either, so it stranded people SILENTLY. **THAT SITE ALSO DESTROYED THE RECOVERY EVIDENCE**: it ran `clearCookie` unconditionally, "regardless of whether the migration happened" — and the guest token is the only half of guest identity that survives a browser close, so dropping it after a failed claim converts a RECOVERABLE orphan into a permanent one. The cookie is now cleared only when the identity we ended up with really IS this browser's guest row (resolved BEFORE the claim, since a successful claim nulls the token), and a non-adoption warns instead of being silent; `isGuest` is deliberately NOT the test, because it is equally false for a freshly minted identity, i.e. for exactly the failure case. **THE CLAIM WAS UNGUARDED AGAINST THE PER-USER UNIQUE INDEX** while the mint path directly below it handles that race: an uncaught throw there surfaces as a 500 from `verifyOtp` AFTER `consumeOtp` has burned the code, so the user is told their code was already used and must request another for a registration that half-completed — the claim now resolves to the race winner, like the mint path. **(3) THE VIDEO-CONSENT PROMPT** (owner screenshot, mid-call after enabling the camera): the "X wants to start video" card ran off the RIGHT edge — name cut to "a Hasan", button to "Turn on vide" — while colliding with the Minimize/Fit chrome and the "Connected" status, reading washed-out over live video. ROOT CAUSE MEASURED IN HEADLESS CHROMIUM, not guessed: the card centred with `transform:translateX(-50%)` and entered with `animation:relayFade … both`, whose final keyframe is `transform:none` — fill-mode `both` makes that PERSIST, so the centring transform was wiped and the card's LEFT edge sat at exactly 50% of the viewport (390px: left 195, right 429 = 39px off-screen; 375px: 47px off; 320px: 74px off; 1280px desktop: just fits, which is WHY it shipped — broken only on phones). The computed transform read `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`, the identity, which is the direct proof. Positioning no longer involves `transform` at all (`inset:0` + `margin:auto` + intrinsic size against `.relay-root`, which is `position:fixed;inset:0`) and the entrance animates OPACITY ONLY; it is opaque instead of translucent-over-blur, with the surroundings dimmed by a spread `box-shadow` (not hit-tested, so hang-up stays tappable). THIS TRAP WAS ALREADY FOUND AND FIXED ONCE for `.addpad`, whose comment spells it out verbatim, and never swept — so this was the same bug in a second place; `client/src/lib/videoAskCentring.test.ts` now guards the WHOLE stylesheet, failing the build if any element centred with `translateX(-50%)` applies `relayFade`, proven to fire against the pre-fix shape and proven not to flag `.call-waiting`/`.held-bar`, which restate the transform in their own `cwIn` keyframes. **(4) DEAD CODE AND DEPENDENCIES REMOVED** (owner: "delete whatever not ours and it's zero value"): 12 files, 4,292 lines, 6 packages, each verified unreferenced by a precise import check and by confirming no test touches it — the Manus template helpers `_core/dataApi|heartbeat|imageGeneration|llm|map|voiceTranscription`, `DashboardLayout` + its skeleton (only the former imported the latter; nothing imported either since v2.92 removed the OAuth sign-in it served), `Map.tsx`, `ComponentShowcase.tsx`, `data/landingCopy.ts` (superseded — `Home.tsx` carries its own copy and `scripts/gen-landing-copy.mjs` regenerates it), `shared/types.ts`; plus `ws` + `@types/ws` (POINTED: this architecture DELIBERATELY refuses WebSocket, since the gateway downgrades the upgrade — it was a dependency for the one thing the rules forbid), `@types/google.maps`, `framer-motion`, `add` (the `pnpm add add` typo) and `pnpm` as a devDependency (redundant against the `packageManager` pin that `ci.yml` itself calls "the single source of truth", and contradictory: `^10.15.1` vs the pinned `10.4.1`). DELIBERATELY KEPT: the unreferenced shadcn/ui primitives, because CLAUDE.md mandates shadcn for new UI and they tree-shake out of the bundle — pruning the sanctioned kit is an architectural call, flagged not taken. **STILL OPEN, told to the owner plainly**: their 601-586 identity is still orphaned (the audit confirmed it retains BOTH its guest token and device id, and the empty row has no device id, so it IS still resolvable — recovery is designed but not yet built); guest identity is SESSION-SCOPED by construction (both halves die on browser close), which is the architectural reason data does not yet "move with you" in every case; and the verification email hitting spam is mostly domain reputation (headers, multipart/alternative and copy were all audited CLEAN — my initial theory was wrong). 1879 tests.) (v2.99.50 — THE SERVE SET NOW MATCHES WHAT A PHONE HANDS BACK. Closes the one surviving item from the red-team pass over today's fixes (its panel refuted all 22 candidates — 19 were already fixed in v2.99.47/.48 while it ran, so the triggers no longer reproduced — and left one LOW kernel, which I re-confirmed against source myself). TWO GATES I WROTE TODAY DISAGREED: M38's `INLINE_SAFE_TYPE` in storageProxy serves only a small allowlist as itself and downgrades everything else to `application/octet-stream` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`, and v2.99.45's self-review checked that list against every type RELAY's own encoders PRODUCE — but the avatar and Status pickers upload the RAW `File` with no re-encode (`uploadBare`) and the upload door only tests `^image/`, so an iPhone `image/heic` or an Android `video/3gpp` stored fine and was then served as an opaque download. Fixed by widening the SERVE side (image/heic|heif|tiff|apng, video/x-m4v|3gpp|3gpp2|x-matroska|mpeg, audio/flac|wave|x-wav|3gpp) rather than narrowing the door, which would have REJECTED a legitimate photo — the exact class of regression this run has been undoing. Impact is honestly LOW (every avatar surface already falls back to an initials disc, `Content-Disposition` is ignored for `<img>`/`<video>` subresource loads, and HEIC doesn't decode in Chrome/Firefox anyway), but two gates disagreeing is a latent trap regardless. The load-bearing addition is a PROPERTY test: `INLINE_SAFE_TYPE` can never admit a markup or script media type (text/*, the XML family, XHTML, SVG, the JavaScript types, octet-stream), plus a structural check that the pattern never mentions the `text` top-level type — so the list is free to grow under the invariant M38 exists to hold. Also corrected a factual error from the parallel session's bulk renumbering: `repoHygiene.test.ts` claimed v2.99.49 shipped with conflict markers; that was v2.99.45. 1835 tests.) (v2.99.49 — **REGISTERING AS A GUEST NO LONGER CHANGES YOUR NUMBER OR ORPHANS YOUR DATA** (owner report with a two-screenshot comparison: they used RELAY as a guest on **601-586** — saved contacts, exchanged messages, made calls — registered with their email, verified the code, and landed on **737-582**, a brand-new number, with an empty account; verbatim: *"the data should be stored and attached to the old number, and the number will not change unless if I request to generate a new number"*). ROOT CAUSE — TWO FUNCTIONS DISAGREED ABOUT WHICH IDENTITY A BROWSER IS USING, and one of them allocates: `createContext` resolves a guest by guest cookie **OR** device id and documents that the DEVICE ID WINS when they disagree ("cookies are a hint, device id is the truth" — that rule exists precisely so a cleared / expired / ITP-dropped cookie doesn't cost a guest their number), while `ensureUserIdentity` — the upgrade that runs at registration — looked the guest up by **cookie token ONLY**. So for every browser whose live identity was device-resolved rather than cookie-resolved, the upgrade found nothing, fell through to its allocate-a-fresh-identity branch, and minted a new 6-digit number; the guest row (with the number, contacts, messages and call history hanging off its id) was left behind with `userId` still NULL and no way back to it. FIX (`server/v2db.ts`): `ensureUserIdentity` now takes `resolvedIdentityId` + `deviceId` and tries candidates in the RESOLVER'S OWN ORDER OF AUTHORITY — the identity the request already resolved (device-id-aware, so it agrees with every other request in that browser by construction), then the cookie token, then the device id — deduped through a `Set`, with each optional lookup individually try/caught so a transient DB hiccup can never be the reason someone gets a new number. Each claim is ONE conditional UPDATE gated `WHERE id = ? AND userId IS NULL`, verified by `affectedRows`, so it can only ever adopt an UNCLAIMED guest row and can never take an identity that belongs to another account (a refused candidate just moves to the next; `getIdentityByDeviceId` independently filters to `userId IS NULL` as a second guard). The claim sets `userId` / name / clears the cookie fields and **never touches `number`**, then re-reads by the SAME id — so the number, contacts, messages and history all simply carry over. Minting is now genuinely the last resort. ALSO — the same hint-blindness existed at **three other identity-minting call sites**, all fixed system-wide (repo rule): `createContext` itself mints on ANY request when a signed-in account has no identity yet (it now passes `deviceId`), `POST /api/auth/register` (the legacy password route, now passes `deviceIdFromRequest(req)`), and the PIN / legacy sign-in path in `v2routers.ts`. The header's shape rule moved into a new dependency-free `server/deviceIdHeader.ts` (`DEVICE_ID_HEADER`, `normalizeDeviceId`, `deviceIdFromRequest`) that `_core/context.ts` now delegates to — a second copy of that rule is what caused this bug, and `context.ts` ↔ `authLocal.ts` already import each other so a shared module was also the only cycle-free way to do it. The `existingByUser` early return now `console.warn`s when it leaves a guest identity unclaimed (re-registering an address that already has an account is the one case where a guest session really is stranded — it should not be silent). SECOND HALF OF THE OWNER'S ASK — *"even if I generate new number and my numbers and others people contact, it will automatically update"* — ALREADY SHIPPED and now pinned by this release's tests: `regenerateIdentityNumber` moves the identity and rewrites every contact row that saved the old number **inside one transaction** (all-or-nothing, so no contact is left dialling a number that is no longer that person), via `planRenumber`, which also drops a stale duplicate when the saver already had a row for the new number. A test asserts there is exactly ONE `.update(identities).set({ number: … })` in the whole codebase, so no future path can renumber someone silently. `server/guestUpgrade.test.ts` (20 — candidate order, the unclaimed-only gate, number/data preservation, all four call sites, behavioural `normalizeDeviceId` coverage incl. the repeated-header and injection-shaped inputs, and the regenerate-propagation pins). Each residual was accepted because the obvious fix broke something, so each was investigated against current source before any change — and THREE of my intended designs were corrected by that pass. **R1 PUSH ENDPOINT RE-BIND**: the upsert re-bound `identityId` keyed on the globally-unique `endpoint` alone, so anyone who learned a victim's endpoint could silently kill their notifications. Shipped instead: a per-browser CLAIM secret in localStorage (deliberately NOT cleared on sign-out, because it identifies the browser profile rather than an identity), stored server-side only as a sha256 hash; shipped a `claimedAt` marker (no DEFAULT, or the reaper would be a permanent no-op) stamped at all four allocator sites, guarded release on the two reachable failure paths, and an hourly reaper needing FOUR independent conditions including a hardcoded EPOCH FLOOR that replaces the backfill I had planned (a NULL on a pre-release row means "unknown", not "leaked"). **R3 REDIS BUS AUTHENTICATION**: HMAC signing whose wire format stays a FLAT `{i,p}` object with the signature in EXTRA fields, because the old decoder ignores extras — any other shape would make every not-yet-updated instance parse-fail and drop 100% of real events during each rolling deploy; unsigned is accepted until `REDIS_BUS_STRICT=1`, with `/api/health` reporting `busAuth` counters so the flip happens on evidence, and the leader now also refuses a frame whose `home` differs from its publisher. **R4 PER-ACCOUNT PASSWORD LOCKOUT**: its OWN columns (sharing the PIN's would let a password brute-force lock out PIN sign-in — a cross-channel DoS), a slot claimed BEFORE the secret is tested so the cap bounds scrypt work, no dependence on SET emission order, three independent escape hatches, a uniform 401 so it is not an oracle, and deliberately NO alert email (an email-bomb primitive). **R5 UPLOAD ORDERING**: a pre-parse gate so a throttled — or wholly ANONYMOUS — request no longer costs 41MB of buffering, refusing with `Connection: close` rather than a socket destroy. (v2.99.46 — PROCESS FIX: the gate that let a broken commit reach `main`. v2.99.45 was pushed with UNRESOLVED merge-conflict markers in three files (`shared/version.ts`, `client/src/app/updateChecker.test.ts`, `CLAUDE.md`) — typecheck, four test files and the production build all broken. ROOT CAUSE: the pre-push command was `pnpm check 2>&1 | tail -2 && pnpm test … && pnpm build …` — a shell pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's, so `tail` (always 0) masked the failing typecheck and `&&` continued to the push. Any `gate | head/tail/grep && next` reads as a passing gate, so two durable guards replace "remember not to do that": (1) **`pnpm verify`** = `pnpm check && pnpm test && pnpm build` as ONE package script — no pipe to insert, so the gates cannot be decoupled from their exit codes by how the command is typed at the call site; (2) **`server/repoHygiene.test.ts`** — a tripwire failing the SUITE on a stray `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` line in any tracked text file (ts/tsx/js/json/md/css/html/yml/sql/sh/kt/java; node_modules, dist, build, coverage, mobile native dirs skipped), because the typecheck only covers compiled sources — CLAUDE.md's markers passed every existing gate — while the suite is the one gate every workflow runs. One turned out WRONG on inspection and is recorded as a refutation. **(1) M45 — MODERATOR POWERS OUTLIVED MEMBERSHIP**: `knock-approve` gated only on `isModerator(meta, pin)`, but it takes `roomId` from the CLIENT and `roomMeta` outlives membership (the roster is add-only; nothing clears `hostPin`/`cohosts` on leave), so a FORMER host who hung up could name the old room and admit an outsider into a call they had left. It CHAINED with `kick`: `leaveRoom` only drops membership and never touched `meta.cohosts`, so a KICKED CO-HOST kept their role, could knock, and could then APPROVE THEMSELVES BACK IN — the kick was undoable by its own target. VERIFIED against the real artifact (zero dev-only top-level imports) AND that dev still boots (react-refresh preamble, `/src/main.tsx` 200). **R7 GAP1 — A NEW MESSAGE NEVER WOKE AN OFFLINE RECIPIENT'S DEVICE**: a missed call has pushed since v2.83 and a voicemail since v2.88, but a plain message only fanned an SSE hint — which by definition reaches only a tab that is already connected, i.e. exactly the case where the user does NOT need telling; a phone with RELAY installed and closed stayed silent until its owner happened to open the app. FIX: `messages.send` now pushes every OFFLINE recipient (`kind:"message"`, tag `relay-msg-<conversationId>` so ten messages REPLACE instead of stacking ten notifications, `url` deep-links the thread), content-free by the owner's standing rule — the sender's name, never a word of the body; a voicemail keeps its own better-worded push (no double-notify). **R7 GAP2 — NO USER-FACING PUSH SWITCH**: new `users.pushEnabled` (additive + nullable via the boot migrator, NULL/true = on) enforced INSIDE `sendPushToIdentity` and BEFORE the subscription lookup, so every push kind and every call site obeys it — including ones added later, which a per-call-site check is exactly the kind of thing to forget. Reads NULL as on and FAILS OPEN on DB trouble so it can never silence a ringing call; exposed via `otpAuth.get/setNotificationPrefs` and a "Push notifications" toggle in Profile (the section is now "Notifications" and renders for ANY signed-in account — the two EMAIL rows stay gated on a linked address). **R7 GAP3 — THE OFFLINE-MESSAGE EMAIL IS NOW A LAST RESORT**: this is the only mail RELAY sends that the recipient did not ask for (someone else's message triggers it), so the failure mode is an annoyed user and an SES sending reputation you do not get back. Four rules on top of the existing pref + atomic claim: (1) SKIPPED entirely when the recipient has a push subscription — they just got the notification above, so the email is pure noise; (2) requires them to have actually been away ≥5 min (`OFFLINE_MESSAGE_EMAIL_MIN_AWAY_MS`) because presence flips offline the moment a tab hides, so a phone that locks for ten seconds mid-conversation would otherwise earn an email for a message its owner is already reading; (3) cooldown 15 min → 60 min, and the copy COALESCES by design ("you have messages waiting", never a per-message count), so a burst is one accurate email; (4) a hard ceiling of 3 per UTC day. The cap is enforced by the claim's WHERE against the PRE-UPDATE row, so two concurrent claims at CAP-1 cannot both win. A REAL BUG in this release's own new code was caught in pre-merge review and fixed before shipping: the counter originally reset itself inside the claim (`SET count = IF(day <=> today, count + 1, 1), day = today`), leaning on MySQL's left-to-right SET evaluation so the IF would read the OLD day — but the emitted order is NOT ours to choose, because drizzle's `buildUpdateSet` walks the table's COLUMNS object (SCHEMA DECLARATION order), not the object literal passed to `.set()`, and `messageEmailDay` is declared before `messageEmailsToday`. The day was therefore written FIRST, the IF always saw `today`, and the counter never reset: 3 emails on day one, then exactly ONE per day forever, with the counter growing unbounded — and the first version of the test asserted the object-literal order, so it proved nothing. The fix is STRUCTURAL rather than a reorder: an idempotent day-rollover UPDATE (race-safe, since concurrent rollovers write identical values) followed by a claim whose SET is a pure increment, correct under ANY emitted order; the test now pins that property plus a behavioural guard on drizzle's dialect so a library upgrade cannot silently reintroduce the dependency. A FAILED send now returns BOTH the cooldown and the day's budget slot (`GREATEST(... - 1, 0)` floors the counter). Plus ONE-CLICK UNSUBSCRIBE THAT NEEDS NO LOGIN: new `server/unsubscribe.ts` mints `<userId>.<hmac>` (signed with the inbound-email secret family, so no new env var) and `/api/email/unsubscribe` accepts GET (a human clicking) and POST (RFC 8058 one-click, where the mail client submits it); the mail carries `List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers AND a visible footer link. The token is a NARROW capability — it can only turn message email OFF, never on, and reaches no other setting, so a leaked link costs at most one channel the user re-enables in Profile — and deliberately does NOT expire (mail lives in inboxes for years; an unsubscribe link that has quietly gone stale is what gets a sender reported as spam). Fails CLOSED with no secret configured. Custom headers are threaded through `sendEmail` → `smtpSend` → `buildMimeMessage` behind a CR/LF + header-name guard (`extraHeaderLines`), so a header value can never inject another header or a body. A SECOND pre-merge finding: `/api/email/unsubscribe` MUTATED ON GET, and express answers HEAD from `app.get` — so a mail security gateway that fetches links found in mail to detonate them (Safe Links, Proofpoint, corporate AV) would have silently unsubscribed the recipient before they ever opened the message, which is exactly what RFC 8058's one-click POST exists to prevent. GET is now READ-ONLY (it verifies the token and renders a confirm page whose button POSTs — still no sign-in) and POST is the only writing path, leaving the RFC 8058 flow untouched; the form action is the only query value reaching the markup, is reached only after the token verified, and is escaped regardless, and the POST gets its own per-IP limiter + sweep. A 5-reviewer adversarial pass over this release's own diff then found FIVE MORE real defects in the new code, all fixed before merge: (a) PUSH OFF ⇒ NEITHER PUSH NOR EMAIL — nothing deletes the `push_subscriptions` row when the switch is turned off, so "has a subscription" was the wrong stand-in for "reachable" and push-off + message-email-on produced silence on both channels; new `pushReachable()` requires a live subscription AND the switch on. (b) THE FAILED-SEND ROLLBACK WAS DEAD CODE (pre-existing since v2.99.19): `sendEmail` never throws and resolves `{ok:false}`, so the `.catch()` never fired and a refused SES send kept the claim — it inspects `r.ok` now. (c) THE UNSUBSCRIBE URL NEVER REACHED text/plain, because the default `stripHtml(html)` deletes anchors together with their hrefs — a hand-written `messageWaitingText()` now carries both URLs. (d) MUTE AND DND WERE BYPASSED: both are per-DEVICE localStorage settings enforced in the page, which was enough only while every alert originated in an open tab — a push reaches the OS directly, and `conversationParticipants.mutedUntil` exists but is never written, so the server cannot know; fixed at the SERVICE WORKER (per-device, like the settings), with the page mirroring `{dnd, muted[]}` into Cache Storage (new `client/src/app/swPrefs.ts`) and `sw.js` parsing the conversation id off the `relay-msg-<id>` tag, failing OPEN and never letting a per-conversation mute suppress a call. (e) THE DEV SERVER STARTED SERVING `.git/**` AND `*.pem` — handing vite the config path made the file's `server.fs.deny` actually apply (the inline server block used to replace it), and `mergeWithDefaults` ASSIGNS arrays, so `["**/.*"]` replaced vite's four defaults; picomatch only matches a dotted LAST segment, so `.git/config` (credentials in its remote URL) and `key.pem` fell through — verified against picomatch directly and the list is now complete. Also `vite.config.ts` had fallen out of the tsc program (the static import was what pulled it in), so type errors there escaped both `pnpm check` and the build; it is in tsconfig `include` now. `server/roundsGaps.test.ts` (41 — including a real assertion against the BUILT `dist/index.js`, the SET order-independence property, a BEHAVIOURAL proof that drives the real express app and counts writes (GET → 0 + a form, HEAD → 0, POST → 1, tampered → 400 and 0), unsubscribe round-trip/tamper/no-secret, and header injection); three v2.99.13 pins in `emailNotifyPrefs.test.ts` updated to the tightened shapes. NO OPS REQUIRED. 1666 tests.) (v2.99.41 — HARDENING PASS 7: the class sweep COMPLETED (14/14 classes, 55 adversarial verdicts — 51 refuted, 4 upheld), and its last wave plus the panel's survivors are fixed here. **(1) ReDoS on the inbound-email webhook — the panel's highest-confidence new finding**: `parseInboundAddress` ran `/<([^>]+)>/` against an untrusted header value with NO length cap on a route that accepts 5MB of JSON. On input containing a `<` but no `>` the engine retries `[^>]+` from every `<` and gives back one character at a time — quadratic, ~10^13 steps for 5MB. Node is single-threaded and this process serves every SSE stream, signaling POST and API call, so ONE request stalls calls and messaging for EVERY user, and the webhook signature check is opt-in so it can be unauthenticated. Capped at 1024 bytes before the match (RFC 5321 caps an addr-spec at 320), which bounds n instead of relying on a cleverer pattern. **(2) `region` was still spliced raw into the SSM remote commands** — a GAP IN MY OWN EARLIER FIX: G11 base64'd `SES_EMAIL` and `DOMAIN` but missed `region`, the THIRD free-text `workflow_dispatch` input on the same path, which was still interpolated unescaped into all five command strings executed on production EC2. Same treatment applied; its other uses run on the runner via safe single-pass substitution and are deliberately untouched. **(3) sign-out never revoked the session ledger row** (upheld by the panel, traced end to end): v2.99.1 built a revocable session model and `createContext` gates every sid-bearing cookie on it, but `auth.logout` only cleared COOKIES — so the row stayed ACTIVE, the device kept appearing in the user's own Devices list as a live session, and the token itself stayed valid, so a copy recovered from a synced profile, a disk backup or a shared machine would still authenticate. "Log out" now means the credential stops working; wrapped so a DB hiccup can never prevent the cookies being cleared. **(4) the media-proxy limiter was too tight for shared egress** (an availability finding, not a vuln): 240 burst / 4-per-second is per-IP, and carrier CGNAT, an office or a café put many real users behind ONE address — on an image-heavy chat a few people scrolling together could exhaust it, and a throttled media request renders as a BROKEN IMAGE, the exact symptom this project has chased repeatedly. Raised to 600 / 20-per-second, which still caps a scraper two orders of magnitude below unlimited; the guard's real target is DB-CPU cost on the miss path, not enumeration (keys carry a random suffix and cannot be guessed). VERIFIED AND DOWNGRADED after independent checking: the Android `release { signingConfig signingConfigs.debug }` line is a real footgun but NOT a live compromise — `native-rn.yml` re-signs the AAB with a real keystore from `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` after the build, so the store artifact is properly signed; recorded as an operator note rather than changed blind. LEFT TO THE OPERATOR (cannot be fixed from the repo, and guessing would break the deploy): the deploy OIDC role trusts `repo:…:*`, so a workflow on ANY branch can assume the production deploy role — that is an AWS IAM trust-policy edit; and `deploy.yml` pins third-party actions to mutable major tags in the job that holds production credentials — pinning needs verified SHAs. `hardeningPass6.test.ts` grows to 35, including a bounded-regex timing check and per-command assertions on the region fix. 1638 tests.) (v2.99.40 — HARDENING PASS 6: the class sweep's later-reporting classes. **(1) HIGH — the 4-try PIN lockout was bypassable by CONCURRENCY**: `attemptPinLogin` gated on `row.loginPinLockedAt` — a field from a snapshot the CALLER had already read — and then ran `verifyPassword` regardless of the row's LIVE state. So N simultaneous requests all saw an unlocked row, all passed the gate, and all got a PIN checked; the S1 fix had made the COUNTER race-free but never bounded how many VERIFICATIONS could occur, so the cap wasn't actually enforced per attempt and a burst could sweep much of the 10^4 space, held back only by the per-IP bucket. Inverted: every attempt must now WIN a slot from the DB first (`UPDATE … WHERE lockedAt IS NULL AND attempts <= cap`, verdict from `affectedRows`) and only a winner may verify — MySQL serializes it per row, so at most cap+1 verifications can ever happen between unlocks, regardless of concurrency or instance. The ladder is unchanged (the 4th try is still verified, so a correct 4th still succeeds; a wrong 4th latches the lock via its own `isNull`-guarded UPDATE, which also owns sending the alert email exactly once). The pure `judgePinAttempt` helper is test-only and now says loudly that it must never gate a login. **(2) HIGH — an unsolicited `video-accept` forced a peer's camera ON**: `onVideoAccept` checked nothing but `inCall`, so any call peer could send that frame and run `unlockApprovedVideo()` on the victim — a total bypass of the v2.81 mutual-consent protocol, whose whole promise is that a camera transmits only after BOTH sides agree; the victim's only notice was a cheerful "Video is on — both sides 🎥" toast, and on a party line one frame could do it to everyone. `videoReqT` alone was not a usable guard: a VIDEO DIAL answered with the Video button also replies `video-accept`, and there the caller consented implicitly by dialing (no request was ever sent), while `outgoingDial` is cleared at establishment though consent frames often arrive before the transport exists. New per-call `videoOfferedByUs` flag set at BOTH consent points and cleared by the existing per-call reset; an unsolicited accept is dropped SILENTLY so it reveals nothing. **(3) HIGH — attacker-chosen `Content-Type` served same-origin**: the storage proxy relays the stored (uploader-supplied) type verbatim, and `nosniff` means the DECLARED type is obeyed — so the upload denylist was the only defence, over an allowlist admitting `text/*` and `application/*` WHOLESALE. The entire XML family was missing (`text/xml`, `application/xml`, `text/xsl`, `application/xslt+xml` — XML carrying SVG/XHTML namespaces with a `<script>` executes in some browsers, the exact outcome `image/svg+xml` is blocked for), as were the other JavaScript media types. Fixed at BOTH layers: the denylist covers those families, AND the proxy now serves only an inline-safe set as itself, downgrading anything else to `application/octet-stream` + `Content-Disposition: attachment` — robust without enumerating every dangerous type, and matching how the client already presents attachments. **(4) `auth.me` shipped the caller's CREDENTIAL HASHES to the browser**: `getUserById` does an unprojected `select()`, so the handler serialized the entire `users` row — scrypt `passwordHash` AND `loginPinHash` — into every response, where it lives in the React Query cache, devtools/HAR captures and anything an extension can read. Self-only, so not cross-user disclosure, but it converts any read-only client foothold (an XSS like #1 of v2.99.37, a malicious extension) into offline cracking — and the PIN hash covers 10^4, which does not survive a trivial offline attack. Stripped as a denylist so no client-consumed field can vanish. **(5) the signaling OFFLINE dial was the last unthrottled number→identity oracle AND a third-party spam amplifier**: its replies differ by design ("<Name> is offline right now." vs "That number doesn't exist."), leaking existence and display name across the 10^6 space, and each pass also writes a History row and fires a missed-call push AND email — with no cooldown, unlike the offline-MESSAGE email. The tRPC resolvers were gated for exactly this (F5), but this path never was, and the signaling limiter is a ~200/s FLOOD guard a scraper stays under (full enumeration in under two hours). New per-caller-pin `offlineDialLimiter` (20 burst, ~1/4s) scoped ONLY to the offline branch — a dial to an ONLINE user never reaches it, so normal calling and group dials are untouched, which is why this avoids the previously-rejected idea of capping invites generally; the throttled reply is the GENERIC offline message and returns before resolving anything or recording a miss. **(6) `identity.regenerateNumber` had no throttle** — the M21 sibling: each call permanently claims another of ~980,000 numbers and the old one is never recycled, so one authenticated account could drain the shared space and break allocation for every future signup; now behind the same mint budget. New `hardeningPass6.test.ts` (22) + M36 coverage in `hardeningPass5.test.ts` incl. a simulation proving a 10,000-request burst yields exactly cap+1 verifications; 3 stale pins retargeted. 1582 tests.) Down it shows you message. Put the PIN number. Put verified beside his name. If he has a status. I needed to redesign and make it very flexible for the eyes, NOT compact — the current design is compact. So act, think professional as perfect designer."). THE ROW (`client/src/pages/app/Messages.tsx`, the whole v2.99.33 4-button block replaced): a 60px avatar as its OWN button (status ring → story viewer / profile, presence LED) + exactly TWO text lines inside ONE tap target — LINE 1 `NAME` at 19px (bold when unread) + a caption-less tier mark + the time pushed right (`ms-auto`); LINE 2 `[muted] PIN(NNN-NNN) · preview` — or "typing" with three pulsing dots — `· N new`. A 5-dimension multi-agent audit (24 agents, every acquire/release path adversarially verified) found a CLUSTER of causes, all fixed: **(a) THE WEDGE (the actual reported symptom)** — the red End button is wired to `endActiveLine()`, which deliberately SKIPS `hangUp()` (the ONLY function that releases capture) whenever `heldRoomId` is set and waits for the server's `resumed`. `onResumed` never cleared `heldRoomId` (it was written for `swapCall`, which re-sets it itself), so after ONE end-and-resume `heldRoomId === roomId`; the NEXT End tap took the silent branch, the server's `promoteHeldRoom` found no held room and replied NOTHING, and the engine wedged: `inCall` stayed true, `localStream` + pipeline stayed captured (indicator lit), End became a permanent no-op, and a new dial was blocked (`programmaticDial` requires `!inCall`). FIX: `onResumed` clears a stale `heldRoomId`; `endActiveLine` arms a 4s fail-closed fallback (`END_ACTIVE_RESUME_MS`) that forces `dropHeld() + hangUp()` if no `resumed` arrives; the SERVER now always answers `end-active` (`error{nohold}` when it promotes nothing) and the client completes the hang-up on that reply. **(b) IDLE HOLD** — `primeMedia()` acquired camera+mic at login and deliberately KEPT them ("we warm the stream and keep it ready"), so the devices were captured the whole time the app was open with NO call, lighting the indicator and blocking every other tab/app. It now warms only the PERMISSION (acquire → immediately `stop()`); the grant persists so an in-call `ensureMedia()` still never prompts. **(c) ORPHANED ACQUISITIONS** — `ensureMedia`/`flipCamera`/`reacquireCameraForPublish`/`recoverDeadLocalTrack` all installed a stream AFTER an await with no staleness check, so a call ending mid-acquisition stranded a live capture nothing could stop. New monotonic `mediaGen` (bumped on every release) + `mediaStale(gen)`/`stopStream()`: each path captures the generation before awaiting and stops the fresh stream if it changed; `ensureMedia` also dedupes concurrent callers through one in-flight promise (concurrent calls used to double-acquire and orphan the loser). **(d) ONE RELEASE PATH** — new `releaseLocalMedia(reason)` (stops tracks + destroys the pipeline + clears the self-preview `srcObject`) is used by hang-up, engine destroy (which never destroyed the pipeline before), and a new backgrounded-while-idle sweep. **(e) VOICE-NOTE MIC** — `voiceNote.ts` only stopped its stream inside `rec.onstop`, so a MediaRecorder construct/start throw left the mic open with no handle; both are now guarded, and `Messages`/`VoicemailPrompt` cancel the recording if they unmount during the acquisition await or mid-record. **(2) IN-CALL UI (owner screenshot)**: the ⋯ **More** button, its overflow menu and the **Diagnostics** floater + overlay panel are REMOVED; **Record** survives promoted into the control bar as a normal labeled chip (still hidden unless recording is configured). The internal `diag()` event log is kept for console debugging; the `?` shortcut and all dead CSS are gone. **(3) DIALER (owner screenshot)**: the preview sub-line was a FIXED `h-4` (16px) row while `RoleBadge` stacks its caption (~22px), so the badge overflowed and collided with the keypad — it is now a two-line block (name + caption-less mark with the tier word INLINE on line 1, presence on line 2, new exported `roleLabel()`); tapping a key now plays a real **DTMF dual tone** (new `client/src/lib/dtmf.ts`, the genuine telephony frequency pairs, output-only so it can never hold the mic, also on hardware-keyboard digits, context closed on unmount); and the "Save … to contacts" pill is no longer clipped by the tab bar (own `shrink-0` row + the card can scroll as a safety valve). The v2.97.2 stopgap let `otpAuth.register` skip minting/emailing an OTP and sign the caller in immediately (email ownership unproven) while SES was sandboxed.
