(v2.99.38 — HARDENING PASS 5 pt.2: the remaining class-sweep findings. **(1) HIGH — `RELAY_OTP_REGISTER_BYPASS` was unauthenticated account TAKEOVER, not just unproven signup**: the bypass branch of `otpAuth.register` (a `publicProcedure` whose whole input is a name + an email) called `findUserByEmailAny` and signed the caller in as WHATEVER IT RESOLVED — so with the flag on, anyone who knew a registered user's email got a full session as them, no code and no password. The accepted trade for this SES-outage stopgap was "email ownership isn't proven AT SIGNUP"; taking over EXISTING accounts was never part of it. The branch is now CREATE-ONLY: it refuses (CONFLICT) when the address already has an account and only ever mints a new one, which preserves the flag's actual purpose. Signing in remains `requestOtp`/`loginWithPin`, both of which still demand a real credential. **(2) HIGH — `BLOCKED_MIME` bypass via a multi-valued Content-Type**: `ALLOWED_MIME` and `BLOCKED_MIME` are both START-ANCHORED, so they only ever inspected the FIRST type in the client-supplied `?mime=` string — `image/png,text/html` passes ALLOWED (starts with `image/`) and misses BLOCKED (doesn't start with a blocked type). That value was stored and replayed verbatim as the `Content-Type` of a same-origin response, i.e. the stored-XSS shape `BLOCKED_MIME` exists to prevent, since header parsers disagree about which listed type wins. New exported `normalizeMimeType` reduces to a canonical `type/subtype` essence (params dropped, case-folded) and demands exactly one RFC-2045-token media type — no commas, no whitespace — applied at BOTH mimeType sources before any gate or storage write. **(3) account DIVERSION (the other half of M29)**: `/api/auth/register`'s `findLocalUserByEmail` matches only rows that HAVE a passwordHash, so it is blind to OAuth/otp accounts and inserted a SECOND `users` row for the same email. `findUserByEmailAny` ranks a `local` row ABOVE a legacy OAuth row, so the victim's email code then signed them into the attacker's empty row — and with the OAuth UI removed in v2.92, the email code is their ONLY way in, so their real account (number, contacts, history) became unreachable. New `findAnyUserByEmail` refuses registration when ANY row already holds the address; the unverified-local resend path is untouched. **(4) gzip amplification on `/api/v2/upload`**: body-parser inflates encoded request bodies by default and enforces `limit` against the DECOMPRESSED stream, so the 41MB ceiling held but the attacker's cost to reach it collapsed ~1000x (tens of KB of compressed zeros → 41MB buffered) — compounding the known ordering weakness that this route's rate limit runs INSIDE the handler, after buffering. `inflate: false` on both upload parsers; no client compresses an upload body, so it costs nothing. **(5) the storage-proxy rate limiter was never swept** — every other limiter in the codebase pairs itself with a periodic sweep, but this one shipped without one, so its per-IP Map grew for the process lifetime on the app's only fully anonymous, high-fan-out endpoint. `hardeningPass5.test.ts` grows to 59 (incl. behavioral `normalizeMimeType` coverage of the real bypass payloads). 1555 tests.) (v2.99.37 — HARDENING PASS 5: CLASS-BASED SECURITY SWEEP (owner: "make sure that you cover all type of security bugs... I want the system to be very perfect"). The four prior passes audited SURFACE BY SURFACE; this one audited by VULNERABILITY CLASS (injection, XSS, authz/IDOR, CSRF, SSRF, upload/path, crypto, race/TOCTOU, DoS/ReDoS, business-logic, info-disclosure, client-trust, deps, CI), which is what surfaced these. 10 fixed, every one verified against source before any change. **(1) HIGH — zero-click DOM XSS in the in-call chat** (`relayClient.ts`): a chat frame's `pin` arrives over the peer's DATA CHANNEL and was validated with nothing but `typeof d.pin === "string"`, then interpolated into the message row's `innerHTML` twice unescaped — once inside the double-quoted `data-pin="…"` ATTRIBUTE, and once through `fmtPin`, which returns a non-matching string UNCHANGED. A peer sending `pin: 'x"><img src=x onerror=…>'` broke out and executed on parse, with no click or hover, on our own origin — i.e. full session takeover (drive the authenticated API as the victim). Reachable by anyone who can share a call, INCLUDING a party line (joinable by number), so one frame could hit every participant. Fixed by validating to `/^\d{6}$/` (a pin is always six digits) rather than merely escaping — the same check `ensureChatAvatar` already did, which just ran AFTER the markup was written; `initials()` sinks on the chat chip, call tiles, and recents are escaped too. **(2) HIGH — account pre-hijacking → takeover**: the unauthenticated legacy route `POST /api/auth/register` creates a `loginMethod:"local"` user with an ATTACKER-chosen `passwordHash` and `emailVerified:false` for ANY email. When the real owner later signs in with an email code, `findUserByEmailAny` deliberately falls back to that `local` row (v2.92 compat), and `markUserEmailVerified` flipped it verified while LEAVING the attacker's password in place — after which `/api/auth/login` (password + verified) handed the attacker a session on the victim's account. New `clearUnverifiedCredentials(userId)` destroys any password/PIN on a still-UNVERIFIED row at the moment the address is proven, called before `markUserEmailVerified` at BOTH claim sites; scoped to unverified rows, so a legitimate local user who verified via their own link keeps their password. **(3) view-once lock bypass** — `getAttachmentForIdentity` authorized a non-uploader via ANY referencing message, including a still-LOCKED expiring one (its `attachmentId` is only nulled at burn). Since that one function backs `attachments.get` (sequential integer ids — just enumerate), `authorizeStorageKey`, AND `messages.send`'s ownership check, a recipient could read view-once media repeatedly WITHOUT burning it (sender never told it was seen) and even RE-ATTACH it to a new permanent message elsewhere, laundering content meant to vanish. Locked expiring messages no longer authorize; the uploader's early return keeps senders unaffected. **(4) MySQL left-to-right UPDATE assignment broke BOTH attempt ladders**: MySQL documents that a later SET assignment reads the value an earlier one just wrote, so the lock CASE saw `attempts` ALREADY incremented and the extra `+ 1` double-counted. The PIN row locked on the THIRD wrong entry, not the fourth — and the persisted count could then only reach 3 while the brute-force alert email requires exactly 4, so **that email was UNREACHABLE and an owner was NEVER told their account was under attack**. Same defect burned the email OTP a guess early. **(5) `startGuest` was an unauthenticated, unthrottled identity MINTER** — the only resource-creating public endpoint with no gate. Each call permanently claims one of ~980,000 six-digit numbers: `numberTaken` treats mere row existence as taken (ignores guest expiry), nothing deletes identities, and M20's reservation ledger is monotonic. Drained far enough, `allocateSharedNumber`'s 40-attempt search fails for EVERYONE and every new guest, registration, and party line dies with "could not allocate a unique 6-digit number" — a permanent, unauthenticated DoS on all onboarding. Added `guestMintGate`. **(6) `revealExpiring` buffered an unbounded body** — the guard was `Number(content-length ?? 0) <= CAP`, so a MISSING header yielded 0, PASSED, and went into `arrayBuffer()` with no ceiling (the later `buf.length` check was too late); base64 then added 33% inside a JSON response. Now a named `REVEAL_MAX_INLINE_BYTES` enforced against the STREAM, so a missing or lying header can't exceed it. **(7) view-once burn was not atomic** — both burn paths did read → check `consumedAt` in JS → write with an await between, so two concurrent reveals both returned the content (same lost-update class as the S1/S9 races). Now one conditional UPDATE guarded on `JSON_EXTRACT(meta,'$.consumedAt') IS NULL`, verdict from `affectedRows`. **(8) `avatarUrl` accepted arbitrary `http(s)://`** — a profile photo became a remote-fetch primitive aimed at other users, and it renders on the INCOMING-RING card, which appears with NO interaction: set an avatar to your own host, dial a victim, harvest their IP + User-Agent from a call they never answered. Same threat the status-background sanitizer already rejects `url()` for, and squarely against this app's no-tracing goal; restricted to our own storage path or `data:image/` (zero compat cost — clients only ever set it from our upload endpoint). **(9) `status.post` skipped its `keyInOwnerNamespace` gate for `kind:"text"`** while still persisting `mediaKey`. Since `authorizeStorageKey` resolves a `/status_` key via whichever ACTIVE status claims it, planting another user's key re-activated their EXPIRED or DELETED status media — readable again by the planter and re-exposed to the planter's audience, defeating the ephemerality guarantee. Gate now applies to any supplied key, and a text status never persists media. **(10) `tryReserveNumber` detected a duplicate key by ERROR-MESSAGE TEXT** in a helper that fails OPEN, so a driver upgrade or localized server would silently turn every lost race into "reservation won", reintroducing the cross-table number collision the ledger exists to prevent; now keys on errno 1062 / ER_DUP_ENTRY with the text sniff only as a fallback. VERIFIED CLEAN this pass (documented negatives): no SQL injection (every `sql` template parameterizes values and uses Drizzle column refs for identifiers); landing-page `innerHTML` escaping intact after the v2.99.35 React-19 rework (`escLp` covers all five chars, applied post-composition, all sinks text-context); secret comparisons consistently `timingSafeEqual` with length guards; CSRF genuinely defended by `SameSite=Lax` on every cookie (the `/api/v2/offline` beacon's cookie path can't fire cross-site, and its deviceId fallback needs a secret); `keyInOwnerNamespace` correctly anchored (the trailing slash defeats the 1-vs-12 prefix collision) and the absolute-URL avatar suffix-match fix unexploitable; `searchMessages` filters expiring content; `tabPresence` stores no secrets and fails safe. ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: `push.subscribe`'s upsert is keyed on the globally-unique `endpoint`, so knowing a victim's endpoint lets you re-bind it and silently kill their notifications — but no API ever returns an endpoint, the hijacker gains nothing readable (pushes are encrypted to their own keys), and the only correct fix is a proof-of-possession challenge; naively refusing re-binds would break the documented account-switch-on-same-device flow, silently killing notifications for real users. Prior-round residuals unchanged. `hardeningPass5.test.ts` (44, incl. a real arithmetic simulation of MySQL assignment order and the XSS payloads the pin guard must reject); 4 stale pins updated. 1540 tests.) (v2.99.36 — LANDING POLISH, three owner asks (screenshot + notes). **(1) ARABIC "OPEN APP" ICON MISSING**: the pill's copy carried a bare `↗` (U+2197). The v2.99.16 RTL rule forces `Noto Kufi Arabic` on EVERY element in Arabic and that face has no U+2197, so iOS fell through to the emoji font and drew a boxed ↗️ beside the Arabic label. FIX: the arrow is now an inline SVG (`ARROW_NE`) that renders identically in every language/font/platform, mirrored in RTL (`.lp-arrow{transform:scaleX(-1)}`) so it still points outward. A SECOND instance of the SAME defect was found while pinning the fix — the CALL button label also ended in `↗` and is NOT inside a `dir="ltr"` island, so in Arabic it rendered the identical emoji box; `setCallState` gained an `arrow` flag that keeps the label as `textContent` (localized copy) and appends the CONSTANT SVG via `insertAdjacentHTML` (no interpolation ⇒ no injection surface). ZERO raw U+2197 now reaches the DOM (verified on the live page: `document.body.innerText` contains none). **(2) ERASE KEY ON THE DIAL PAD** (owner: "make delete number icons so if you enter you can erase it"): an erase key now occupies the keypad's bottom-right cell, replacing `#` — pure decoration here, since the pad only accepts 0-9 for a 6-digit RELAY number and `#` did nothing but play a tone. It dims to .35 when there is nothing to erase, erases one digit per tap, and no-ops when empty. A REAL BUG was caught mid-build and fixed: the first implementation put the button beside the number display (absolute, `inset-inline-end`) — in English it covered the 6th placeholder dot and in ARABIC, where it mirrors to the leading edge, it landed ON TOP of the first digit (the display is too wide to share that row). Moving it into the grid removes the overlap by construction and gives a full 54px touch target. **(3) AUDIBLE KEY TONES**: DTMF existed but was effectively silent for two reasons, both fixed — the oscillators were scheduled at `ac.currentTime` in the SAME tick as the ASYNC `ac.resume()`, so on iOS the note's start time had already elapsed by the time the context ran (classic iOS Web Audio race), and the peak gain was 0.045 (≈ -27 dBFS). Now the context is unlocked on the first real gesture (1-sample silent buffer on `pointerdown`), a suspended context resumes and THEN schedules, every note starts at a +5ms lookahead so it can never be scheduled in the past, and the peak is 0.18; erase gets its own softer low tone (420/310Hz). HONEST LIMIT documented in-source: on iPhone the hardware mute switch silences Web Audio outright — no web page can override that. Verified headlessly on an emulated phone against the REAL built bundle: exactly 2 oscillators per keypress at the correct DTMF frequencies, peak 0.18, ZERO notes scheduled in the past, the iOS unlock buffer firing on first touch; the erase key overlapping neither the display nor any key in EITHER language; all 10 digit keys registering correctly in Arabic (a single earlier miss was proven a synthetic-tap artifact of the pad's 3D tilt — correct 5/5 by coordinate, by raw touchscreen, and 10/10 by direct dispatch). `server/v29936LandingPolish.test.ts` (15 tests). 1495 tests.) (v2.99.35 — LANDING PAGE STRUCTURALLY ALIVE (owner: "the dial pad… if you click, doesn't click. The numbers doesn't show… the Arabic tab is not active"). ROOT CAUSE traced live with an instrumented `Element.innerHTML` setter, not guessed: React 19 re-applies `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` whenever the `{__html}` OBJECT identity changes — even for a byte-identical string. `Home.tsx` passed an inline `{{__html: html}}` (fresh object every render), so the first unrelated re-render — the live-stats query resolving ~0.5s after mount — re-set innerHTML on the live DOM, rebuilding EVERY node and silently discarding all of the engine's listeners (keypad, CLEAR, DEMO, CALL, the AR/EN toggle) while the `[lang]`-keyed wiring effect saw no change and never re-ran; the pure-CSS watchdog then cleared the orphaned boot overlay, so visitors saw a normal load into a dead page (empirical timeline: engine wired t≈450ms, DOM replaced t≈565ms, same string hash / new object). This is also why the v2.99.24 "wire controls first" hardening didn't cure the symptom — the controls WERE wired; the nodes were thrown away afterward. FIX, three reinforcing layers: (1) the `{__html}` object is memoized (`dsih`) so its identity changes only when the markup truly does; (2) the wiring effect keys on `[lang, dsih]` so any future DOM swap re-wires in the same commit; (3) every dialer/lang click rides ONE DELEGATED listener on the stable host wrapper (never replaced — only its children are) instead of per-node listeners. The v2.99.15 live number-lookup + v2.99.21 RTL binding + v2.99.24 ordering all survive unchanged on top. POLISH found while verifying: `dialStatus` sat on "CHECKING NUMBER…" forever next to a RESOLVED `dialPreview` ("Sara · ONLINE") — the status line now hides while a resolved preview shows, and the fail-open (FALLBACK) paths flip it to "LINE READY" instead of a stale "checking". ALSO: `index.html` shipped a literal `%VITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT%/umami` script whenever the env was unset (vite keeps unknown %VARS% verbatim) — every production load fetched the bogus URL, 400 + strict-MIME console error; tag removed, `main.tsx` injects analytics at runtime only when configured. (v2.99.34 — M11: SERVER-SIDE EPHEMERAL CONTENT GATING (the final heavy-QA-sweep item; owner: "finish the M11"). Previously `messages.list` returned the full `body` + `meta` + `attachment` (url + thumbUrl) for an UN-CONSUMED view-once/disappearing message, so a recipient reading the raw tRPC response (devtools) — or fetching `attachment.url` directly — saw the secret WITHOUT ever burning it; `consumeExpiringMessage` was the only thing that nulled the content and nothing forced it, so the "view once, then gone" guarantee was defeated with no tap (the casual Copy/Reply menu vectors were already shut in v2.99.23; this closes the raw-response vector). FIX (server): `list` now WITHHOLDS the content of a LOCKED message — `locked = isExpiring && !consumedAt && senderIdentityId !== me` → `body:null`, `attachment:null`, plus a `locked` flag to the client (the sender always sees their own; a consumed row is already null and renders "disappeared"). The ONLY path to the content is the new `revealExpiring` mutation → `revealExpiringMessage` (`server/v2db.ts`): same authorization as consume (participant, not the sender, not already consumed), it CAPTURES `body`+`attachmentId` then BURNS (nulls both + sets `consumedAt`, keeps the attachments row per F3), and the router INLINES the media as a `data:` URL (reads the object via `storageGetSignedUrl` server-side, ≤30MB, base64) so the immediate burn can't race a client fetch — the old client fetch-then-burn flow (`URL.createObjectURL` + a separate `consumeExpiring.mutate`) is RETIRED. Client (`Messages.tsx`): the tap-to-view card calls `revealExpiringMutation.mutateAsync` and renders `res.body`/`res.media.dataUrl` (a data URL survives the burn — no blob/revoke), and `burned` now keys on the server `locked` flag + `consumedAt` (empty content alone no longer reads as burned, so a withheld message correctly shows the tap-to-view card). `consumeExpiring` server endpoint is kept for back-compat. `server/m11ContentGating.test.ts` (8 pins); `qaSweepV29919.test.ts` #47 + `peerIdentityBatch.test.ts` v2.96 reveal pins updated to the M11 flow. (v2.99.32 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 10 (presence). **M12 (MED) CLOSING ONE OF TWO TABS FLIPPED THE IDENTITY OFFLINE**: presence is ONE boolean per identity, but every tab runs its own `PresenceManager` — so closing one of two open tabs of the same account fired `pagehide → sendBeacon /api/v2/offline → markOffline`, blinking the user offline to every contact, and then the surviving tab's next 30s heartbeat re-marked online (`becameOnline=true`) → a FALSE "X is back online — tap to call them now" push/toast to every watcher. FIX: a browser-scoped last-tab ref-count (new `client/src/app/tabPresence.ts`) — each tab records `tabId→ts` in a per-identity localStorage map on every VISIBLE heartbeat (`touchTab`), and `onLeave` only sends the offline beacon when no OTHER tab of the identity is fresh (`otherTabsAlive`, freshness `TAB_FRESH_MS`=45s > the 30s beat); a real close/unmount `removeTab`s its slot first. A single tab still beacons instantly (no regression to v2.89 instant-offline); localStorage is per-browser so it coordinates all tabs regardless of which fleet instance each tab's SSE hit; FAILS SAFE — any storage error → treated as "no other tab" → beacon fires (today's behaviour) and the 2-min server reaper stays the backstop. Pure decision helpers (`anyOtherTabFresh`/`pruneTabs`) are unit-tested. **L4 (LOW) REAPER SPURIOUS-OFFLINE TOCTOU**: `reapStalePresence` SELECTed the stale victims, then UPDATEd `isOnline=false WHERE isOnline=true AND lastSeenAt<cutoff` — a victim that HEARTBEAT back online between the two isn't flipped by the UPDATE (its lastSeenAt is fresh again) yet was still returned to the caller, which fanned a spurious "went offline" for a user who is actually online. FIX: after the UPDATE, re-confirm each candidate is genuinely `isOnline=false` now (`inArray(identityId, ids) AND isOnline=false`) and return only those; a re-check error falls back to the captured victims (pre-fix behaviour). `client/src/app/qaBatch10.test.ts` (9 pins incl. behavioural ref-count logic); `v2offline.test.ts` pins updated to the onClose/onVisibility restructure. (v2.99.31 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 9 (draft + auth edges). **M6 (MED) DRAFT LOST ON A FAST THREAD SWITCH**: `useDraft` (`client/src/app/draftStore.ts`) debounced the localStorage save 500ms, and its conversation-change effect cleanup `clearTimeout`'d the pending save WITHOUT flushing — so typing then switching threads (or unmounting) within 500ms silently dropped the draft, defeating the feature's whole "navigating away mid-draft doesn't lose it" purpose. FIX: a `flush()` (backed by `draftRef`/`convRef` so it writes the CURRENT text to the CORRECT conversation) runs in the `[conversationId]` cleanup instead of a bare clearTimeout, plus a `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` flush so a reload <500ms after typing also persists. **L2 (LOW) STALE "DECLINED" BOUNCED A RETRY**: `AuthPanel`'s new-device approval poll (`sessionApprovalStatus`) is a react-query with a stable key, so its cache survived the `enabled:false` toggle and remounts; after one attempt was DENIED on another device, retrying (a NEW pending session) had the waiting-stage effect served the CACHED `denied` immediately and bounced the user back to email with a false "declined" before the server ever evaluated the new session. FIX: `utils.otpAuth.sessionApprovalStatus.reset()` right before `setStage("waiting")`, so the effect only acts on a FRESH result. **L3 (LOW) DIGIT-CORRECTION BURNED OTP ATTEMPTS**: the code input auto-fires `verifyCode` the instant it hits 6 digits, and a wrong code left `code` populated (unlike the PIN path) — so deleting one digit and retyping re-fired and consumed one of the 5 server attempts PER single-character correction, exhausting a correct-but-fat-fingered user's budget. FIX: `setCode("")` in the wrong-code catch, so a correction is a fresh 6-digit entry = exactly one attempt. `client/src/app/qaBatch9.test.ts` (5 pins). (v2.99.30 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 8 (number-allocation races). **M20 (MED) CROSS-TABLE NUMBER COLLISION**: identities and party_lines share ONE 6-digit number space, and each table has its OWN `UNIQUE` key on `number` — but MySQL cannot enforce uniqueness ACROSS two tables, so `allocateNumber`/`allocatePartyLineNumber` (a check-then-insert: `numberTaken` SELECTs both tables, then the CALLER inserts) let two concurrent allocations targeting DIFFERENT tables both pass the gate and claim the SAME fresh number — both inserts then succeed (different tables, neither unique key fires) and the collision permanently SHADOWS a person (a dial resolves the party line first) or unreachables a line. FIX (`server/v2db.ts`): a new shared `number_reservations` ledger (boot-migrator `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `PRIMARY KEY (number)`); a new `allocateSharedNumber(db)` — used by BOTH allocators — runs `numberTaken` (pre-existing rows) THEN atomically `INSERT`s the candidate into the ledger via `tryReserveNumber` (dup-key → the loser retries a fresh candidate; ANY other error, incl. the table not existing on a first boot, FAILS OPEN → returns true → behaves EXACTLY as pre-ledger, so the per-table unique keys + numberTaken stay the backstop and the ledger can only ADD cross-table safety). The ledger is monotonic (never trimmed) so a handed-out number is never recycled — a deleted user's number can't later misroute to someone else. **L8 (LOW) PARTY-LINE CAP RACE**: `createPartyLine`'s per-owner cap was `owned.length >= MAX_PARTY_LINES_PER_OWNER` THEN insert (check-then-act), so two concurrent creates at count 9 both passed → an owner ended with 11. FIX: the fast pre-check stays (clean over-cap error in the common case), but the cap is now enforced deterministically AFTER the insert by the new row's id-RANK — `count(*) WHERE ownerIdentityId=? AND id <= insertId`; since id is monotonic and unique, concurrent racers get DISTINCT ranks, so exactly the rows ranked > MAX self-delete (each deletes only its OWN inserted id — no double-delete) and reject, converging to exactly MAX. `server/qaBatch8.test.ts` (5 pins); `partyLines.test.ts` allocator pins updated to the shared-allocator refactor. DEFERRED: rare leaked reservations on a post-reserve insert failure (900k space, cosmetic — no reaper). 1446 tests. QA-sweep progress: 27 of 37 fixed.) (v2.99.29 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 7 (status stories). **M15 (MED) VIDEO/AUDIO STATUS ALWAYS RAN 5s**: the story viewer's `itemMs` already honored `item.durationMs` for video/audio, but the COMPOSER never captured or sent a duration, so `durationMs` was always null and every media status auto-advanced at the flat 5s `DEFAULT_ITEM_MS` — a 30s video note flashed by in 5s while the `<video autoPlay>` kept playing under a finished progress bar. Copy is the only thing that was wrong-direction. FIX: poster-side copy now reads "visible for 24h to anyone who has you in their contacts" (enforcement unchanged — NO visibility change, purely corrective labeling). **L5 (LOW) PRESS-HOLD RESTARTED THE STORY**: the left/right tap-zone `<button>`s overlay the viewer body, and their `onClick` fired on release even after a press-and-HOLD (which sets `paused`), so holding to pause then releasing navigated — on the first item `prev()` just re-ran `resetTimer()`, reading as "holding restarts it". FIX: a `pressStartRef` stamped on `onPointerDown` (`Date.now()`); the tap zones navigate only when the press was a quick tap (`< HOLD_MS` = 220ms), so a hold pauses/resumes with no navigation. `client/src/pages/app/qaBatch7.test.ts` (5 pins). DEFERRED: none new. 1441 tests. QA-sweep progress: 25 of 37 fixed.) Keep them blocked instead if you just want them out of sight."), turning a silent unblock into an informed choice (the sanctioned "warn" fix; a server tombstone was considered but would leave an invisible forever-blocked row, surprising the user who chose "remove"). `server/qaBatch6.test.ts` (6 pins); `verifiedBadge.test.ts` contacts-role pin updated to the null shape. 1436 tests. (v2.99.27 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 5 (group-call invitee handling; all 9 HIGH findings shipped in v2.99.22–26, this is the MED/LOW tail). **M19 (MED) GROUP-PICKER OFF-BY-ONE**: the create-group-call picker used the TOTAL room cap (`engine.maxParticipants` = mesh 6 / SFU 10, which INCLUDES the caller) as the count of OTHERS to invite, so selecting the full cap rang one too many and the LAST acceptee hit a full room (`error{full}`). FIX: reserve the caller's slot — `MAX_PARTICIPANTS = max(1, engine.maxParticipants - 1)` in `GroupCallScreen.tsx` AND `cap = (livekitEnabled ? 10 : 6) - 1` in `programmaticGroupDial` (`relayClient.ts`). **L7 (LOW) PICKER ACCEPTED THE CALLER'S OWN NUMBER**: `toggle`/`addManual` didn't reject `engine.pin`, so the host could add themselves (silently dropped by the dial, but it burned an invitee slot at the cap); both now reject the own number. **M2 (MED) CALL-WAITING PARKED A DEAD DIAL ROOM**: answering a call-waiting invite DURING an UNANSWERED outgoing dial ran `parkActiveAsHeld()` on the empty dial room (no peer accepted) — nothing to resume, and the dialed party kept ringing into a room we'd left; Swap/Resume then entered a dead empty room. FIX (`switchCall`): when the current call is an unanswered outgoing dial (`outgoingDial && !establishedOnce`), CANCEL it (`leave` reaps the dial room + cancelPendingRings stops the outgoing ring) instead of parking it, then accept the incoming (no switch race — the leave targets the OLD dial room, the accept a DIFFERENT new room). `client/src/pages/app/qaBatch5.test.ts` (4 pins). DEFERRED: L1 (a group dial where EVERYONE declines hangs on "Ringing…" until the 65s backstop instead of failing instantly — needs outstanding-invitee tracking + real device testing). 1430 tests. QA-sweep progress: 19 of 37 fixed.) (v2.99.26 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 4 (storage-media). **H5 (HIGH) AVATAR LAUNDERING VIA AN ABSOLUTE URL**: `identity.updateProfile` ran the `keyInOwnerNamespace` ownership gate ONLY when `avatarUrl` was a RELATIVE `/manus-storage/…` path, but `isIdentityAvatarKey` (the `authorizeStorageKey` avatar-rescue) matches the key as a SUFFIX (`%/manus-storage/<key>`), so an ABSOLUTE `https://host/manus-storage/<victim-key>` avatarUrl slipped past the gate and, once stored, made the storage proxy serve ANOTHER user's private attachment (or burned view-once media) to anyone — the F2 gate's own comment wrongly assumed absolute URLs "never resolve through our proxy". FIX (`server/v2routers.ts`): validate the key after the LAST `/manus-storage/` (via `lastIndexOf`) so BOTH the relative and absolute shapes are gated; data:/external-CDN URLs (no `/manus-storage/`) are untouched. **M10 (MED) UNAUTHENTICATED STORAGE-PROXY DoS**: `/manus-storage/*` had no rate limit and each request could trigger an `identities` full-scan (the avatar rescue on an unindexed TEXT `avatarUrl`), so an anonymous loop over guessed `status_…`/`avatar_…` keys was an easy DB-CPU DoS. FIX (`server/_core/storageProxy.ts`): a per-IP token bucket (240 burst / ~4/s sustained — generous, since a chat screen legitimately bursts many images) runs BEFORE any key sanitize/authorize DB work and returns 429 on a flood; honors `RELAY_RATELIMIT_OFF`. `server/qaBatch4.test.ts` (2 source pins). 1426 tests. QA-sweep progress: 16 of 37 confirmed findings fixed (v2.99.22–26).) (v2.99.25 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 3 (three HIGH findings). **H9 (HIGH) LANDING LOOKUP ERRORS SHOWED "NO RELAY USER"**: the landing hero dialer's `onLookup` wrapper (`Home.tsx` React shell) ended in `.catch(() => null)`, so a `directory.lookup` ERROR (a shared-NAT `directoryGate` 429, a transient 500) resolved as `null` — indistinguishable from a genuine not-a-user — and the landing rendered "NO RELAY USER WITH THIS NUMBER" with CALL disabled for a REAL online user; `runLookup`'s documented fail-open `.catch` (→ `FALLBACK` → arm CALL → let `/i` re-resolve) was unreachable dead code. FIX: drop the `.catch(() => null)` so a real rejection propagates to `runLookup`'s fail-open (a genuine not-found still RESOLVES to null → correct "NO RELAY USER"; only true errors now fail open). **H4 (HIGH) STALE wasRegistration MISROUTED A LOGIN INTO A BROKEN SETUP SCREEN**: `AuthPanel`'s `wasRegistration` was set true by `submitRegister` and never reset, so a user who started a registration, went Back, then signed IN to an existing PIN-less account was routed by `verifyCode` into the "Finish setting up" screen — where `whoami` has no minted number and `setLoginPin`/`updateProfile` 401, stranding them. FIX: `setWasRegistration(false)` at the top of `routeAfterProbe` (the login-routing chokepoint, which always runs before `submitRegister` re-sets it true). **H6 (HIGH) HEARTBEAT RE-MARKED A HIDDEN TAB ONLINE**: `PresenceManager`'s 30s `tick` fired `heartbeat.mutate()` with NO visibility check, so after `onLeave` (visibilitychange→hidden) marked the user offline, the next tick re-marked them online (`becameOnline=true` → false "X is back online" pushes to every watcher) while the tab was still backgrounded. FIX: `tick` returns early when `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` (the visibilitychange handler already re-heartbeats on return to visible, so nothing is lost). `client/src/app/qaBatch3.test.ts` (4 source pins). 1424 tests.) (v2.99.24 — LANDING ROBUSTNESS: CONTROLS WIRED BEFORE THROWABLE INIT (owner: after clearing cache + reopening on a real phone, the landing "dial pad is not active" and the ع/EN language button "is not clickable"). NOT reproducible here — the exact DEPLOYED artifact (the strip-manus-runtime'd `index.html` + the real bundle) passes every headless Chromium check (desktop AND emulated phone with touch): keypad updates, toggle flips `.lp-root` to `dir=rtl` with the Noto Kufi Arabic font, no JS errors, no overlay, loader dismissed — and the sandbox network blocks ALL outbound hosts so the live site can't be loaded from here to diagnose directly. DEFENSIVE FIX regardless (`client/src/pages/Home.tsx` `startLanding`): the symptom (page renders but nothing is clickable) is the signature of the interactive wiring never attaching, so ALL interactive controls — keypad, Clear, Call, AND the language toggle — plus `syncDial()` are now wired FIRST, before any decorative/3D/audio/boot code; that decorative init (`onScroll`/`initReveals`/`initScramble`/`initMatrix`) and the boot/fx block (`fxLoop`/`runLoader`/`bootThree`) are each wrapped in try/catch, and a `dismissLoader()` on the boot-catch guarantees the opaque full-screen loader can never sit over the page swallowing taps if boot throws before it cleared. Previously `$("langBtn")` was wired AFTER `initReveals/Scramble/Matrix`, so a throw in any of those (a stricter/older browser's WebGL/AudioContext/rAF quirk) left the toggle dead. `Home.test.ts` +2 (ordering + try/catch pins). NOTE: this is a robustness hardening, not a confirmed root-cause fix — the live symptom still needs the owner's `https://your-chat.io/api/version` value (distinguishes "server not serving this build" from "browser can't run the JS"); the deployed CODE is verified sound. 1420 tests.) (v2.99.23 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 2 (ephemeral-message security). **H2 (HIGH) VIEW-ONCE EXTRACTABLE VIA THE MENU**: a still-LOCKED view-once/disappearing received message (`meta.expire` set, not yet tapped-to-reveal, not burned) exposed the plaintext through the received-message context menu — **Copy** wrote `m.body` straight to the clipboard and **Reply** surfaced it in the composer — and NEITHER called `consumeExpiring`, so the card never burned and the secret was re-copyable indefinitely. Compounding it, `replyingTo` omitted `meta`, so `previewOf`'s disappearing-guard was bypassed and the reply bar printed the raw body. FIX (`client/src/pages/app/Messages.tsx`): suppress the whole `!mine` menu while a message is `locked` (`isExpiring && !revealed.has(m.id) && !burned` → `return null`), so Copy/Reply only exist once the recipient has tapped to view (which burns it); and carry `meta` on `replyingTo` (type + setter + draft-reconstruct) so `previewOf` masks it to "⏱ Disappearing message" everywhere. **M3 (MED) GROUP DISAPPEARING BURNED FOR ALL**: a disappearing message in a GROUP is one shared row — the FIRST member to open it burns it for EVERYONE (the rest see "This message has disappeared"). Until per-recipient burn exists, the composer toggle is now gated to 1:1 (`!isGroup`), the convo-switch effect keeps `expire` null on entry, and the send path re-guards (`const exp = isGroup ? null : expire`). **M5 (MED) REPLY TARGET LEAKED ACROSS THREADS**: `replyingTo` wasn't reset on `conversationId` change, so a "Replying to Alice" banner from one thread persisted into the next and posted with the wrong `replyToId`; a `useEffect(..., [conversationId])` now clears it (the draft-reconstruct effect re-hydrates the new thread's own saved reply). `client/src/pages/app/qaBatch2.test.ts` (5 source pins). DEFERRED: M11 (full server-side content-gating-until-consume — needs a consume-to-reveal content-delivery redesign; the menu is now closed and `previewOf` masks, so the casual UI-extraction vector is shut). 1418 tests.) (v2.99.22 — HEAVY-QA SWEEP FIXES, BATCH 1 (the owner "activate the heavy QA" run: 57 agents, 43 candidates, 37 adversarially-verified confirmed; this batch takes the clearest HIGH findings). **H1 (HIGH) GROUP CALL COLLAPSED ON A DECLINE**: a group dial rings A/B/C off ONE room; while everyone rings, the caller's room is still size 1 (nobody accepted). The `reject` handler (`server/relay.ts`) reaped that size-1 non-party-line room via `leaveRoom` the instant ANY invitee declined — but `leaveRoom` doesn't `cancelPendingRings`, so B/C kept ringing with `pendingRings` pointing at a DELETED room and got `error{gone}` on accept, silently killing the whole conference over one decline (distinct from v2.99.19 #46, which was the OFFLINE-first-invitee client path). FIX: only reap when the caller is ringing NOBODY else — added `&& target.ringing.size === 0` (the decliner was already removed from `target.ringing` just above), so an in-progress group dial survives a decline. **H7/H8/M1 (HIGH) BLOCKED-CALLER MISSED-CALL BYPASS**: `onMissedCall` (`server/_core/index.ts`) recorded History + fired a "Missed call from B" push/email with NO block check — so a blocked caller's offline/declined dials were a repeatable push/email/history-injection channel (onInvite/onPageCallee already block-guard the live path; this one was missed). FIX: `if (await isNumberBlockedBy(callee.id, info.callerPin)) return;` at the top of the hook (fail-open on DB error). **H3 (HIGH) DEAD THREAD SEARCH**: the Messages thread-list `useMemo` filtered by `threadSearch` but omitted it from the dep array (`[threads.data, me]`), so typing re-rendered but returned the cached unfiltered list (threads.data is stable via structural sharing) — search did nothing. FIX: add `threadSearch` to the deps. **M8 (MED) PREMATURE SESSION LOGOUT**: the v2.99.19 session reaper's 95-day idle cutoff was shorter than the 365-day (`SESSION_TTL_MS`) default cookie, so a user idle 95–365 days had their session row reaped → `sessionState` read it as revoked → force-logged-out up to ~270 days early. FIX: raise the idle cutoff to 372 days (365 + 7 grace) so a row outlives every cookie it backs (corrects #51(d)). `server/qaBatch1.test.ts` (5 — behavioural relay tests for H1 + source pins). DEFERRED to later batches: H8's missed-call email THROTTLE (needs a cooldown column), and the remaining 33 findings (view-once menu leak, presence re-online, auth approval edges, etc.). 1413 tests.) (v2.99.21 — ARABIC TOGGLE ACTUALLY ACTIVATES (owner: "the Arabic language section, when you click the button, it's not active"). ROOT CAUSE — the v2.99.16 Arabic parity was DEAD ON ARRIVAL: all its CSS (`.lp-root[dir="rtl"] *{font-family:'Noto Kufi Arabic'…}` + the LTR-island monospace override) is scoped to `.lp-root[dir="rtl"]`, but `dir="rtl"` was only ever stamped on the INNER `[data-lp="root"]` div (a CHILD of `.lp-root`, `client/src/pages/Home.tsx` `markup()`), while the OUTER React `.lp-root` div had NO `dir` at all — so `.lp-root[dir="rtl"]` never matched, the Arabic font/sizing never applied, and Arabic rendered in the small fallback system face (also why the #40 "renders smaller" report was never truly fixed). FIX: bind `dir` on the `.lp-root` element itself — `<div className="lp-root" dir={lang === "ar" ? "rtl" : "ltr"}>` — so the toggle flips the whole page to RTL + the correct Arabic font. HEADLESS-VERIFIED in Chromium against the built bundle (desktop AND an emulated phone with touch): clicking the ع/EN toggle flips `.lp-root` `dir` `ltr→rtl`, switches the copy to Arabic, and the heading's COMPUTED `font-family` becomes `Noto Kufi Arabic` (was the fallback before); a hit-test confirmed NO overlay covers the controls and the boot loader is fully dismissed (`display:none`, `pointer-events:none`). The landing DIAL PAD was also verified working in BOTH English (`5 5 5 · · ·`) and Arabic (`7 8 9 · · ·` after the toggle re-renders the markup) — so the keypad + toggle are functional in the current bundle; a live "can't click anything" is a STALE CACHED BUNDLE (hard-refresh). `Home.test.ts` +2 (pins the `.lp-root` dir binding). NOTE: this rebased onto a parallel session's v2.99.20 hardening pass (version bumped to avoid the collision). 1408 tests.) (v2.99.20 — HARDENING PASS 4 (owner: "expose the security bugs... I want full backend and frontend" — the dedicated `claude-security` orchestrator was handed the whole app; every candidate it and a direct manual re-read of the full backend surfaced was independently verified against source before any fix). 11 confirmed and fixed: **(1) HIGH — storage-proxy key-normalization bypass**: `authorizeStorageKey` ran its exact-string DB match against the RAW request key, while `s3PresignGetUrl` silently normalized via `sanitizeS3Key` (collapsing `a//b`→`a/b`, stripping a leading `/`) at presign time — a real private attachment's key with an extra slash inserted missed the exact-match lookup (fell into the fail-open `unknown`/avatar classification) yet still resolved to, and served, the real object with no participant check; fixed by canonicalizing the key ONCE via `sanitizeS3Key` up front in `storageProxy.ts` so authorization and serving can never disagree about which object is being requested. **(2) `openThread`/`createGroup` block bypass** — either endpoint let a caller force a brand-new DM or group thread onto a target who had blocked them (blocking only stopped `messages.send`, not thread/group creation), pointless-ifying the block; both now check `isNumberBlockedBy` before creating a FRESH thread/group (existing threads predating a block are untouched) and respond identically to "not found" so the block itself is never revealed. **(3) `push.unsubscribe` IDOR** — deleted a push-subscription row by `endpoint` alone with no ownership check, so anyone who learned a victim's endpoint string could silently kill their incoming-call/missed-call notifications; now scoped to the caller's own identity via new `deleteOwnPushSubscription` (the unscoped helper stays for `webPush.ts`'s own dead-token cleanup, which has no identity context). **(4) `attachments.register` accepted an arbitrary client `url`** — pointing an attachment row at any external/`javascript:`/`data:` URL that every client (`AttachmentView`/`FileCard`/`MediaLightbox`) then trusted and rendered unchecked (no-interaction tracking beacon / phishing open-redirect); `url` is now always derived server-side from the already-namespace-validated `storageKey`, matching what `/api/v2/upload` produces. **(5) OAuth session secret fail-open** — `getSessionSecret()` silently signed/verified sessions with an empty key when `JWT_SECRET` was unset (the S10/S11 pattern applied to every OTHER secret, missed here); now throws in production, matching the established fail-closed convention. **(6) `cidToPin` memory leak** — a disconnected signaling client whose call room later reaped left its `cidToPin` entry orphaned forever (nothing ever cleared it); a 15-min sweep now purges entries with no live client AND no active-or-held room, deliberately leaving the reconnect-window entries the auto-rejoin logic depends on untouched. **(7) Redis bus event-kind allowlist** — `relay:v2ev` has no message authentication (anything with VPC/SG reach to Redis can publish); `_handleBusV2Event` now drops any envelope whose `kind` isn't one of the known `V2Event` shapes, a cheap backstop against a forged/malformed envelope reaching the browser's SSE handler unfiltered. **(8) SMTP STARTTLS response-injection** (CVE-2011-0411 class) — the plaintext read buffer was shared across the STARTTLS upgrade boundary, so an on-path attacker could pack extra reply lines into the same segment as the genuine "220 go ahead" and have them consumed as the FIRST reply once the encrypted session started reading, forging the perceived outcome of the real dialog; `upgradeTls` now clears the buffer before the TLS handshake. **(9) weak RNG for 6-digit number allocation** — `randomDigits6` used `Math.random()` (recoverable internal state) while every other identifier in the codebase already used a CSPRNG; switched to `crypto.randomInt`. **(10) `appUrl.ts` host-header validation** — `requestOrigin()` fed an unvalidated `X-Forwarded-Host`/`Host` straight into sitemap XML and (narrowing, not eliminating) email-verification links; a `SAFE_HOST_RE` allowlist now rejects malformed/injection-shaped host values. **(11) CI/CD command injection in `aws-ops.yml`'s `ses-ssm` action** — the `SES_EMAIL`/`DOMAIN` `workflow_dispatch` free-text inputs were spliced unescaped into single-quoted command strings executed on production EC2 via SSM `RunShellScript`; a value containing a quote/semicolon could break out and run arbitrary commands under the instance role. Fixed with the same base64-encode-on-runner/decode-on-remote treatment the adjacent `DESC_B64` value already used (the sibling `iam-grant-ses` action was reviewed and found NOT vulnerable — its interpolation runs directly on the runner via safe single-pass substitution, never re-serialized through a second remote shell). New/updated tests: `storageProxy.test.ts` (+3), `awsOps.test.ts` (+3), plus source-pinned coverage for the block-bypass, push IDOR, attachment-URL, OAuth fail-closed, and cidToPin-reaper fixes. Accepted residuals (documented, not fixed this pass): Redis bus still lacks message authentication at the transport level (architectural, VPC-trust-boundary change out of scope for a bug-fix pass), cluster-leader trust of bus-forwarded `__ownedNumber`/`home` (same trust boundary), no per-account password-login lockout (only per-IP; would need new schema), upload-DoS ordering (rate limit runs after body buffering), `/api/v2/offline` has no rate limit, and anonymous `/api/relay/ice` TURN credential minting for arbitrary `who` (bandwidth-freeloading risk, only matters with an operator coturn configured). 1392 tests.) (v2.99.19 — QA-SWEEP FIXES (the heavy multi-agent QA pass #35 surfaced a cluster of real bugs, several v2.99.11 offline-rework regressions). #46 (HIGH) GROUP CALL COLLAPSED IF ANY INVITEE WAS OFFLINE: a group dial rings the FIRST invitee to CREATE the room, then the `room` ack flushes the rest — but v2.99.11 means an OFFLINE first invitee returns `error{offline}` with NO room, so the rest were never rung AND the client's fatal-error branch tore the whole dial down over one offline person. `client/src/lib/relayClient.ts`'s error handler now splits `reachErr` (offline/nonexistent/gone — the INVITEE is unreachable) from `joinErr` (self/full/forbidden — WE couldn't join): during a group-dial BOOTSTRAP (`callIsGroup && outgoingDial && !establishedOnce && !roomId && aloneInCall()`) a reachErr PROMOTES the next `pendingGroupInvites` entry as the new bootstrap (one at a time, never all-at-once → no duplicate-room race) and only `failDial`s once every invitee is exhausted; a reachErr inside an ESTABLISHED parked call (`inParkedCall()`) never ends the call; `joinErr` stays fatal to a peerless joiner (`(reachErr||joinErr) && inCall && aloneInCall()`). #47 (HIGH) VIEW-ONCE MEDIA BROKE FOR THE RECIPIENT: opening burned it (`consumeExpiring` nulls `attachmentId` → the proxy 403s the url) BEFORE it rendered, so a kept server url showed a broken image; `Messages.tsx`'s `revealExpiring` is now async — it `fetch`es the bytes into a local blob object-URL (and drops `thumbUrl`) BEFORE burning, so the reader views a local copy that survives the burn; object URLs are revoked on countdown purge / thread switch / unmount (no leak), with an "Opening…" spinner over the fetch. #48 (MED) OFFLINE RESOLVER FIRED A STALE ERROR: the invite handler's offline `onPageCallee(...).then/.catch` (`server/relay.ts`) only checked the caller still existed, not that `ctxEpoch` was unchanged — a hang-up/takeover during the await could fire a stray `error` + phantom miss into the caller's NEW context; both continuations now re-check `callerNow.ctxEpoch === ctxEpoch` (same discipline as the party-line `settle`). #49 (MED) MULTI-DEVICE HANG-UP LEFT OTHER DEVICES RINGING: the invite fans the ring to EVERY device but `cancelPendingRings` only cancelled the primary socket; it now fans `ring-cancel` to all `reg.devices` mirroring the ring fan-out. #50 (MED) NEW-DEVICE APPROVAL COULD STRAND A LOGIN: the approver device may be closed and never tap Approve — `AuthPanel`'s waiting screen now always offers a "Sign in with your PIN instead" escape (PIN bypasses approval by design) plus, after 35s, an honest "the other device may be offline or closed" note (fails toward the user getting in). #51 (LOW batch): (a) the in-call add-person offline guard accepts BOTH `offline`+`nonexistent`; (b) UNSEND cleared a phantom unread badge — `deleteMessage` (`v2db.ts`) now decrements (floored at 0) every non-sender recipient who hadn't read past the unsent message (`unreadCount` is a stored counter, not id-derived); (c) a FAILED offline-message email used to keep the cooldown watermark (suppressing notifications for the whole window) — `releaseOfflineMessageEmailClaim` rolls it back on failure so the next message retries; (d) `reapStaleSessions` (every 30 min) drops dead pending-approval rows (inflated the approval bell forever) + rows idle past the longest cookie TTL (95 days). `server/qaSweepV29919.test.ts` (14 — behavioural relay tests for #48/#49 + source-pins); two pre-existing pins updated to the refactored error handler. 1400 tests.) (v2.99.18 — FIRST+LAST NAME ON THE DIALER (#43) + ANIMATED AVATARS (#45), both owner asks surfaced in a transcript re-audit. #43: `directory.lookup` now returns `firstName`/`lastName` (from the `identities` row); the landing hero dialer composes "First Last" via `dialLookupName()` (falls back to `displayName`, still `escLp`-escaped before innerHTML). Registered users already had `displayName = "First Last"`, so this makes the "show the name first and last" explicit. #45 (owner: "an animated icon also"): NEW `client/src/lib/animatedAvatar.ts` — a dependency-free GIF89a + LZW encoder (fixed 216-colour web-safe palette, NETSCAPE2.0 loop-forever) renders a picked emoji as a looping GIF (10-frame bounce/pulse). `AvatarPicker.tsx` gains an "Animated ✨" toggle; an animated pick uploads `image/gif` through the SAME `uploadAvatarImage` bare path (bytes pass through untouched — `uploadBare` never canvas-re-encodes, so animation survives), and the v2.99.14 streaming proxy relays `image/gif` so it animates on EVERY surface (thread rows, contacts, in-call tiles, other users' previews) and syncs like a photo. Headless-verified in Chromium: the output is a valid GIF89a, decodes at 160×160, has 10 GCE frames + the NETSCAPE loop block. `animatedAvatar.test.ts` (4, Node encoder checks), `Home.test.ts` XSS pin updated. 1386 tests.) (v2.99.17 — DIALER: A NONEXISTENT NUMBER OFFERS NO ACTIONS (owner screenshot: dialing `888 888` showed "No RELAY user with this number" YET still lit active Voice/Video/Group call buttons AND a "Save 888-888 to contacts" pill — you shouldn't be able to call, group-call, or save a number that isn't a real RELAY user). In `client/src/pages/app/Dialer.tsx` a new `nonexistent` flag = `/^\d{6}$/.test(dialed) && dialed !== myNumber && previewQuery.isSuccess && !previewIdentity` — keyed on `isSuccess` (a SUCCESSFUL public `directory.lookup` resolve to null: not a user, not a party line) so a lookup ERROR or still-loading query FAILS OPEN (actions stay enabled; the dial then surfaces the real error). `callable` gains `&& !nonexistent` (the Voice + Video buttons already `disabled={!callable}`); the Group Call button — previously ALWAYS enabled — gains `disabled={nonexistent}` (still opens the picker on an empty/partial pad, only blocked for a confirmed-dead 6-digit number); the v2.99.8 "Save to contacts" quick-add pill gains `&& !nonexistent`; and `startCallNow` early-returns on `nonexistent` defensively. Existing-but-OFFLINE users and party lines are unaffected (they resolve to a real `previewIdentity`, so `nonexistent` is false — offline users stay callable per v2.99.11's leave-a-message flow). `client/src/pages/app/dialerNonexistent.test.ts` (5). 1382 tests.) (v2.99.16 — LANDING POLISH: ARABIC SIZING PARITY (#40) + LIVE GROUP-CALL GRID (#41), both `client/src/pages/Home.tsx`. #40 (owner: "the Arabic version renders smaller than English"): ROOT CAUSE — every element hardcodes a LATIN face (`'Space Grotesk'`/`'IBM Plex Mono'`) inside its inline `font:` shorthand and `FONTS_HREF` loaded only those, so Arabic glyphs fell back to a smaller SYSTEM Arabic face and the whole RTL layout read as shrunken. FIX — load `Noto+Kufi+Arabic` in `FONTS_HREF` and force it for RTL text: `.lp-root[dir="rtl"] * { font-family:'Noto Kufi Arabic',… !important }` (inline `font:` shorthands are NOT !important, so a stylesheet `font-family !important` overrides ONLY the family — sizes/weights untouched), with a later, higher-specificity `.lp-root[dir="rtl"] [dir="ltr"], … [dir="ltr"] * { font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',… !important }` keeping the dial-display/keypad/percent LTR islands monospace. #41 (owner: "make the talk moving, not fixed images"): the 10-up group-call grid already had subtle per-tile Ken-Burns, but read as static — added a ROTATING ACTIVE-SPEAKER SWEEP: a green ring overlay (its own `<span>`, so it never fights the container's per-tile speaking box-shadow) on every tile running a shared 20s `@keyframes lpActive{0%,13%,100%{opacity:0}3%,10%{opacity:.95}}` at a staggered `-i*2s` delay, so the highlight rotates around the grid; the container also gets a subtle transform-only `lpTalk` scale pulse (COMMA-combined with any existing `spk` speaking anim so both run — a second `animation:` would clobber the first). Headless-verified the ring sweeps (tile0 opacity .95 while tile1 is 0 at the same instant). All motion stays under the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ .lp-root *{animation:none} }` gate. CAVEAT: two backticks inside a CSS comment terminated the CSS template literal (build break) — fixed by removing them; keep comments inside the `CSS` template backtick-free. `Home.test.ts` +2. 1377 tests.) (v2.99.15 — FUNCTIONAL LANDING DIALER + GUEST ONLINE-ONLY CALLS (owner: on the main page, type a number → it AUTO-shows the target's name + "he is online" → Dial → asks the visitor's name → gives a random RELAY number → rings the callee to accept — BUT only if online; an offline user can't be called by a guest). The landing hero dialer (`client/src/pages/Home.tsx`, raw-DOM `startLanding`) previously did NOT resolve the dialed number at all — it just armed CALL at 6 digits and, after a 3s loader, navigated to `/i/<n>`. Now the React shell passes an imperative `onLookup` (`utils.directory.lookup.fetch` — the PUBLIC, rate-limited resolver) into `startLanding`; when the 6th digit lands, `runLookup` resolves the owner and `applyLookup` writes a live preview into a new `data-lp="dialPreview"` node — **name + "ONLINE"** (green) for an online user, **name + "OFFLINE — you can't call them"** (CALL disabled) for an offline user, **"NO RELAY USER WITH THIS NUMBER"** for an unknown number, or **"PARTY LINE · N on the line" + JOIN** for a line. The CALL button is gated by a new `dialCallable` flag (armed only for an online user / party line / a lookup that ERRORED — fallback to `/i` which re-resolves); `callNow` also guards `if (!dialCallable) return`. Display names are `escLp`-escaped before `innerHTML` (no XSS). The "DIAL A DEMO NUMBER" gimmick cancels its in-flight lookup and arms in fallback mode so the cinematic still plays. GUEST OFFLINE BLOCK, mirrored in `OnboardingGate.tsx` (the `/i/<pin>` join card): a guest has no persistent thread to leave a message on (unlike a signed-in caller's post-dial voicemail card), so an offline callee (or unknown number) now DISABLES "Join call" (`joinBlocked = numberNotFound || calleeOffline`, party lines exempt, FAILS OPEN on a lookup error) with an honest "They're offline — can't call" + "you can reach them once they're back online" line, replacing the old "offline — we'll try to reach them" allow-through. `directory.lookup` returns only `displayName` (no first/last split) — shown as-is. `Home.test.ts` +3, `callLinkJoin.test.ts` +3. 1375 tests.) (v2.99.14 — MEDIA URL LOCKDOWN (owner: a video-note URL `https://your-chat.io/manus-storage/relay-chat/62/…_video-note_….webm` could be opened + copied OUTSIDE the app; "everything should be encrypted, cannot be traced — the file URL stays in the app"). ROOT CAUSE (per pre-fix recon) was NOT missing authorization — video/voice/file/image are participant-gated attachments and the relative `/manus-storage/<key>` URL 403s a non-participant/anon. It was that the storage proxy (`server/_core/storageProxy.ts`) answered an AUTHORIZED request with a `307` redirect to a session-independent presigned S3/Forge URL (300s TTL); following the redirect surfaced that raw URL in the address bar/devtools, and it was then copyable + replayable by ANYONE for its lifetime (no cookie). FIX: the proxy no longer redirects — it resolves the presigned URL SERVER-SIDE only, `fetch`es it, and STREAMS the bytes back through the cookie-gated route (`Readable.fromWeb(upstream.body).pipe(res)`), Range-aware (forwards `Range`, relays 206/`Content-Range`/`Accept-Ranges` so `<video>`/`<audio>` seeking works), `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` (never `public`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The browser now only ever sees `/manus-storage/<key>`; no shareable storage URL is ever emitted. Also closed a fail-open: an `unknown` (orphaned/guessed) key is now refused to an anonymous caller (`kind==="unknown" && identityId==null → 403`); avatars stay semi-public (invite previews) but likewise stream (no presigned leak). Attachment + status gating unchanged. TRADEOFF: media bytes now transit the app server (S3→app→client) instead of client→S3 direct — ~2× egress on media, acceptable for RELAY's volume and the necessary cost of "stays in the app"; the 60s presigned-URL cache is kept but used only server-side. `server/_core/storageProxy.test.ts` rewritten (no-redirect, unknown+anon 403, streams), `server/storageProxy.test.ts` updated (legal key streams 200, no Location), new `server/mediaUrlLockdown.test.ts`. 1369 tests.) (v2.99.13 — EMAIL-NOTIFICATION PREFERENCES (owner, offline batch: "if he's a registered user and put his email, he'll get an email for a missed call OR when somebody sends a message while he's offline — but WITHOUT the content, just 'you received a message, log in to see it'. He can enable/disable it"). Two additive nullable `users` booleans `emailNotifyMissedCall`/`emailNotifyMessage` (+`lastMessageEmailAt` cooldown watermark) via the boot migrator; NULL = ENABLED (historical default — the missed-call email always sent), so a user disables by storing false. The existing missed-call email in `server/_core/index.ts` gains a single gate `if (user.emailNotifyMissedCall === false) return;` placed AFTER the push + `recordMissedCall` so History/push stay unconditional. NEW offline-message email: in `v2MessagesRouter.send`, for every OFFLINE recipient (1:1 or group) with a linked account email, a CONTENT-FREE `messageWaitingHtml()` nudge ("You have a new message waiting on RELAY … we don't include message contents") — no body, no sender, no thread. Throttled by `claimOfflineMessageEmail(userId, cooldownMs)` — a SINGLE atomic conditional UPDATE (stamp `lastMessageEmailAt=now` WHERE pref on `(NULL OR true)` AND cooldown elapsed `(NULL OR < cutoff)`), returning true only when `affectedRows>0` — so N messages while away send at most one email per 15-min cooldown, race-free (mirrors the v2.98.4 S1 lockout-race fix) and fail-safe (DB down → returns false → no email, send unaffected). tRPC `otpAuth.getNotificationPrefs` (normalizes NULL→on, reports `hasEmail`) + `otpAuth.setNotificationPrefs` (auth-guarded partial write via `setUserNotificationPrefs`). (v2.99.12 — OFFLINE-RETURN NOTIFICATIONS: UNREAD MESSAGES SURFACE + BLINKING ICON (owner, offline-call batch: "when he logged in again he will see the notification on the main page and also on the icon and to keep blinking if there is a message or there was in the history a missed call"). AppShell computes `latestUnread` (most-recent unread thread; group `title` or `peerDisplayName`/`peerNumber`) to label the messages row. The dismiss watermark keys on the latest-item TIMESTAMP per category (localStorage `relay_away_popup_seen_v2` `{missedAt,msgAt}`), NOT a count — counts are non-monotonic (they fall on History review / reading a thread), so a count high-water mark goes stale-high and would silently hide genuinely-new activity, incl. a fresh next-day login with fewer-but-new items (caught + fixed by the pre-ship adversarial review). (v2.98.5 — RELIABILITY PASS (owner: "make it successful" — a focused bug hunt across calling/messaging/onboarding, independently verified against source before any fix): **`getOrCreateDmConversation` could permanently orphan a DM thread** — the conversation-row insert and the participant-row insert were two separate round trips with no transaction (unlike its sibling `createGroupConversation`, which already wraps both in one); a failure or slow participant insert between them left a committed conversation row with NO participants and no recovery path — every later `openThread` call hit the early-return and handed back a thread `listMessages`/`sendMessage`'s membership checks would 403 BOTH users out of, forever. Fixed by running the participant upsert unconditionally on every call (self-healing for already-orphaned rows too, and closes the race window for new ones). **Messages: scrolling back to the bottom never re-fired the read receipt** — only a new message arriving or the tab regaining focus did; catching up by scrolling alone left a thread "unread" (badge lit, sender never got ✓✓) if neither happened again; the scroll handler now debounce-fires `markRead` when the user is back near the bottom. **Call-waiting: a promoted ring didn't mirror the incoming-ring's video button** — `waitingRing` never carried the `video` flag from the original message, and the post-hangup "promote the waiting caller" block (explicitly commented as "a mirror of onRing's presentation") omitted the one line that actually resets the Video-answer button's visibility, so it kept whatever a PRIOR ring left it in; both now carry/apply `video` correctly. **`useRealtime`'s SSE handler could read a stale identity id** — the effect depended on `[enabled]` only while its `onmessage` closure captured `selfId` (used to suppress self-sent-message chimes); added `selfId` to the dependency array so the subscription is never stale. Reviewed-and-left-alone: `PresenceManager`'s instant-offline-on-tab-hide is a *deliberate* trade-off (documented in its own comment) to catch mobile-Safari tab closes that don't fire `pagehide` — a debounce would defeat detection on exactly the browsers it targets, so it's untouched. New `server/reliabilityPass.test.ts` + `client/src/app/reliabilityPass.test.ts` + a pin added to `useRealtime.test.ts`. 1216 tests.) (v2.98.4 — SECURITY SWEEP ROUND 2 (owner: "maximize the bugs, fix it everywhere"): an exhaustive multi-agent audit of 12 attack surfaces, each candidate adversarially verified against source. 7 confirmed + 6 partial survived; ALL meaningful ones fixed (S1–S11), report appended to `SECURITY-AUDIT-2026-07-22.md`. **S1 (HIGH) — PIN lockout brute-force race:** `attemptPinLogin` wrote `stale_read+1`, so N concurrent wrong guesses all saw `attempts=0` and lost increments, defeating the 3-try cap on the 10^4 PIN space; fixed with a single conditional `UPDATE` (increment + lock-on-threshold) guarded on `loginPinLockedAt IS NULL`, verdict derived from the persisted post-value, lock email sent once via `affectedRows`. **S2 (MED) — `signal` relay had no room-membership check:** any registered client could push SDP/ICE to any ONLINE pin and harvest its ICE candidates (IP deanonymization) with no call/ring/consent; fixed to relay only when sender+target share a room (active `pinRoom` OR held `heldRoom`), mirroring accept/reject. **S3–S5 (LOW) — F5 enumeration gaps:** `directory.presence` (also missing guest-privacy), `directory.watchOnline` (name-harvest oracle), and `calls.logStart` (existence oracle + history-row injection) bypassed the F5 `directoryGate`; all three now gated. **S6 (LOW) — `markRead` IDOR:** the peer-message `status:"read"` flip wasn't membership-scoped (unreadCount already was), letting anyone corrupt other conversations' read receipts; `markThreadRead` now checks `conversationParticipants` in-tx, returns membership, and the router only fans out the `read` SSE when a member. **S7 (LOW) — upload DoS:** `POST /api/v2/upload` had no rate limit; added per-IP + per-identity token buckets before `storagePut`. **S8 (LOW) — Web Push SSRF:** unvalidated `endpoint` URL fed to `web-push`'s server-side request; new `isAllowedWebPushEndpoint` (https + known push-service host allowlist) on subscribe + defensively before send. **S9 (LOW) — OTP attempt race:** same lost-update class as S1 in `recordOtpFailure`; made atomic. **S10/S11 (LOW) — signing secrets failed open:** `sessionSecret`/`inboundSecret` fell back to a public constant when env unset (bare-HMAC session ⇒ trivial forgery); now fail CLOSED in production (dev/test keep the fallback), inbound webhook route also rate-limited. New `server/securitySweep.test.ts` (behavioral SSRF-allowlist + source pins) + a behavioral S2 test in `relay.test.ts`. Accepted residuals: no per-caller invite cap / pendingRings reaper (bounded benefit vs. signaling-path risk), inbound webhook signature stays opt-in. 1208 tests.) (v2.98.4 pt.1 — SECURITY AUDIT & REMEDIATION (owner-requested full review of "all app connections, front and back, and the database"; report saved as `SECURITY-AUDIT-2026-07-22.md`). 5 findings confirmed against source and ALL fixed. **F1 (HIGH) — signaling had no identity binding:** `POST /api/relay/send` keyed connections only by a client-minted `cid` and `register` granted ANY free number from the client's `msg.pin`, so an attacker could seize a victim's number while their app was closed and intercept inbound calls / spoof caller-ID. Fix: for `register` messages the handler resolves the caller's own identity number via `createContext` (session/guest cookie) and stamps a SERVER-ONLY `__ownedNumber` (any client value stripped first); the register handler binds the claimed pin to it — resolved ⇒ your own number (also self-heals a stale client post-`regenerateNumber`); null (no cookie / resolve error) ⇒ explicit claim REFUSED, fresh number allocated (fail closed); field absent (direct `handleMessage`/tests) ⇒ legacy behavior. Client now sends `x-relay-device-id` on the signaling POST so cookie-dropped ITP guests still resolve; only `register` pays the async cost (offer/answer/ICE stay fully synchronous). **F2 (MED) — avatar laundering:** `identity.updateProfile` validated only the SHAPE of `avatarUrl`, so a user could point it at another user's private `/manus-storage` attachment key and `authorizeStorageKey`'s avatar-rescue would then serve that key to anyone; fixed with a `keyInOwnerNamespace` gate on write (matches `attachments.register`/`status.post`). **F3 (MED) — view-once media served public after burn:** `consumeExpiringMessage` DELETED the attachments row, which made `authorizeStorageKey` classify the still-present S3 object as `unknown` — served by the proxy WITHOUT auth (burning made it MORE accessible); fixed by keeping the row (message `attachmentId` already nulled ⇒ participants lose access) so the key stays classified `attachment` and fails CLOSED (403) for every non-uploader. **F4 (LOW) — spoofable rate-limit key:** `clientIpOf`/`pickClientIp` trusted the LEFTMOST `X-Forwarded-For` hop (client-appendable behind the appending ALB), defeating every per-IP limiter by header rotation; fixed to trust the hop the proxy APPENDED (`trustedProxyHops()` from the right, default 1; `RELAY_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` for CloudFront→ALB). **F5 (LOW) — free directory enumeration:** `directory.lookup`/`presenceMany` were public with no throttle over the 10^6 number space; added a generous per-IP `directoryGate` (120 burst / ~60/min, honors `RELAY_RATELIMIT_OFF`) — endpoints stay public so the `/i/<pin>` call-link direct-join still resolves callees. New `server/securityAudit.test.ts` (F1 behavioral + F2/F3/F5 wiring pins); `rateLimit.test.ts`/`geoSelf.test.ts`/`peerIdentityBatch.test.ts`/`relayCluster.integration.test.ts` updated. Residual/follow-up: a room-membership check on the signaling `signal` relay. 1196 tests.) (v2.98.1 — LANDING LOADER + MOBILE NAV (owner reports): (1) the boot loader's bar no longer freezes at 0% on main-thread-saturated devices — the fill is COMPOSITOR-DRIVEN (`lpFill` transform:scaleX keyframes on a full-width `#loadBar`, declared in plain CSS so it runs with zero JS, re-timed per run by runLoader; rAF now only syncs percent/messages/lock; `[dir="rtl"]` grows from the right; the reduced-motion animation-kill re-asserts the zero-JS lpAutoClear watchdog). (v2.98.0 — three-part owner batch, delivered from a single garbled voice report resolved by direct investigation rather than guessing: (1) PROFILE AVATAR SAVE RACE — capturing/picking a profile photo could report "done" (camera-badge spinner stops) before it actually saved. `onAvatarPick` uploaded the bytes THEN fired the `updateProfile` mutation fire-and-forget, clearing `uploading` in a `finally` that only awaited the upload step — a save failure (session hiccup, dropped request) left a real uploaded photo in storage with the profile's `avatarUrl` never actually updated, while the UI had already signalled success. Fixed by awaiting `updateProfile.mutateAsync` in the SAME try block as the upload (`client/src/pages/app/Profile.tsx`), so the spinner and the error path cover the whole pipeline, not just the first half. (2) VIDEO RECORDER HONEST LABELING — confirmed live via a headless Chromium capture with a fake camera device: this browser's `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported("video/mp4")` returns true, but the recorder actually encodes VP9+Opus under that label (`rec.mimeType` only reveals `"video/mp4;codecs=vp9,opus"` once encoding starts — it stays the bare "video/mp4" for tens-to-hundreds of ms after construction/start, so a naive construction-time check never catches it; a real .mp4 that isn't really H.264/AAC risks a strict decoder like Safari's refusing it for the RECIPIENT). `client/src/lib/videoNote.ts`'s `recordFromStream` now forces an immediate `requestData()` flush right after `start()`, which reveals the true codec within ~2ms with no meaningful footage recorded yet, and swaps to an honest `video/webm` recorder when the label lied — verified end-to-end: the resulting blob's first four bytes are the genuine WebM/Matroska magic `0x1A 0x45 0xDF 0xA3`, not just a relabeled file. A SECOND bug was found and closed while building this fix (also reproduced headlessly before the guard existed): a `cancel()` landing in the same tick as construction — before the mislabel check had run — used to ignore the cancellation and start a fresh live recorder that nobody would ever stop again, leaking the recorder and hanging the `done` promise forever; a `cancelled` guard inside the swap branch closes the race. (3) OUTGOING-CALL HANG-UP REDESIGN (owner: "the red one for Hangout... it's not nice") — the pre-connect dial screen's lone red circle now sits on a soft ambient halo (a radial glow behind the button, distinct from the existing tight ripple ring), a richer two-tone gradient, a bigger glyph, and a real "End Call" caption underneath; all new motion is gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`. A real bug was found and fixed while building this: the mobile media query that lets a CROWDED in-call control bar scroll (`max-height:40vh;overflow-y:auto`) was silently clipping the new halo + caption on the pre-connect screen, where there's only one button and nothing to scroll — fixed with a higher-specificity override, confirmed via a headless render (screenshot evidence). `server/v298ProfileAvatarFix.test.ts` (3 tests), `server/v298VideoMislabelFix.test.ts` (6 tests), `server/v298CallerHangup.test.ts` (6 tests); two stale pre-existing pins (`server/v2962VideoRecorder.test.ts`, `server/v2963Fixes.test.ts`) updated to match the new source shape instead of silently passing on an empty slice. 1178 tests.) (v2.97.2 — `RELAY_OTP_REGISTER_BYPASS` (owner directive, email-outage stopgap): AWS SES (ap-south-1) is sandboxed pending the owner's production-access request (confirmed pending live via the AWS account API), so every registration OTP to a non-pre-verified address is refused by AWS itself (owner screenshot: "couldn't send your code"). New env flag, read per-call, default OFF (byte-identical): when `=1`, `otpAuth.register` skips minting/emailing a code and performs the SAME account/session outcome a real `verifyOtp` would (resolve-or-create user, mark verified, unlock PIN, upgrade guest identity, set session cookie) — a deliberate TEMPORARY trust reduction the owner explicitly accepted (email ownership isn't proven at signup while it's on). Login (`requestOtp`/`verifyOtp`/`loginWithPin`) is completely unaffected — registration only. `AuthPanel.tsx`'s `submitRegister` recognizes the mutation's `bypass:true` and skips straight to the post-registration "setup" step instead of a code screen for a code that was never sent. To restore full verification once SES is approved: unset the flag on both EC2 instances + restart pm2 — no code change. `server/otpRegisterBypass.test.ts` (6 tests, proves the branch is genuinely taken via distinct DB-unavailable error paths). 1163 tests.)
