(v2.92: the owner's "Round 3+4" batch — sign-in, mailer, domains, TURN. R3 — the **Manus OAuth sign-in UI is REMOVED entirely** (owner decision): the native AuthPanel (email one-time code + 4-digit PIN, v2.87) is the ONLY sign-in. Earlier versions had already put AuthPanel behind the visible CTAs; v2.92 kills the last reachable OAuth paths — main.tsx's global 401 handler no longer hard-navigates to the portal (it only logs), useAuth's default `redirectPath` is `/`, DashboardLayout's Sign in routes to `/app`, `ManusDialog.tsx` is deleted, and `getLoginUrl` itself is deleted from const.ts (a client-wide test in `verifiedBadge.test.ts` forbids OAuth-portal references outside tests). The server's `GET /api/oauth/callback` is deliberately KEPT (unreachable from UI; existing sessions stay valid). Existing Manus-OAuth users keep their accounts + numbers and sign in via email code at the same address — `server/authOtp.ts findUserByEmailAny` prefers otp/local rows then falls back to ANY user row with that email, so the OTP flow lands on the old OAuth row. R4A — SES mailer compat: **`EMAIL_FROM` is an accepted alias for `SMTP_FROM`** (`SMTP_FROM` > `EMAIL_FROM` > `SMTP_USER`; the SES SMTP username is an `AKIA…` key id SES rejects as a From) and **`MAIL_PROVIDER`** = `smtp` forces the built-in SMTP client (Resend NEVER used, even on send failure) / `resend` forces Resend (SMTP skipped) / unset = auto (SMTP-first, Resend fallback). R4B — **ZERO hardcoded deployment domains** in `server/` `client/src/` `shared/` (owner requirement): new `server/appUrl.ts` `appBaseUrl(req?)` derives `APP_URL` → `DOMAIN` (bare hostname ⇒ https) → request `x-forwarded-proto`/`-host`/Host → null — deliberately NO traffic-derived fallback (an observed-origin ledger was cut in review: x-forwarded-host bursts could poison it and steer ABSOLUTE email links; request-free contexts require env and degrade — the missed-call email omits its button, the VAPID subject stays the neutral mailto — so operators SHOULD set `APP_URL` on both deployments); converted: missed-call email links (`_core/index.ts`), authLocal verification links, the VAPID subject (`VAPID_SUBJECT` → own https origin → neutral mailto, computed per-call), and the marketing/legal pages via `client/src/lib/siteHost.ts` (Technology eyebrow/contact/©-footer, PrivacyPolicy) — `server/noHardcodedDomains.test.ts` walks the tree and forbids the literals (mobile/, scripts/, docs, tests are the deliberate exceptions). R4C — `TURN_TTL` (default 3600; NaN/non-positive now guarded) and `TURN_TCP_HOST` (`turn:<host>:443|3478?transport=tcp`, same HMAC creds) are contractually pinned by new relay tests. 1003 tests.) (v2.91: horizontal-scale building blocks for `.io`, all env-gated dormant (unset ⇒ byte-identical to v2.90; `.org` untouched). ZERO-DEP NATIVE S3 DRIVER — `server/s3.ts` implements SigV4 with `node:crypto` only (smtp.ts/fcm.ts pattern; unit-tested byte-for-byte against the official AWS `examplebucket` GET/PUT/presign vectors): when `S3_BUCKET/S3_REGION/S3_ACCESS_KEY/S3_SECRET` are set (+optional `S3_ENDPOINT`/`S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` for R2/MinIO, `S3_PREFIX` default `relay-chat/`, ensure-style so upload keys never double-prefix), `storagePut` PUTs straight to the bucket and returns the SAME `/manus-storage/{key}` URL shape, and the storage proxy presigns GETs locally (60s cache, 307, 300s expiry) — Forge stays the fallback (`.org`). REDIS EVENT BUS — `server/redisBus.ts` (ioredis as a regular dep, pub+sub connections), gated on `REDIS_URL`: v2events delivers SSE events locally FIRST then publishes `{targets, ev}` on `relay:v2ev` with a per-boot `INSTANCE_ID` (subscribers drop their own envelopes), so `/api/v2/events` can stay LOAD-BALANCED across instances; the signaling node mirrors busy-line + party-line counts into `relay:busypins`/`relay:plcounts` (diff-syncs from the join/leave/reap funnels coalesced per tick + 30s full re-sync + 90s TTL + API-tier write-guard), and `pinsInCallAsync`/`partyLineLiveCountsAsync` (now used by directory.lookup/presenceMany/contacts.list/partyLines.list) read the mirror only on API-tier instances (bus on, zero local relay clients). CROSS-INSTANCE RELAY ROOMS EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — the registry's call-state transitions are transactional per-process (phase 2); ALL `/api/relay/*` must hit ONE node: `docs-aws-scale-out.md` is the runbook (ALB with `relay-signaling` TG holding instance A only + priority-10 `/api/relay/*` rule above the both-instance default, idle timeout 300s, ElastiCache Redis cluster-mode-OFF one small node same VPC + SG 6379-from-app-SG, `REDIS_URL` into `/home/relay/.env` AFTER the rule — single-writer order — then `S3_*`), and `.github/workflows/aws-ops.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`-ONLY; graceful no-secrets failure) automates `verify` (read-only status) / `cloudfront` (us-east-1 ACM cert with printed validation CNAMEs → create-or-update distribution: ALB origin https-only+AllViewer, CachingDisabled default, `/assets/*` CachingOptimized, SSE paths CachingDisabled with 60s origin timeout, http2and3 — prints the DNS change, never touches DNS) / `alb-tune` (idle 300s + TG + rule, idempotent, prints everything). 965 tests incl. a real spawned-redis-server integration pair that auto-skips off-box.) (v2.90: AWS/`.io` deploy scaffolding, repo-side only — a `GET /api/health` liveness route, a **dormant** (`workflow_dispatch`-only) `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` that builds `main` → S3 → SSM rolling-deploys to an EC2 fleet serving `your-chat.io` in AWS Mumbai (a parallel perf-test deploy of the same branch Manus serves as `.org`), a repo-root `ecosystem.config.cjs` correcting the real esbuild entry to `dist/index.js` with `instances:1` (the signaling registry is in-memory/per-process), and `docs-aws-io-deploy.md`. Deliberately NO domain find-replace: the app is already env/Host-driven (`APP_URL` ‖ Host header ‖ `window.location.origin`), so `.io` is set by env+DNS and `.org`/Manus + the `.org` APK stay untouched; the AWS side is blocked on the owner adding a scoped IAM key. v2.89: three audit-backlog features. PHOTO DOWNSCALE + THUMBNAILS — Messages photos are canvas-downscaled pre-upload (cap 2048px, webp q≈0.85/jpeg fallback, original kept if smaller, gifs skipped) with a ≤512px thumb uploaded first (`/api/v2/upload?thumb=1`, no row) and referenced via `?thumbKey=` (owner-prefix-validated, thumbUrl derived server-side; new nullable `attachments.thumbKey/thumbUrl` via boot migrator); bubbles render the thumb with explicit width/height (no layout shift), tap opens the full url; base64 (mobile) route untouched. PARTY LINES, the signature feature — `party_lines` table shares the identity number space (both allocators check both tables); `attachRelay`'s new async `onResolveDial(pin)` hook is consulted in the invite path BEFORE identity/paging (the identity flow now lives in `runIdentityInvite()`, still fully sync without the hook), so dialing a line NEVER rings anyone: standard `room` ack + `joined` into the persistent DERIVED room `pl-<number>` (reaping an empty room never kills the line — re-dialable forever), peer-joined merges like add-person, standard 6/10 caps, conference history logs with the line's title in History; directory.lookup resolves lines first (title + live `partyLineLiveCounts`), Dialer preview shows "Party line · N on the line" with a Join button, GroupCallScreen manages lines (tRPC `partyLines` create/list/remove, guests allowed, rate-limited, 10/owner, share via /i/<number>); client `joined{partyLine}` mid-dial = the answer (callIsGroup, empty line ⇒ established immediately). INSTANT OFFLINE — PresenceManager sendBeacons `POST /api/v2/offline` (scoped text parser, createContext + body-deviceId fallback, goOffline path) on pagehide/tab-hide, heartbeats on return-to-visible; 2-min reaper stays the backstop. 876 tests.) Three phone-grade features ship: a carrier-style BUSY LINE ("on a call" amber LEDs from the in-memory registry via `pinsInCall`), VOICEMAIL on no-answer/declined/offline (≤60s MediaRecorder → chat audio message with `meta:{voicemail:true}` + "Voicemail from X" push), and CALL-BACK ALERTS (`directory.watchOnline` + `online_watches` table → push + SSE toast when they're back online).) reload-mid-ring is also redelivered), the two instant pre-ring drop bugs are fixed (a stale callee `pendingRing`/`waitingRing` no longer blind-rejects the next call — same-caller/expired rings REPLACE; `sendRejoinIfInRoom` no longer reaps a LIVE dial room on mid-dial re-registers), pre-establishment SFU `Disconnected` retries instead of hanging up, failed dials show an honest reason card (~2s) before teardown, History rows carry batched presence LEDs (`directory.presenceMany`), every remaining video-default dial site is voice-first, and iOS finally RINGS: the ringtone AudioContext is gesture-unlocked at boot (was born suspended inside the SSE handler = silent), rings vibrate + flash the tab title + raise a SW notification when hidden, foregrounding reconnects the SSE instantly, and **Web Push infrastructure** ships end-to-end (push_subscriptions table, push router, VAPID derived from JWT_SECRET, sw.js push/notificationclick, incoming-call + missed-call pushes, one-time enable banner; iOS requires Add-to-Home-Screen per Apple). v2.81 ships **fast startup** (route-level code splitting — the entry chunk fell 1,941→723 kB, the docs markdown stack loads only on /docs; hashed /assets now get `immutable, max-age=1y` and index.html no-cache), the **mutual-consent video protocol** (1:1 calls are voice-first: rings for voice dials hide the video answer; camera transmits ONLY after both parties agree — video dial answered with the Video button = consent, mid-call camera tap sends `video-request` → in-call prompt → accept turns BOTH cameras on; groups bypass; answerer flips offered video m-lines to sendrecv pre-answer so consent needs no renegotiation; 1:1 calls auto-END when the peer leaves), and **guest-first login** (name + "Enter as guest" primary, passwordless email login/register secondary). v2.80 is a **multi-party A/V reliability batch** (19 fixes from a 6-participant QA report + 6-dimension audit + an empirical 6-browser matrix test): camera-less mesh peers now negotiate a null-track sendrecv video m-line (their inbound video was silently dead forever) with msid-less ontrack MERGED not wiped; remote video going quiet (mute/congestion/adaptiveStream pause) flips tiles to the avatar on BOTH paths instead of freezing; mesh camera reacquire exists now (+ honest failure states); local track death self-heals (mic reacquired + re-fed everywhere); SFU autoplay unlock is cross-platform; loudspeaker taps use fresh wrapper streams (one-participant-on-earpiece fix); `sendWS` retries dropped signaling (a lost offer was pair-fatal); mesh encoders scale with party size; the server excludes ghost members from rosters. Both pinned in `appShellNav.test.ts`. v2.77 turns the Dialer's actions into a **trio of round icon buttons** (Voice = blue `PhoneCall`, Video = green `Video`, Group Call = purple `Users` — the "Create Group Call" text bar is gone). v2.76 locks the **document** while the app shell is mounted (`html/body.relay-app-lock` — all scrolling is internal; kills the iOS keyboard scroll-into-view shoving the app past its own end) and adds a **one-time iOS tip** after the first camera/mic grant pointing at Safari's permanent per-site Allow (aA → Website Settings) — the getUserMedia popup itself is browser policy no site can suppress. v2.75 overhauls the **History tab**: All/Dialed/Missed filter tabs with count badges, a confirm-guarded **Clear History** (per-user soft clear via an additive `identities.historyClearedAt` high-water mark — `calls.clearHistory` mutation; both history queries filter `startedAt > clearedAt`; the other party keeps their log), color-coded rows (missed **red** / dialed **green** / received **blue**), full date + precise-time-with-seconds stamps (`formatFullWhen`), durations, dialed PINs, and unanswered outgoing dials now listed ("No answer"; a conference's direction comes from roster order — the caller seeds the roster). v2.74 adds **staged caller progress** — a dedicated pre-connect dial screen (`#dialCard`, only End Call visible) walking "Calling…" (invite sent) → "Ringing…" (new server `ringing` delivery ack, carries the callee's name) → "Connecting…" (on answer) → full in-call UI ONLY on real media establishment; fixes the SFU caller showing "Connected" while still ringing (caller joins the room alone at dial — establishment now waits for the first remote `TrackSubscribed`); voice dials stay camera-off with a "Voice call" chip, video dials connect camera-live with a "Video call" chip. v2.73 **docks the mobile bottom tab bar in-flow** (no `position:fixed`, no `pb-28` clearance — page content ends exactly at the bar's top edge and the Messages composer sits pixel-0 above it) and gives each tab a **distinct active accent** (Calls green / History sky / Messages orange / Contacts purple; gradient squircle + glow, inline styles because runtime-composed Tailwind class names don't JIT). Key layout invariant since v2.73: pages fill the shell with `flex-1`, NOT `h-full` — `height:100%` does not resolve against the scroll container's flex-derived height and silently collapses short pages (pinned in `client/src/app/appShellNav.test.ts`). v2.50 makes **PiP show video on iPhone** (iOS Safari can't render a `canvas.captureStream` source in PiP, so on iOS the PiP `<video>` is fed a **real remote stream** via `webkitSetPresentationMode` — a single active speaker, not the Android 2-up composite) and folds two adversarial-review call-routing fixes (call-waiting `switchCall` no longer races a redundant `leave` against the room you just joined; auto-inviting an offline number from the in-call "+" no longer tears your call down via the primary-dial offline-teardown path). v2.49 gives the in-call "+" add-person window an **on-screen keypad that auto-invites on the 6th digit** (online → rings them in; offline/nonexistent → "That number doesn't exist or is offline."; pad self-closes) and makes **call waiting actually work** (a second caller to someone mid-call now rings through to a call-waiting popup instead of getting a "busy" bounce). v2.48 adds a **self-checking auto-updater** (`shared/version.ts` is the single source of truth, served at `GET /api/version`; a mounted-once `UpdateChecker` polls every 30s and either reloads silently mid-call — auto-rejoin keeps the call — or shows a centered reappear-on-dismiss refresh prompt when idle) and **"enable once" auto Picture-in-Picture** (persisted `relay_auto_pip`; primes the compositor at call start so the browser auto-opens a 2-up active-speaker PiP whenever the app is backgrounded mid-call). Recent batches added a **multi-device ring** (flag-gated), **persistent call membership + auto-rejoin** (refresh/step-away keeps the call; only an explicit hang-up or logout locks you out — hardened against a cross-user hijack on shared browsers), a **multi-party camera fix + mobile screen-share**, **conference call history** (the History tab: dialed number, party count, each party's name + PIN, duration, per room), and an **active-speaker / spotlight view** (the in-call grid follows the talker, auto-focuses a shared screen, tap-a-tile-to-spotlight, and collapses to a 2-up when minimized — pure decision logic in `client/src/lib/callLayout.ts`). The legacy single-screen calling UI is still reachable at `/app/call` for the actual in-call experience.> Versions v2.1–v2.30 layered on a lot since this doc's v2.0 baseline — LiveKit SFU calls, Resend missed-call email, Do-Not-Disturb, invite links, offline auto-reply, call waiting, device **passcode app-lock** + **biometric (WebAuthn) unlock**, a call-engine reliability batch (raw-track publishing to kill mobile heat, a 10s reconnect window, live top-bar status), **screen sharing**, **call recording (LiveKit Egress → S3)**, **group messaging**, an installable **PWA**, **rich contact fields** (+ an additive boot-migrator), **inbound email reply-to-thread**, **voice calls + voice↔video**, message **unsend** / **reply** / **per-conversation mute**, and **typing indicators**. See `todo.md` for the per-version changelog; treat it as the source of truth for what shipped.

| Call history (start/end) — independent of the legacy in-memory signaling | shipped | `server/v2routers.ts` (`v2CallsRouter`) |
| Stale-presence reaper (60s sweep, 2 min timeout) | shipped | `server/_core/index.ts` (setInterval) |
| DB helpers (Drizzle queries) | shipped | `server/v2db.ts` |
| App shell: mobile bottom-nav, desktop sidebar, sticky header with number + Upgrade button | shipped | `client/src/app/AppShell.tsx` |
| Onboarding gate: name-entry form before entering `/app/*` | shipped | `client/src/app/OnboardingGate.tsx` |
| Identity hook: whoami + 30s heartbeat + pagehide go-offline | shipped | `client/src/app/useIdentity.ts` |
| Dialer tab: fluid responsive 3×4 keypad + dialed echo + presence preview + recent calls | shipped | `client/src/pages/app/Dialer.tsx` |
| Messages tab: thread list, conversation view, emoji picker, image/video/audio/file attachments, voice-note recording, read receipts | shipped | `client/src/pages/app/Messages.tsx` |
| Contacts tab: search, sort, presence dots, last-seen, favorite, edit/delete, inline message+call | shipped | `client/src/pages/app/Contacts.tsx` |
| Design spec (OKLCH dark palette + responsive sizing rules) | shipped | `design/v2-spec.md`, generated by `scripts/gen-design-spec.mjs` via `gemini-flash-latest` |

**Known gaps in v2.0 (carry into v2.1):**
- The legacy `/app/call` Relay component does **not** read the guest cookie — users still have to type a name when entering the actual call session. Wiring the cookie into the embedded HTML/JS is a deferred port.
- Messaging is **polling-based**, not WebSocket push. Typing indicators are not implemented. The `signaling` table is created for the eventual DB-backed signaling mailbox but not yet used.
- Avatar upload UI is a placeholder (DB column exists).
- The OAuth upgrade flow migrates the guest's number into the user row, but no end-to-end vitest covers it yet (only shape/validation tests cover v2 routers).
- No vitest coverage yet for message send/read/unread, attachment roundtrip, or presence transitions. The 8 new tests in `server/v2routers.test.ts` cover the pair-key helper, validation, and whoami shape only.

The full history of features and bugs lives in `todo.md` at the repo root; check it before you start a change so you don't redo work or relitigate a closed bug.

## Architectural decisions (and why)

These are decisions that look unusual but were made deliberately. Don't undo them without reading the rationale.

### 1. Signaling uses Server-Sent Events + HTTP POST, not WebSocket

The original RELAY zip the user uploaded used a `ws` WebSocket server. That works on a VPS but **does not work behind the Manus production gateway (Cloudflare + Cloud Run)** for arbitrary paths — WebSocket upgrade requests get downgraded and our server returns the SPA's HTML instead. We replaced the transport with **GET `/api/relay/stream` (SSE) for server → client** and **POST `/api/relay/send` for client → server**. Both are standard HTTP and route through the gateway cleanly. The protocol semantics (`register`, `invite`, `accept`, `reject`, `signal`, `leave`, `room`, `peer-joined`, `peer-left`, `bye`, `busy`) are unchanged.

> Don't switch back to WebSocket. If you need bidirectional, extend the SSE+POST envelope.

### 2. The calling UI is a React route, not standalone HTML

We originally served the unmodified `index.html` / `app.js` from `client/public/relay/`. In production, Manus's Space Editor injects a `<manus-content-root>` Web Component and a Space Editor script that interferes with the global scope of plain HTML pages — `connectWS` ended up `undefined` on the global object, so the page stayed stuck on "Connecting…". The fix was to port the markup + CSS + behavior into a real React component (`client/src/pages/Relay.tsx` mounts the markup via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` once; `client/src/lib/relayClient.ts` runs the WebRTC logic via `useEffect`). The Space Editor leaves React routes alone.

> If you need to add a new page, make it a React component under `client/src/pages/` and register the route in `client/src/App.tsx`. Don't add raw HTML to `client/public/`.

### 3. The local camera goes through a canvas processing pipeline

`client/src/lib/mediaPipeline.ts` takes the raw `getUserMedia` track, paints each frame into a hidden `<canvas>` (applying CSS-filter color grading, MediaPipe-segmented background blur, and MediaPipe-detected face overlays), and republishes the canvas as a `MediaStream` via `canvas.captureStream(30)`. The processed stream is what's sent to peers; we hot-swap the track on every peer via `RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack` whenever the user picks a different filter or flips the camera — **no SDP renegotiation needed**, so it's silent on the wire.

MediaPipe models (selfie segmenter, face detector) are **lazy-loaded** — only fetched the first time a filter that needs them is picked. Don't preload them at app boot.

### 4. Outgoing video is never mirrored; local self-preview is mirrored only on the front camera

The outgoing canvas stream is the source of truth and is never flipped. CSS mirrors the **local self-tile** only when the front camera is active (so movements feel natural to you); the back camera and the remote tiles always show the true orientation.

### 5. In-memory state in `server/relay.ts` only survives within one Cloud Run instance

Channels (`channels: Map<cid, RelaySocket>`) and peer registry (`peers`, `rooms`) live in memory. Cloud Run scales to zero with `min-instances=0` and can spin up additional instances at low traffic. We've seen this work in practice because RELAY's traffic is so low that one instance is typically warm. **If you add a feature that needs multi-instance coordination, externalize the state to MySQL (already wired) or a Redis-like store.** Don't pretend the in-memory map is durable.

## Build & run loop

```bash
pnpm install              # install
pnpm dev                  # NODE_ENV=development tsx watch server/_core/index.ts (serves React + tRPC + relay on port 3000)
pnpm test                 # vitest run (453 tests)
pnpm check                # tsc --noEmit
pnpm format               # prettier --write .
pnpm db:push              # drizzle-kit generate && drizzle-kit migrate
pnpm build                # vite build (client) + esbuild bundle (server) → dist/
pnpm start                # NODE_ENV=production node dist/index.js
```

**Cloud Run constraints**: Node-only build image, 1 vCPU, 512 MiB RAM, 180s request timeout, min-instances=0 (cold starts). No Python, no native binaries beyond what npm ships. The signaling SSE connection is long-lived; Cloud Run is fine with this within the 180s window (and we send a ping every 25s).

## Environment variables (all injected by Manus, do NOT commit `.env`)

`DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `VITE_APP_ID`, `OAUTH_SERVER_URL`, `VITE_OAUTH_PORTAL_URL`, `OWNER_OPEN_ID`, `OWNER_NAME`, `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_URL`, `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_KEY`, `VITE_FRONTEND_FORGE_API_KEY`, `VITE_FRONTEND_FORGE_API_URL`, `VITE_APP_TITLE`, `VITE_APP_LOGO`, `VITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT`, `VITE_ANALYTICS_WEBSITE_ID`.

**RELAY-specific** (optional; set when operator has their own coturn):
- `TURN_SECRET` — same `static-auth-secret` as the coturn instance
- `TURN_HOST` — public hostname/IP of coturn (port 3478). SINGLE-relay spelling.
- `TURN_HOSTS` (v2.99.61) — comma/whitespace separated LIST of relay hosts, one per availability zone
  (e.g. `13.232.119.83,13.204.23.58`). Takes precedence over `TURN_HOST`; each relay is advertised with
  every transport (UDP, TCP:443, TCP:3478, and `turns:` when `TURN_TLS=1`) and they SHARE one minted
  credential, because coturn in `use-auth-secret` mode validates the HMAC against its own
  static-auth-secret — so every relay configured with the same `TURN_SECRET` accepts it. Clients gather
  relay candidates from all of them, which is what makes a zone loss survivable without renegotiation.
  Duplicates are dropped. With a list, `TURN_TCP_HOST` is IGNORED (each relay uses its own address);
  it still applies in the single-relay case it was written for.
- `TURN_TCP_HOST` (optional, v2.92-pinned) — separate host/IP for the TCP/TLS candidates when the UDP and TCP listeners sit behind different public IPs (two L4 LBs). Falls back to `TURN_HOST`. Adds `turn:<host>:443?transport=tcp` + `turn:<host>:3478?transport=tcp` with the SAME minted HMAC credentials.
- `TURN_TTL` (optional, v2.92-pinned) — credential lifetime in seconds; default `3600`. Garbage/non-positive values fall back to 3600 (never `NaN:` usernames). The anonymous `/api/relay/ice` probe always mints 300s creds regardless.
- (also read: `TURN_PORT` default 3478, `TURN_TCP_ALT_PORT` default 443, `TURN_TLS=1` + `TURN_TLS_PORT` default 5349 to advertise `turns:`.)

These are read **per-call** in `iceServers()` so they can be added without restarting the process.

**Public base URL** (v2.92 R4B — there are ZERO hardcoded deployment domains in `server/`, `client/src/`, `client/public/`, `shared/`; pinned by `server/noHardcodedDomains.test.ts`). Server-side URLs (email links, VAPID subject) derive via `appBaseUrl(req?)` in `server/appUrl.ts`: `APP_URL` → `DOMAIN` → the request's `x-forwarded-proto`/`-host`/Host → null (degrade). There is deliberately NO traffic-derived fallback — a "most-observed request origin" ledger was removed in security review (D1): `x-forwarded-host` is attacker-controlled and the value fed absolute links in missed-call emails. Client marketing/legal pages use `window.location` (`client/src/lib/siteHost.ts`):
- `APP_URL` — explicit full origin (e.g. `https://example.org`); wins outright.
- `DOMAIN` — bare-hostname convenience for self-host `.env`s (e.g. `example.org` ⇒ `https://example.org`); second priority.
- Operators SHOULD set `APP_URL` on BOTH deployments (org: the canonical https origin; io already has `DOMAIN`) — absolute links in missed-call emails now REQUIRE one of the two; without them the email sends without its "Open RELAY" button and the VAPID subject stays the neutral mailto fallback.

**Signaling abuse backstop** (optional):
- `RELAY_RATELIMIT_OFF` — `1` to DISABLE the per-IP token-bucket rate limiter on `POST /api/relay/send`
  (`server/rateLimit.ts`, wired in `server/_core/index.ts`). The limiter is ON by default and tuned
  generously (~200 msg/s sustained, 1000 burst per IP) so only a true flood is ever throttled; set this
  only if you suspect it's interfering. The signaling handler also caps a single `message` at 256 KB.

**Multi-device ring** (optional, **experimental**; one number rings all signed-in devices):
- `MULTI_DEVICE_RING` — `1`/`true` to enable. **Default OFF**, and the off-path is byte-identical to the historical single-device behavior (a 2nd device on the same number evicts the 1st). When ON, multiple devices share a number, an incoming call rings every idle device, the first to accept wins (the rest get an "answered elsewhere" `ring-cancel`), and in-call signaling routes to the accepting device. Needs real 2-device testing before relying on it. Read per-call from `multiDeviceEnabled()` in `server/relay.ts`.

**Native S3 storage** (optional, v2.91; first-party attachment storage for self-hosted deploys — the `.io` fleet has no Manus Forge). When all four are set, `storagePut` uploads via the zero-dep SigV4 driver (`server/s3.ts`) and `/manus-storage/*` reads presign locally; when unset, the Forge flow runs unchanged (that's `.org`). Returned URLs keep the `/manus-storage/{key}` shape either way, so DB rows and clients are storage-agnostic. Read per-call like `TURN_*`:
- `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_REGION`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_SECRET` — all four required to enable. Keep the bucket private; browsers only ever get 300s presigned GETs via 307 redirect.
- `S3_ENDPOINT` (optional) — custom endpoint for non-AWS S3 (Cloudflare R2, MinIO, …).
- `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` (optional) — `1`/`true` for R2/MinIO path-style (`endpoint/bucket/key`).
- `S3_PREFIX` (optional) — key prefix, default `relay-chat/`. Ensure-style: keys already under the prefix (all `/api/v2/upload` keys) are NOT double-prefixed, so the default produces byte-identical keys to the Forge backend.

**Round 11 (v2.99.66) — durable room registry.** In clustered mode the elected leader shadows every room into Redis (`relay:room:<id>` + the `relay:rooms` index, 6h TTL, fenced by `relay:leader:epoch`) and the NEXT leader hydrates from it before serving signaling, so losing the leader no longer ends every call fleet-wide. Fully dormant outside clustered mode (writes are gated on a fence epoch, which only leadership grants), needs no new env var, and every key self-expires. Design + the manual failover test: `docs-cross-instance-signaling.md` § Round 11. Two rules for anyone editing it: **the pin→room index is DERIVED from membership** (a member's `held` flag), never stored as its own key, so it rides one atomic write; and **`rejoin-recreate` must never trust a client-asserted roomId or role** — it is authorized by a server-minted capability (`server/roomCapability.ts`), because trusting the client there reopens the class closed by v2.99.43/M45 and v2.99.57/R-GENPIN.

**Redis event bus** (optional, v2.91; REQUIRED before running more than one instance of the app). Gated entirely on one var — absent ⇒ every bus call is a no-op and behavior is byte-identical to the single-instance build:
- `REDIS_URL` — e.g. `redis://relay-bus.xxxxx.cache.amazonaws.com:6379` (`rediss://` + auth supported via the URL). When set: v2 SSE events fan out cross-instance on `relay:v2ev` (so `/api/v2/events` can stay load-balanced), and busy-line/party-line state is mirrored into `relay:busypins`/`relay:plcounts` (90s TTL) by the signaling node for API-tier reads. NOTE the invariant: this does NOT make `/api/relay/*` scalable — signaling must still be pinned to ONE instance (ALB rule; see `docs-aws-scale-out.md`, and set `REDIS_URL` only after that rule is live).

**Media transport — THE HOSTED SFU IS GONE (v2.106.53).** There is no third-party SFU and no
`LIVEKIT_*` variable: the owner cancelled that account, so the code was deleted rather than gated, and
setting such a variable now does nothing at all. The ladder is **mediasoup → mesh**, both on the
owner's own infrastructure:
- **mesh** — always available, needs no configuration, and is what every fallback lands on. Its cap is
  the exported `ROOM_MAX = 6` in `server/relay.ts` (mirrored client-side by `transportMax()`), which is
  a MEASUREMENT rather than a preference: each phone runs N−1 encoders and N−1 decoders (v2.99.84).
  Do not raise it without measuring on a real handset, and do not add a second copy of the number —
  the group picker, the invite guard and `maxParticipants()` must agree with what the user was shown.
- **mediasoup** — the owner's two media nodes, selected through `server/voipRegistry.ts` (nodes
  self-register in Redis; nothing here holds an address). Its `transportCap` is 10, inherited rather
  than derived, and still provisional — the nodes are 2-core, so the real ceiling wants load-testing.

**Recording does not exist (v2.106.53, finished in .55).** `server/recording.ts` was LiveKit Egress in
its entirety, so it went with the account: the in-call Record chip, the ● REC badge, `reg.recordings` and
both signaling cases are all gone, and `RECORDING_S3_*` is read by nothing. v2.106.55 removed the
**native** half too — it was a chip driven by a `recording` flag the server no longer sends, so it could
never appear and its taps reached no handler. Bringing it back means a mediasoup recording path, which is
new work rather than a re-enable.

**Email** (optional; OTP sign-in codes + missed-call notifications). Two senders — the v2.87 built-in SMTP client (`server/smtp.ts`, zero-dep, works with SES/any mailbox) and the Resend API fallback (`server/email.ts`):
- `SMTP_HOST` / `SMTP_PORT` / `SMTP_SECURE` / `SMTP_USER` / `SMTP_PASS` — enable + configure the built-in SMTP client (587 STARTTLS default; `SMTP_SECURE=1` for 465).
- `SMTP_FROM` — SMTP sender, e.g. `RELAY <no-reply@example.org>`.
- `EMAIL_FROM` (v2.92) — accepted ALIAS for `SMTP_FROM` (`SMTP_FROM` > `EMAIL_FROM` > `SMTP_USER`). SES `.env`s commonly use this name; without either From var the fallback is `SMTP_USER`, which on SES is an `AKIA…` key id that SES rejects as a sender.
- `SMTP_TLS_CA` (optional, v2.105.2) — a PEM (inline, or a path to one) to trust when the relay presents a certificate from a private CA. Read only by `scripts/mail-verify.mjs`; absent means TLS verification uses the Node defaults, i.e. STRICT, exactly as `server/smtp.ts` is. It is NOT a way to skip verification — that is what makes it safe to have.
- `MAIL_PROVIDER` (v2.92) — `smtp` forces the SMTP client (Resend never used, even if `RESEND_API_KEY` is set and even when an SMTP send fails); `resend` forces Resend (SMTP ignored); unset/other = auto (SMTP first when configured, Resend fallback).
- `RESEND_API_KEY` — enables Resend. Without a DNS-verified sending domain, Resend test mode only delivers FROM `onboarding@resend.dev` TO the account owner's address.
- `RESEND_FROM` — Resend sender; defaults to `onboarding@resend.dev`. Set to a verified-domain address to email arbitrary registered users.
- Email links use `appBaseUrl()` (see "Public base URL" above) — set `APP_URL` (or `DOMAIN`) on EVERY deploy; there is no hardcoded default domain and no traffic-derived fallback, so a missed-call email on an env-less deploy ships without its absolute "Open RELAY" button.

**Inbound email** (optional; reply to a RELAY notification from your inbox and it posts into the thread). When set, missed-call emails get a SIGNED `Reply-To` (`relay+{convId}.{identityId}.{hmac}@domain`); the operator points an inbound provider (Resend Inbound) at `POST /api/email/inbound`. Replies are bound to the mailbox owner (the email `From` must match the signed identity's registered address):
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN` — enables the feature, e.g. `inbound.your-chat.org`. Add the provider's MX records for this domain + a route/webhook to `https://<app>/api/email/inbound`.
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_LOCALPART` (optional) — default `relay` (the part before `+`).
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET` (optional) — HMAC key for the reply-address signature; falls back to `JWT_SECRET`.
- `INBOUND_EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (optional, recommended) — the provider's Svix signing secret (`whsec_…`) to verify webhook authenticity.

**Native push — THREE transports, and the token's SHAPE picks one** (v2.99.79). `push_subscriptions.kind`
is `webpush` | `fcm` | `expo`, and `sendPushToIdentity` fans out to each in turn. Read this before touching
any of them:

- **`webpush`** — an ordinary browser. VAPID keys are DERIVED from `JWT_SECRET`, so there is nothing to
  configure. This is what the website itself has used since v2.83, and it needs **no Firebase**: adding
  the `firebase` npm package for web push would be a second, parallel notification stack for a case
  already covered. Do not install it.
- **`fcm`** — a raw FCM registration token (Android) or an APNs device token (iOS), sent to FCM directly
  by the zero-dep `server/fcm.ts`. The service-account JSON is read from **either
  `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`**, and in either case as the
  JSON itself **or a path to it** — the SHAPE decides (a value starting with `{` is content),
  because guessing wrong either way is a silent misconfiguration. `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`
  wins when both are set, so nothing that works today changes; the production fleet uses
  `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/home/relay/fcm-sa.json`, which the code could not see before
  v2.106.69. `FCM_PROJECT_ID` is honoured as a **cross-check only** — the token is minted by the
  service account and is valid only for its own project, so the JSON's `project_id` wins and a
  mismatch is warned about once. **That private key is a real secret** — it belongs in
  `/home/relay/.env` (or a file only root can read), never in a commit, and never in a
  `workflow_dispatch` input (inputs are visible in run metadata).
- **`expo`** — an `ExponentPushToken[…]`, sent through Expo's own service by the zero-dep
  `server/expoPush.ts`. Needs no server credential for ordinary use; `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` is honoured for
  Expo accounts with enhanced security enabled. The FCM server key and APNs key go to **EAS**, not here.

Two rules that are easy to get wrong and produce a SILENT failure rather than an error:

1. **Never route by a client-supplied label.** An Expo token is not an FCM registration token and vice
   versa; sending one to the other transport is accepted and then simply never delivered, with nothing in
   any log pointing at the cause. `classifyNativeToken` (`server/expoPush.ts`) is the single rule, and
   `push.subscribe` **re-derives** the kind from the token rather than trusting the `kind` field the
   client sent. A token it cannot classify is REFUSED, not stored.
2. **The token arrives by `postMessage` from a WebView, and that listener is a security boundary.** The
   owner's shipping mobile app is a React Native + Expo shell wrapping this site, so the native layer
   holds the token and the web app holds the identity. `client/src/app/nativeTokenBridge.ts` gates on
   origin + source + a strict envelope. Do **not** simplify it into a bare
   `window.addEventListener("message", …)` that registers whatever arrives — any frame that can post into
   the page would then hand us a token for its own device and start receiving somebody else's
   notifications (the v2.99.49 R1 class).

- **`apns-voip`** — a **PushKit** device token, sent VoIP-style by the zero-dep `server/apnsVoip.ts`.
  This is the ONLY transport that makes a **locked iPhone** show the real full-screen CallKit call
  screen: iOS hands an `apns-push-type: voip` message on the `<bundle>.voip` topic to PushKit even
  with the app not running.

  **APNs takes EITHER of two provider credentials and RELAY supports both**, because an operator has
  whichever Apple gave them:
    - **token** — `APNS_P8_KEY` (inline PEM or a path) + `APNS_KEY_ID` + `APNS_TEAM_ID`. Signs a
      short-lived ES256 JWT. Never expires. **Preferred when both are configured**, precisely because
      it cannot silently lapse.
    - **cert** — `APNS_VOIP_CERT_PEM` + `APNS_VOIP_KEY_PEM` (each inline or a path). Mutual TLS: the
      pair is presented at the handshake and there is **NO `authorization` header at all**. Sending a
      bearer alongside a client certificate is how a working cert setup earns a 403 that reads like a
      bad certificate. It **EXPIRES**, which is why the admin push doctor reports the date and goes
      red 30 days out.

  Plus a topic — `APNS_VOIP_TOPIC`, or derived as `<APNS_BUNDLE_ID>.voip`. `APNS_ENV` opts into
  sandbox; production is the default so a production build is never silently un-ringable.

  **Both credentials are real secrets** — same rule as the Firebase key: `/home/relay/.env` only,
  never a commit, never a `workflow_dispatch` input.

  **`apns-voip` IS NOT `apns`, and the difference is destructive.** iOS issues TWO hex tokens per
  device: the PushKit one (topic `<bundle>.voip`) and the ordinary ALERT one (topic `<bundle>`). They
  are indistinguishable by shape, so `isVoipDeclaration` trusts the shell's `kind` label for this one
  case only — safe because mislabelling costs the declarer their own ring and nobody else anything. A
  VoIP push sent to an ALERT token earns `BadDeviceToken`, which the sender reads as stale and
  **PRUNES**. A plain `apns` row therefore stays inert and diagnosable (v2.105.11) and is never rung.

  It is **ring-only**: a VoIP push carries no `aps.alert`, so anything else sent this way is a
  notification nobody sees, and Apple terminates apps that send VoIP pushes without reporting a call.
  That is also why both hex kinds stay out of `ROUTABLE_PUSH_KINDS` — the offline-message email
  fallback must still fire for a device that can only ring.

**A ring IS pushed (v2.105.12).** `kind:"incoming-call"` was removed in v2.99.11 at the owner's
explicit request and restored at their request; `onPageCallee` in `server/_core/index.ts` sends it and
reports `pushed`, and the relay **pages only when a push actually reached a device**. That gate is
what makes the two directives compatible: a phone with the app installed rings, while a callee nothing
can wake still gets the fast `offline` reply and the leave-a-message card rather than 65 seconds of
"Reaching their phone…". Three rules to keep if you touch it:

1. **The block gate in `onPageCallee` is load-bearing.** E4 (v2.98.6) exists because a blocked caller
   could otherwise fire the callee's full-screen ring; v2.99.11 deleted the push and the guarding
   assertion was rewritten to "there is no push here", which let the bypass re-open the moment the push
   came back. It refuses by reporting `pushed: 0` so the reply is indistinguishable from an ordinary
   unreachable callee — never a distinct code, or it becomes an oracle for having been blocked.
2. **The ring goes through `sendPushToIdentity`, never a parallel sender.** That is where the user's
   own master push switch is enforced.
3. **The dial room is created before the hook awaits**, because the payload carries the room the callee
   must join to answer. A ring with no room is a phone that rings and then cannot connect.

**Said plainly: an iPhone will not show the FaceTime-style screen until the Expo shell adds PushKit +
CallKit.** The shell today has `fullScreenIntent` (Android) and `interruptionLevel: "timeSensitive"`
(iOS), so iOS currently gets a time-sensitive notification. That is a config plugin plus a Mac build.
Android rings through the existing FCM/Expo path with no shell change.

## Coding conventions

1. **tRPC-first** for any new HTTP feature. Don't introduce `axios` or `fetch` wrappers in `client/src/` — use `trpc.feature.useQuery()` / `useMutation()`. Exception: the SSE/POST relay endpoints, which are deliberately raw HTTP because tRPC doesn't model long-lived streams well.
2. **Optimistic updates** for list ops, toggles, profile edits (`onMutate` → `onError` rollback). Use `invalidate` only for critical operations (payments, auth).
3. **shadcn/ui** components for any new UI primitive (`@/components/ui/*`); compose with Tailwind utilities. Avoid bespoke CSS.
4. **Stable query inputs** — never pass `new Date()` or fresh array literals as tRPC query inputs. Use `useState(() => new Date())` or `useMemo`. (See `README.md` "Common Pitfalls" → "Infinite loading loops from unstable references".)
5. **File storage** — use `storagePut(key, bytes, mime)` in `server/storage.ts`. Save the returned `key` in MySQL; don't store bytes in the DB.
6. **Animation discipline** — 100–300ms, ease-out for entering UI, ease-in-out for moving. Never animate `width/height/padding/margin/top/left`; only `transform` and `opacity`. Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` gates around non-essential motion.
7. **Auth** — use `useAuth()` for current user state; never read cookies directly. v2.92 (R3, owner decision): the Manus OAuth sign-in UI is REMOVED — `getLoginUrl` no longer exists; every sign-in affordance opens the native `AuthPanel` (email one-time code + 4-digit PIN). Do NOT re-add an OAuth sign-in path (a client-wide test in `verifiedBadge.test.ts` forbids it); the server's `/api/oauth/callback` remains only for pre-existing sessions.
8. **Origins/domains** — always use `window.location.origin` client-side and `appBaseUrl(req?)` (`server/appUrl.ts`) server-side. Never hardcode `manus.space` or deployment domains anywhere in `server/`, `client/src/`, `shared/` (pinned by `server/noHardcodedDomains.test.ts`; `mobile/` and `scripts/` are the deliberate exceptions).
9. **Datetime** — store as UTC Unix ms in the DB; convert in React via `new Date(ts).toLocaleString()`.
10. **Logs** — `.manus-logs/devserver.log`, `browserConsole.log`, `networkRequests.log`, `sessionReplay.log`. Don't read these as text files; use grep/tail.

## Testing

Vitest runs Node-environment tests under `server/**/*.test.ts` and `client/src/lib/**/*.test.ts` (see `vitest.config.ts`). New features must come with tests — focus on protocol shapes, business logic, and pure functions. Browser DOM tests are not currently configured; UI is verified via manual preview.

> Run `pnpm test` before every checkpoint / PR. All 453 must stay green.

## Deploying

> **`main` IS THIS PROJECT AGAIN, AND ANY WORKFLOW YOU DISPATCH MUST RUN ON IT
> (verified 2026-07-28).** For a few days `main` carried a different project of the
> owner's (their Expo/React-Native WebView shell) and an earlier revision of this file
> said so, adding "do not open a pull request against `main`" and "there is no live
> deployment path". **All of that is now false and following it wastes runs.** The
> owner restored `main`; it carries the web app (`client/`, `shared/version.ts` at the
> current release, `ecosystem.config.cjs`, and all five workflows), PRs from
> `claude/connected-ready-glsdab` merge into it normally, and every merge deploys.
> Confirm rather than trust this paragraph:
> `git ls-tree --name-only origin/main .github/workflows/` and
> `git show origin/main:shared/version.ts`.
>
> **THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: dispatch `aws-ops.yml` with `ref: main`, never a feature
> branch.** The `relay-github-deploy` OIDC trust policy is scoped to
> `repo:khalifa1982/relay-chat-video3:ref:refs/heads/main`, so
> `configure-aws-credentials` on any other ref retries a dozen times and then fails
> with `Could not assume role with OIDC: Not authorized to perform
> sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`. That error names STS, so it reads like an AWS-side
> problem or a throttle and invites you to retry — it is neither, and three identical
> re-runs on a branch will fail identically. The tell is `head_branch` on the run: every
> successful aws-ops run in the history has `main`. (This is also why the failure is
> SAFE: it happens before the first AWS call, so a refused apply wrote nothing.) The
> workflow prefers `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` repo secrets when they
> exist and only falls back to OIDC — setting those would remove the ref constraint,
> and until then `main` is the only ref that authenticates.

**Every push to `main` auto-deploys to `.io`**: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds,
uploads to S3, and rolling-deploys via SSM to the EC2 fleet (one server at a time,
`/api/health` gated, ~60–90s end to end). Verify with
`curl https://your-chat.io/api/version`.

The former Manus/`.org` deployment was **emptied and retired by the owner (2026-07-21)** — the Publish-button flow no longer applies. Do not point anything (docs, mobile clients, emails) at `.org` or `manus.space`. There is **no Vercel, Netlify, Railway, or Render involved**.

## What to be careful about

1. **Don't refactor `server/relay.ts`'s in-memory maps into a database** unless you also implement durable cross-instance routing — the simple design relies on single-instance affinity that Cloud Run usually provides.
2. **Don't add SSR / Next.js** — this is a Vite SPA + Express server. Different framework.
3. **Don't add WebSocket** anywhere user-facing — production gateway won't pass the upgrade. Use SSE+POST or long-polling.
4. **Don't preload MediaPipe models** — they're ~3 MB each and most users won't use filters.
5. **Don't mirror the outgoing video** — only mirror the local self-preview on front camera, never the published stream.
6. **Don't bypass `RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack`** when changing the local track — replacing the stream object entirely forces a renegotiation that drops media for ~1s.
7. **Don't commit secrets** — `.env*` is in `.gitignore`. Use `webdev_request_secrets` in Manus or `Settings → Secrets` in the Management UI.
8. **Database changes** are not auto-reversible. Use `pnpm db:push` only after reviewing the generated SQL in `drizzle/migrations/`.
9. **Never hardcode a mediasoup media-node address, and never put the media plane behind a load balancer.** The nodes' public IPs are auto-assigned (the account hit its EIP quota), so they change on stop/start — a configured host list is a value that goes silently wrong and sends media to an address nobody is listening on. Each node self-reports from IMDSv2 and signaling reads `server/voipRegistry.ts`. And media is a live UDP flow that must reach the *exact* host holding that room's router, so a balancer would spray packets across hosts and break the stream: signaling keeps one endpoint (the ALB), the media plane fans out beneath it one public IP per node, and a room is **pinned** to one node.
10. **Do not add `mediasoup` to the root `package.json`.** The server bundle is `esbuild --packages=external` and every app instance runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on every deploy, so it would make each app box fetch or compile a ~9.7 MB C++ worker it never runs, on every release. The agent lives in `voip-node/` as its own package; `server/voipNodeParity.test.ts` fails the build if that changes, or if the release tar starts shipping it.

## Working with the user

The user prefers:
- **Concise, honest progress updates** — no exaggeration ("perfect", "fully bug-free"); just specific, testable claims.
- **Versioned footer on every deploy** — bump the version string in `Relay.tsx` (`RELAY · v1.2.0`) on every shipped change.
- **Direct deployment to the live server** when possible — keep iteration cycles tight.
- **System-wide application** — when fixing a bug or adding a feature, apply it consistently across the codebase, not just where the bug surfaced.
